summary: Read-only web research on lab inventory systems, Quartzy API, biology domain needs, duplicate-order prevention/adoption and tech building blocks; then synthesize and critique a prioritized feature catalog

synthesis.executive_summary:
Recommendation: keep Quartzy as the lab's purchasing system and build a Python/Django companion app that owns physical inventory and acts as the duplicate-order guard. No commercial or open-source product checks a new Quartzy request against personal stock, open requests and recent deliveries together. Quartzy's own check is narrow: it matches only an identical catalog #, only within the same lab, only against open requests, and never looks at inventory. The Quartzy API can read and create order requests and change their status, but it cannot add comments, create inventory or list users. There are also no webhooks for approvals, cancellations or backorders. So the app has to (1) mirror Quartzy by polling, with webhooks added where the network allows, (2) send alerts outside Quartzy (Slack/Teams/email), and (3) keep its own inventory.

MVP (about 4-6 weeks part-time, read-only against Quartzy):
- poll Quartzy's order history and seed a normalized product catalog from it
- run a tiered matcher on every new Quartzy request, whether it came from the web UI, the mobile app, the Connect browser extension or QBot, and alert the requester and approver within minutes, before Quartzy's hourly approver email
- one mobile 'check before you buy' search across personal stock, open orders and past purchases
- inventory records created at receiving: the requester only confirms a location
- personal spreadsheets imported with ownership kept but visible to the lab
- URL QR labels that the phone's own camera opens, leading to big-button pages
- a baseline report plus a PI dashboard of duplicates caught and $ avoided

v1 adds the approver console and API write-back (after sandbox tests), visual box grids, cryo labels, GS1 scanning, expiry and low-stock alerts, a Slack bot, public-database lookups, and selfish features (antibody dilution tables, primer sequence search). v2 is the ambitious part: a vendor-site browser extension, cell-bank QC, a plasmid registry, chemical safety/EHS, AI search and an MCP server.

Running cost is $0-25/month to host. The real constraints are adoption and having one maintainer.

build_vs_adopt.recommendation: Build a focused Django app from scratch. Copy InvenTree's data model and dependency stack, but do not fork it. Keep Quartzy for purchasing. Before writing feature code, run two short time-boxed spikes: (1) 2 days with InvenTree in Docker plus two bench users, to settle the 'build on it?' question with evidence; (2) 1 week against the Quartzy API: measure page size and sort order, test the webhook signature, and run the baseline duplicate count.
build_vs_adopt.rationale: Every other path still needs custom code for the lab's core problem, because no product checks Quartzy requests against personal stock, open requests and recent receipts. Commercial tools either duplicate Quartzy's purchasing, lock audit/API/storage features behind enterprise tiers, or price per seat (LabArchives Inventory is about $2,970/yr for 30 people). None integrates with Quartzy, and their bench UX gets weak reviews. InvenTree is the only credible open-source base (MIT, Django, mobile app, plugin mixins). But its manufacturing vocabulary (Parts/BOM/Build), lack of box grids, missing per-vial parameters, purchase orders that overlap Quartzy, and breaking releases (1.6.0) mean the differentiators would all live in fragile plugins anyway. A plain Django monolith with django-treebeard, Django-Q2, RapidFuzz, pg_trgm, allauth, WeasyPrint and segno gives one Python maintainer the most control at the least cost. Keep domain logic in a service layer so a later move onto InvenTree remains possible.

candidates.name: Custom Django app (companion to Quartzy)
pros: Built around Quartzy-aware duplicate interception and owned-but-visible personal stock
Bench-first UX and per-type schemas (cell lines, antibodies, plasmids) without workarounds
One language, Django admin as the back office, no license fees, full data ownership/export
cons: Bus factor of one; needs docs, tests and a backup maintainer
Everything (grids, labels, mobile) must be built and maintained

candidates.name: InvenTree + out-of-tree plugins (quartzy, boxes)
pros: MIT, Python/Django, very active, native iOS/Android app with scanning
21 plugin mixins (AppMixin, ScheduleMixin, UrlsMixin, UserInterfaceMixin, BarcodeMixin, LabelPrintingMixin)
Ready-made Part/SupplierPart/StockItem model, expiry digests, ownership, label printing
cons: Parts/BOM/Build vocabulary is foreign to biologists
No box-grid model; StockItem has no parameters
UI panels in JS/TS against an evolving React UI; AppMixin is a documented 'danger zone'; breaking releases
candidates.verdict: Runner-up. Choose it only if the 2-day spike shows bench users accept its UI and terminology

candidates.name: Quartzy Inventory module + thin duplicate-alert sidecar
pros: Already paid for; has instances (lot, expiry, up to 7 location levels), freezer boxes, owners, min/max, QBot, mobile app
Smallest build: just the mirror and alert service
cons: API cannot create inventory items or locations, so bulk entry is Excel import only
Visibility needs a Quartzy seat (Academia plan includes 3 users); labs don't share data with each other
Per-module search needs full catalog #/name; mobile app rated 3.2/5 with crash complaints; regional availability is contradictory
No cell-line, antibody or plasmid depth
candidates.verdict: Fallback if time or adoption collapses. The MVP's mirror and alert service is exactly this sidecar, so building it is never wasted

candidates.name: Commercial inventory/LIMS (LabArchives Inventory, Genemod, Labguru, SciNote)
pros: Mature freezer UX and lot models
LabArchives: $99/user/yr academic, 90-day trial; Genemod free up to 10 users
cons: No Quartzy integration or cross-source duplicate check
API/SSO/audit often enterprise-only (LabArchives, Genemod); SciNote storage and stock features are add-ons
A second ordering workflow would compete with Quartzy
candidates.verdict: Not recommended, unless the university already has a site license. In that case, evaluate pairing it with the sidecar

candidates.name: eLabFTW (adopt as-is)
pros: Free, self-hosted ELN plus resources, booking scheduler and procurement requests; Python client
cons: PHP; no box grids or consumption semantics; procurement routing not implemented; AGPL
candidates.verdict: Optional companion if the PI also wants an ELN and equipment booking. Link to it; don't extend it

candidates.name: openBIS
pros: Best life-science object types; Request->Order locking; freezer/rack/box positions
cons: Heavy Java deployment; 6.x/7.0 version transitions; too much for one person
candidates.verdict: Only if the institute already runs it

candidates.name: ChemInventory
pros: $56/yr for 30 users; GHS, CAS/structure search, items on order shown in search
candidates.verdict: Optional chemicals/EHS complement if the campus has no EHS system; otherwise skip

modules.name: Quartzy Sync & Purchasing Mirror
modules.purpose: Keep a near-real-time, read-only copy of Quartzy order requests, inventory and types. This is the data source for duplicate checks, receiving and spend reports.

features.name: Order-request poller with status history
features.description:
Django-Q2 job:
- every 5 min, pages GET /order-requests?lab_id=..&page=N (newest pages)
- nightly, a full scan until an empty page
- upserts by id and records each status/updated_at change in a status-observation table
- stores the raw JSON
- parses money and quantities (returned as strings) with Decimal
features.rationale: There are no webhooks for approved, cancelled or backordered requests, and webhooks retry only 3 times. Polling also works behind a campus firewall.

features.name: Quartzy inventory, types and labs mirror
features.description: Nightly read of GET /inventory-items (with instances[]), GET /types and GET /labs (uses_instances true/false/missing). Mirrored items count in duplicate checks and can be linked at put-away.
features.rationale: Stock already entered in Quartzy must not be missed by the duplicate guard.

features.name: History backfill and baseline duplicate analyzer
features.description: Pull all past requests, or the UI 'Export Requests: Submitted + All Time' CSV if no token is available. Normalize vendor and catalog number, then report the same product requested by different people within 30/60 days, plus purchases made while stock was recorded, with $ and top categories. Re-run monthly.
features.rationale: There are no credible public numbers on duplicate spend. The lab's own baseline justifies the project and calibrates the matcher.

features.name: Integration health panel
features.description: Shows GET /healthz, the token owner (GET /user), lab IDs, last successful sync, and an alert if no new requests appear for N hours. Includes token rotation and a weekly diff of public-api.yaml to catch silent API changes.
features.rationale: The API is unversioned and tokens belong to individual users. A silent failure would quietly reopen the duplicate gap.

features.name: Webhook receiver (fetch-on-hint)
features.description:
Subscribes to:
- order-request.created/ordered/received/deleted
- inventory-item.*
- type.*
- sales-order-item.*
- shipment.*
Returns 2xx within 3 s, stores the raw event, de-duplicates on the CloudEvents id, then re-fetches GET /order-requests/{id} as the authoritative record. HMAC signature checks are enforced only after testing what is signed and how it is encoded.
features.rationale: Cuts alert latency to seconds, but needs inbound HTTPS, and the signature format is undocumented.

features.name: Write-back to Quartzy
features.description:
After tests in a sandbox lab:
- PUT /order-requests/{id} status (CANCELLED/APPROVED/RECEIVED) from the approver console
- POST /order-requests from the app's gated request form
- in v2, PUT /inventory-items/{itemId}/instances/{instanceId} for quantities of items Quartzy tracks
All writes are logged with who and why.
features.rationale: Closes the loop, but how role checks, budget/custom-field rules and Money units behave is unverified.

modules.name: Duplicate-Order Guard
modules.purpose: Detect likely duplicates at every point where a purchase can happen. Make borrowing or joining an existing order easier than buying, and record the outcomes.

features.name: Tiered product matcher
features.description:
Matching tiers, in order:
1. Exact match on vendor family + normalized catalog key.
2. Same catalog base with a different pack size.
3. Shared identifier (CAS, RRID, Cellosaurus ID, Addgene ID) when known.
4. Fuzzy name match within the item type: pg_trgm finds candidates, RapidFuzz token_set_ratio scores them.
Negative rules: a different conjugate, host or clone means not a duplicate. Confidence tiers: High alerts the requester and approver; Medium alerts the requester only; Low appears only in search. Fast-moving consumables are compared with par levels instead.
features.rationale: Duplicates hide behind vendor rebrands, pack sizes and free-text names. Quartzy matches the exact catalog # only.

features.name: Instant alert on every new Quartzy request
features.description: Within one poll cycle (5 min or less), the requester and approver get a message such as: 'Lab has 2 vials (-80 #2 > Box 4, owner Priya); Sam requested this 3 days ago (APPROVED)'. It links to Quartzy's app_url and to a match page with one-tap outcomes: I'll cancel / Borrowing instead / Not a duplicate / Need it anyway (reason picklist). Covers requests from the Quartzy web UI, the mobile app, the Connect extension, QBot and the API.
features.rationale: This targets the PI's problem directly, and it lands before Quartzy's hourly approver emails. The API cannot comment inside Quartzy, so alerts must go outside it.

features.name: 'Check before you buy' search
features.description:
One mobile-first search box (by name, catalog #, CAS, lot or owner) with results grouped as:
- In the lab: owner, location path, quantity/status, expiry
- On order: requester, status, age, expected date
- Bought before: who, when, price
Buttons: Ask owner, and Request in Quartzy (a link).
features.rationale: People search before ordering only if search is faster than walking to the freezer. Personal stock and items already on order must appear together.

features.name: In-flight orders board
features.description: Lab-wide list of CREATED, APPROVED, ORDERED and BACKORDERED requests grouped by product, showing requester, age, backordered_expected_at, tracking number and budget. Requests ORDERED more than 21 days ago are flagged stale.
features.rationale: Handles the 'two people ordered it the same week' case. Reviewers asked Quartzy for exactly this dashboard.

features.name: Outcome ledger and threshold tuning
features.description: Every check stores its candidate matches, tier, score and outcome. '$ avoided' is counted conservatively (unit_price x quantity, only for cancelled or borrowed outcomes). 'Not a duplicate' answers feed back into the thresholds.
features.rationale: Gives honest numbers to the PI and fewer false alarms over time.

features.name: Approver console
features.description: Queue of CREATED requests showing a risk badge, the matches (the requester's own holdings highlighted), budget and the last 3 prices. Actions: Approve, Cancel as duplicate (PUT), or Decline and borrow from X (notifies both people). Every action is recorded with a reason.
features.rationale: Approval is the last cheap point to stop a duplicate. Once a request is Ordered, Quartzy cannot revert it.

features.name: Gated in-app requests
features.description: Reorder and New request run the duplicate check before POST /order-requests. Our check summary and a link go into Quartzy's 'notes' field. Requests are attributed through per-user tokens or Quartzy's declared OAuth2 flow; otherwise the app deep-links to Quartzy's own request form.
features.rationale: Catches the duplicate before the request exists. The POST body has no requested_by field.

features.name: Join an existing request (+1)
features.description: Records a second person's need against an open request and notifies the requester and approver to raise the quantity in Quartzy. The API cannot edit quantities.
features.rationale: Turns a would-be duplicate into one larger order.

features.name: Stale-request nudges
features.description: ORDERED for more than 21 days: ask the requester 'Did this arrive?' with Arrived / Still waiting / Cancelled. The answer updates the app (and Quartzy in v1).
features.rationale: Stale open requests pollute both our duplicate checks and Quartzy's.

features.name: QBot coordination
features.description: Recognizes Quartzy's automatic requests (QBot), suppresses our own reorder prompts for those items, and warns when a person requests something that already has an open QBot request.
features.rationale: Stops automatic requests from becoming a new source of duplicates.

features.name: 'Already have it?' browser extension
features.description: Chrome/Edge banner on vendor product pages (Thermo, Sigma, ATCC, CST, Abcam, NEB): 'Lab has 2 (Priya, -20 B2); Sam ordered 3 days ago', with Borrow / Join / Continue buttons.
features.rationale: Ordering decisions happen on vendor sites. No reviewed product, Quartzy Connect included, checks existing stock there.

features.name: Group-buy merging
features.description: Suggests combining open needs that match within a time window, or moving to a larger pack size, with the cost split across budgets.
features.rationale: Turns duplicates into discounts.

modules.name: Product Catalog & Identity
modules.purpose: Give every product one canonical identity that requests, stock and enrichment all point to.

features.name: Product master with vendor families and normalized catalog numbers
features.description: Vendor alias table (e.g. Gibco/Invitrogen/Life Technologies -> Thermo Fisher; Sigma-Aldrich/MilliporeSigma/Supelco -> Merck), with distributors kept separate. catalog_key = NFKC, uppercase, separators stripped, stored as text. catalog_base comes from per-vendor pack-suffix rules (e.g. NEB R0650S -> R0650). Seeded from Quartzy history; lab manager merges and splits in Django admin.
features.rationale: Everything downstream depends on this, and matching on raw strings misses most duplicates.

features.name: Item types with preset field schemas
features.description: Per-type JSON schemas (antibody, cell line, plasmid, strain, oligo, chemical, enzyme, kit, media/buffer, consumable, equipment), with product-level and vial-level fields, rendered by one generic form. Only identity fields are required.
features.rationale: Typed fields make search and dedup work (target+clone+conjugate) without 14 hand-built models.

features.name: Public identifier enrichment
features.description:
Resolve an identifier and prefill the record:
- Cellosaurus (CVCL_)
- PubChem (CAS -> CID, GHS)
- Antibody Registry (AB_)
- Addgene (approval-gated token)
- UniProt / NCBI
Uses per-source rate limits, a JSONB cache with fetched_at, and never overwrites curated fields.
features.rationale: Prefilled records save typing and supply the identifiers used for cross-vendor matching.

features.name: Equivalence groups and lab-standard products
features.description: Groups built from shared identifiers (e.g. HeLa = ATCC CCL-2 = ECACC 93021013 = DSMZ ACC-57) plus manual 'interchangeable' links (two FBS products). A lab-standard flag marks the preferred product.
features.rationale: Catalog-number matching can't see the same cell line or chemical sold by another vendor.

features.name: Nightly reference-data reconciliation
features.description: Re-checks Cellosaurus releases, ICLAC register versions, discontinued antibodies and GHS changes. Differences go into a review queue, never silently applied.
features.rationale: Reference data changes after purchase.

modules.name: Physical Inventory & Stock Ledger
modules.purpose: Track physical containers as distinct from catalog products and lots, keep an append-only history of every change, and keep updates to a tap or two.

features.name: Product -> Lot -> StockItem model
features.description: StockItem is one bottle, vial, tube, aliquot or box. It has an opaque short_id, lot, quantity+unit or a status-only mode, owner, visibility, location+position, a source order request, and per-vial attributes in JSONB. The product total is the sum of active items.
features.rationale: Hidden stock lives in individual tubes, and both Quartzy (2026) and LabCollector had to migrate to this model.

features.name: Big-button status actions
features.description: After a scan: Used some / Opened / Running low / Empty / Moved / Discard (reason required). Consumables need no volumes; exact quantities are optional for vials and aliquots.
features.rationale: Reviewers call per-use volume logging unrealistic. Status events keep the data current.

features.name: Empty -> reorder handoff
features.description: 'Empty' re-runs the duplicate check (does someone else have one?), then deep-links to the original Quartzy request, where 'Request Again' is available, or notifies the lab's supplies person.
features.rationale: Reordering from inventory links the request to existing stock, with zero API writes.

features.name: Append-only StockEvent ledger and model history
features.description: Every create, receive, move, use, split, discard, owner change or stocktake writes an immutable event: user, time, delta, from/to, reason, source, client_uuid. django-simple-history covers edits to reference data. Undo works by writing a compensating event.
features.rationale: Answers 'who took the last vial?'. History can't be backfilled later (Quartzy's audit only starts in March 2024).

features.name: Projected availability
features.description: SQL view per product and equivalence group: in_stock + requested (CREATED/APPROVED) + on_order (ORDERED/BACKORDERED) + received-not-shelved. Shown in search and alerts. When a request moves to ordered, its quantity moves buckets, so it is never counted twice.
features.rationale: ERPNext's projected-quantity accounting is exactly what duplicate prevention needs.

features.name: Aliquot/split with lineage
features.description: Split one item into N child items that inherit product, lot and owner. Positions are assigned and labels batch-printed. Freeze-thaw counter. The parent's remaining amount is reduced.
features.rationale: Aliquoting is constant work, and lineage traces which lot a failed experiment used.

features.name: Stocktake mode
features.description: Scan a location, then everything in it. Items not scanned go to a 'missing?' list sent to their owners; unlisted items can be quick-added. Quarterly schedule with reminders.
features.rationale: A short scheduled scan keeps counts trustworthy (Warwick: 30-60 min for a small lab).

features.name: Kits with components in several locations
features.description: A kit is a parent item; its components are child items, each with its own storage temperature, location and expiry. Reactions remaining are decremented.
features.rationale: Kit parts split across fridge and freezer are a common case of 'we had it all along'.

modules.name: Storage & Freezer Maps
modules.purpose: Model where things physically are, from building down to box position, and make freezers readable at a glance.

features.name: Typed location tree down to box
features.description: Location types: building > room > freezer/LN2 tank/fridge/cabinet > shelf/rack/canister > box. Prefixed codes (FRZ-, RCK-, BOX-), full breadcrumb paths, an owner on boxes that their contents inherit, and an optional row/column position. Built with django-treebeard MP_Node.
features.rationale: 'Who has it and where' is answerable at box level. Quartzy had to migrate from 2 to 7 levels.

features.name: Visual box grids
features.description: Box types (9x9, 10x10, 5x5) with A1-style labels. Click to place, select a whole row or column, drag to move. Color by owner, type or expiry; next-free-slot suggestion. Unique (box, row, col) for active items.
features.rationale: Freezer boxes are where personal stock hides. Use positions for cell lines and plasmids first.

features.name: Freezer templates and bulk creation
features.description: One form builds, say, 5 shelves x 4 racks x 7 boxes, with names and labels. A configurable depth lets fridges stay coarse.
features.rationale: Setup effort puts people off.

features.name: Capacity report and empty-slot finder
features.description: Percent occupancy per freezer and box, free-space highlighting, and dead-stock boxes (untouched for 12 months).
features.rationale: LabCollector users complained about finding space; freezer space costs money.

features.name: 2D rack-scanner import
features.description: Import VisionMate/DP5 rack scans, show missing/extra/changed tubes, and apply the changes.
features.rationale: Only worthwhile if the lab moves to pre-barcoded 2D tubes.

features.name: Freezer monitoring hooks
features.description: Store a probe ID per freezer and show alarms from an external monitor on the freezer page.
features.rationale: Protects the irreplaceable stock the map now shows.

modules.name: Receiving & Put-away
modules.purpose: Make inventory a by-product of purchasing: every delivery ends with an owner, a location and a label.

features.name: RECEIVED -> put-away task
features.description: When a request turns RECEIVED, the requester gets a 'to shelve' task prefilled from the order. They pick a recent location, search, or scan the box label; the box page then lists 'your items waiting -> Put here'. Lot and expiry are optional. Matching Quartzy inventory items are linked, and the requester is told where it went.
features.rationale: Separate data entry is the main reason inventories go stale. This step needs only one confirmation.

features.name: Self-reported arrival and partial receipts
features.description: 'It arrived (n of m)' from the in-flight board when Quartzy hasn't been updated. Partial receipts keep the remainder open.
features.rationale: Partial receipts stay ORDERED in Quartzy, and people forget to mark items received.

features.name: Outside-Quartzy purchase and gift log
features.description: 30-second form for P-card buys, direct vendor orders, collaborator gifts and free samples. They enter the same product and stock pipeline.
features.rationale: Duplicate detection only covers what the app can see.

features.name: GS1 and vendor barcode autofill
features.description: Scan the vendor barcode. biip parses AI 01 GTIN, 10 lot, 17 expiry and 21 serial (MilliporeSigma DataMatrix); custom parsers handle formats such as NEB's Code 128. The first scan teaches the app which GTIN belongs to which product.
features.rationale: Removes the most error-prone typing at receiving.

features.name: Unshelved reminders
features.description: Put-away tasks open for more than 2 days nudge the requester. The digest lists unclaimed deliveries.
features.rationale: Unclaimed boxes turn into hidden stock.

modules.name: Bench Mobile, Scanning & Labels
modules.purpose: Scan first, gloves on, no app install: every physical thing gets a label that opens its page.

features.name: URL-QR labels and mobile item/location pages
features.description: Opaque short IDs encoded as https://inv.<lab>/i/7F3K9Q. Any phone camera opens a big-button page. No mutable data in the code; the human-readable ID is printed too.
features.rationale: Avoids iOS BarcodeDetector gaps and app stores; labels stay valid when items move.

features.name: PDF label sheets and Brother QL printing
features.description: WeasyPrint/segno templates per object type, printable on any printer (including laser cryo sheets). Direct printing to a network Brother QL via brother_ql_next.
features.rationale: Without fast labels nothing gets scanned.

features.name: In-app scanner and keyboard-wedge support
features.description: barcode-detector polyfill + zxing-wasm (QR, DataMatrix, Code128, GS1), self-hosted WASM. Global listener for USB/Bluetooth HID scanners at the receiving bench and freezers.
features.rationale: Needed for continuous scanning (stocktake, receiving). html5-qrcode/zxing-js are in maintenance mode.

features.name: Cryo label printing
features.description: Zebra thermal-transfer printer, ZPL over TCP 9100, 8000T CryoCool labels (-196 C) with resin ribbon. Templates: vial, box, glycerol stock (ID on lid; plasmid + resistance on side).
features.rationale: Paper labels fall off in LN2 and -80, which destroys trust in the inventory.

features.name: Link existing vendor and pre-barcoded tube codes
features.description: Attach an external barcode to a record instead of relabeling. Check for duplicate barcodes.
features.rationale: Relabeling thousands of existing vials isn't realistic; barcode at next touch instead.

features.name: Installable PWA with offline scan queue
features.description: Service worker caches the app shell and box maps. Offline events go to IndexedDB with client UUIDs and replay when back online (Safari has no Background Sync).
features.rationale: Cold rooms often lack Wi-Fi. Move to v1 if a Wi-Fi survey finds dead zones.

modules.name: Ownership, Sharing & Lifecycle
modules.purpose: Let people keep their personal stock but make it visible to the lab, and make borrowing easier than buying.

features.name: Owned-but-visible stock
features.description: Each item has an owner (user or group, inherited from 'Priya's box') and a visibility level: shared, ask first (default), reserved for a project, or restricted (MTA/regulated, named people only). Lab-wide search always shows that an item exists and who owns it.
features.rationale: People hide stock out of fear of losing it; visible ownership removes the blind spot without a political fight.

features.name: Ask the owner
features.description: One-tap 'Can I use 20 uL of your anti-FLAG?' message (email/Slack/Teams) from search or item pages.
features.rationale: Borrowing has to take less effort than ordering.

features.name: Borrow/lend workflow
features.description: Owner approves or declines. Records a transfer (quantity, home vs current location, borrower, return-by date), sends reminders, credits lenders.
features.rationale: Formal borrowing replaces parallel purchases.

features.name: Leaver handover
features.description: Report of everything a departing person owns, bulk reassignment, and an orphaned-item queue. An account can't be closed until its items are transferred, pooled or discarded.
features.rationale: Student/postdoc turnover is how labs end up with mystery boxes.

features.name: Check-out and reservations
features.description: Check out to an assignee with a comment; reserve for a future date; check back in to a location.
features.rationale: Useful for shared antibodies and the last bank vials.

features.name: Surplus marketplace including neighbor labs
features.description: Post near-expiry or surplus items as free to claim; claims create transfers; optional department-wide visibility.
features.rationale: Campus reuse programs report large savings (Michigan over $1M in under 2 years).

modules.name: Onboarding & Migration
modules.purpose: Surface the 30 hidden personal inventories quickly, with no retyping and ownership kept.

features.name: Spreadsheet import with dedupe preview
features.description: XLSX/CSV templates per type. django-import-export dry run with column mapping. Catalog # and CAS imported as text. Likely duplicates clustered (RapidFuzz) for one-click merge. Owner defaults to the uploader; rows with no location go to a 'needs location' queue.
features.rationale: Personal inventories already exist as spreadsheets; import pain is a common complaint about every vendor.

features.name: Quick-add form
features.description: Only name, owner and location required; product matched as you type; everything else optional and auto-filled later.
features.rationale: A 20-field form at first contact kills adoption.

features.name: Amnesty-week leaderboard
features.description: Counts of items registered, locations verified and items shared, per person and bay, posted to the lab channel.
features.rationale: Makes the one-time backlog social and time-limited (Freezer Challenge pattern).

features.name: Box-map import
features.description: Excel grid (position -> sample) imports into box positions, with validation before commit.
features.rationale: Paper and Excel freezer maps are common for cell lines.

modules.name: Notifications & Chat
modules.purpose: Reach people where they already are, with few, targeted messages.

features.name: Channel adapters
features.description: Email (university SMTP or SES via django-anymail), a Slack bot posting DMs and channel messages, or a Teams Workflows webhook with Adaptive Cards (Office 365 connectors were retired in May 2026). Messages link to app pages, so outcome buttons work from any channel.
features.rationale: Alerts must go outside Quartzy.

features.name: Monday digest
features.description: Lab-channel and email summary: arrivals with locations, duplicates caught and $ avoided, stale requests, unshelved items; expiring items once v1 lands.
features.rationale: Digests beat per-event emails, which train people to filter the app's mail.

features.name: Interactive Slack/Teams bot
features.description: /have <query>, Approve/Decline buttons for borrowing, Cancel / Keep (reason) on duplicate alerts. Bolt for Python in Socket Mode, so no public URL is needed.
features.rationale: One-tap cancel is what actually saves money; works behind the campus firewall.

features.name: Per-user preferences and routing
features.description: DM vs digest-only. Expiry and test-due messages go to owners, duplicates to requester and approver, safety timers to the safety officer.
features.rationale: Avoids alert fatigue in a 30-person lab.

modules.name: Replenishment & Expiry
modules.purpose: Prevent the stock-outs and expiries that trigger panic orders and duplicates.

features.name: Expiry tracking, use-first ordering and 30/60/90-day reports
features.description: Received, opened and expiry dates per container, plus shelf-life-after-opening rules. Search shows the earliest-expiring instance first. Weekly 'use me first' digest to owners.
features.rationale: Expired stock is money already lost, and often a hidden duplicate.

features.name: Low-stock thresholds summed across lots
features.description: Product minimum computed across all active items and locations (optional per-location minimum). Below the minimum, a duplicate-aware reorder suggestion goes to the owner or supplies monitor.
features.rationale: Without the sum, one low lot triggers a reorder while other boxes are full.

features.name: Kanban shelf cards and supplies rota
features.description: Shelf/bin QR cards for tips, gloves and media: scanning one means 'running low'. Weekly rotating supplies monitor with a checklist reminder.
features.rationale: Tracking every box of cheap consumables wastes effort; shelf-level signals capture most of the value.

features.name: Standing orders and weekly vendor batching
features.description: Templates for high-volume consumables; pending needs grouped per vendor into one weekly order.
features.rationale: Cuts both panic orders and shipping fees.

features.name: Usage-based reorder forecasting
features.description: Predicts run-out dates from consumption events and Quartzy lead times (requested_at -> received).
features.rationale: Needs months of usage data first.

modules.name: Cell Lines & Biobanking
modules.purpose: Authenticated cell lines, banked stock you can trust, and protection for the last vial.

features.name: Cell line registry with vial tracking
features.description: Line record (Cellosaurus ID/RRID, source catalog #, BSL, MTA) linked to vial items (passage, freeze date, frozen by, cells per vial, tank > rack > box > position). Low-vial alert.
features.rationale: Cell lines are among the costliest duplicates (ATCC CCL-2 lists at $577).

features.name: Misidentified-line warning
features.description: Checks against Cellosaurus 'problematic' fields and the ICLAC register v14 (608 lines). Banner on the line, its vials and any request for it.
features.rationale: Cheap, and adds scientific value that wins over bench scientists.

features.name: Tiered banks
features.description: Token (3-5 vials), master (10-20) and working (20-200) banks with freeze passage/population doublings, QC on 5-10% of vials, and 'expand a new working bank from the master' prompts.
features.rationale: A trustworthy shared bank is what replaces personal stashes.

features.name: Passage and population-doubling ledger
features.description: Thawing creates a culture at vial passage+1. Splits record ratio and compute population doublings (1:4 = 2). Per-line limits are configurable data, not hard-coded.
features.rationale: Passage numbers aren't comparable between people without split ratios.

features.name: Mycoplasma/STR schedule with quarantine gates
features.description: Testing cadence per line (configurable). Overdue lines show 'unverified'. New arrivals stay quarantined until negative. STR alleles are sent to CLASTR (/str-search/api/query); a match below 80% raises a flag.
features.rationale: Attaching the checks to the vial people already touch is what makes them happen; it also supports NIH NOT-OD-15-103.

modules.name: Antibodies, Plasmids, Strains & Oligos
modules.purpose: Type-specific depth that gives people their own reason to open the app.

features.name: Antibody dilution table
features.description: Per antibody: application, dilution, diluent, sample, who, date, worked or failed (with image link). Vendor claims kept separate from lab-validated results.
features.rationale: Prized lab knowledge that currently lives in notebooks; brings people into the app.

features.name: New-lot re-validation alerts
features.description: A new antibody/serum/enzyme lot gets its own Lot record marked 'needs re-validation', and previous users are notified.
features.rationale: Lot-to-lot variation is the hidden cause of experiments that stop working; registries won't track lots.

features.name: Oligo registry with sequence search
features.description: Exact, reverse-complement and substring search; primer pairs; a resuspension calculator (uL for 100 uM = nmol x 10, using the delivered amount); bulk import from vendor order sheets.
features.rationale: Names are personal, so only sequence search catches re-ordered primers.

features.name: Plasmid registry with maps
features.description: GenBank/SnapGene/FASTA upload, features parsed with Biopython, seqviz viewer, Addgene ID, and a sequence-verified gate requiring evidence. Linked to glycerol stocks and DNA preps.
features.rationale: Re-cloning a labmate's construct costs weeks.

features.name: Strain lineage and backup-tube rule
features.description: Parent strain and plasmid links required at freeze-down, a lineage tree, and a required backup tube in a second freezer.
features.rationale: Strain collections become unreadable after their creator leaves.

features.name: sgRNA/siRNA and library records
features.description: Protospacer stored separately from the PAM, plus build coordinates and score provenance. Edited clones are linked back to their guide.
features.rationale: Only if the lab does a lot of editing.

modules.name: Chemicals, Safety & Compliance
modules.purpose: Make EHS and biosafety duties a side effect of normal inventory use, flagging and escalating rather than encoding regulations.

features.name: Regulated-material flag and escalation
features.description: Flag for DEA-scheduled, select agent/toxin, export-controlled or radioactive items. Hides self-service actions and names the responsible institutional officer.
features.rationale: Safer and less work than implementing the regulations.

features.name: GHS autofill and SDS store
features.description: CAS -> PubChem CID (xref/RN) -> properties plus PUG View GHS Classification, rate-limited to 5 req/s or less. SDS files stored per revision; pictograms shown on lists and labels.
features.rationale: Nobody types hazard data by hand.

features.name: Biosafety and MTA linkage
features.description: BSL and IBC/IRB protocol number on cell lines, vectors, strains and samples. Structured MTA flags (academic-only, no redistribution) checked before sharing outside the lab.
features.rationale: Human/primate lines are BSL-2 under BMBL guidance, and MTA terms are usually remembered by one person.

features.name: Peroxide-former timers
features.description: Class A/B/C set at intake; test-or-discard tasks generated from receipt and opening dates; intervals configurable by the institution.
features.rationale: A real explosion hazard controlled only by dates the app already records.

features.name: EHS inventory export
features.description: Quantities by room and control area grouped by hazard class, in the format campus EHS asks for.
features.rationale: Turns an annual manual spreadsheet exercise into a by-product.

features.name: Methods-section and RRID export
features.description: Select the materials behind a figure and export a formatted paragraph: RRIDs, catalog #, lot, passage, last STR/mycoplasma test, dilutions.
features.rationale: A visible personal payoff at submission time.

features.name: Storage-compatibility warnings
features.description: Warns when putting away incompatible groups together (oxidizer near flammable, acid near base or cyanide).
features.rationale: Useful but depends on clean hazard data first.

features.name: Controlled-substance perpetual log
features.description: Tamper-evident receipt-to-disposal log, Schedule I-II kept separate, biennial count report. Built with the institutional program.
features.rationale: Only if the lab holds scheduled substances.

modules.name: Reporting & PI Dashboard
modules.purpose: Prove value to the PI with conservative numbers, and watch adoption.

features.name: PI dashboard v0
features.description: Duplicates flagged and their outcomes, $ avoided (conservative), open requests by age, % of items with owner+location, weekly active users out of 30, % of updates made at the bench. Lab-level, not used to shame people.
features.rationale: The PI asked for visibility and savings; this is what keeps the mandate.

features.name: Monthly one-page report
features.description: Spend by budget (spend_tracking_code), project, person and vendor; expiring and dead-stock value; personal vs shared value; duplicate trend vs baseline; CSV/PDF export.
features.rationale: Quartzy's Spend Dashboard doesn't measure duplicates avoided.

features.name: Spend and vendor analytics
features.description: Same product bought from several vendors or at several prices, price creep, vendor lead times, top recurring items as standing-order candidates.
features.rationale: Consolidating recurring buys is a commonly reported saving.

modules.name: Admin, Security & Ops
modules.purpose: Easy sign-in, simple roles, and boring, recoverable operations for a single maintainer.

features.name: Login and roles
features.description: django-allauth: login-by-code (emailed code) and Google/Microsoft OIDC, long sessions on phones. Django Groups: Member, Lab manager/Approver, PI, Admin. Object rules (owner, manager, restricted) via the rules library.
features.rationale: Every password prompt at the bench costs adoption.

features.name: Backups, monitoring and full export
features.description: Nightly pg_dump plus media to off-site storage via restic, monthly restore drill, heartbeat checks on sync and backup jobs, error tracking, one-click CSV/XLSX export of every table.
features.rationale: Bus factor of one, and vendors in this space have merged or pivoted.

features.name: 'This is annoying' button
features.description: One tap logs friction with screen and context; triaged weekly, top 3 fixed and announced.
features.rationale: Workarounds are the earliest sign of failure.

features.name: University SSO and passkeys
features.description: SAML 2.0 (Shibboleth/InCommon) or Entra OIDC, passkeys, MFA for admins, automatic offboarding.
features.rationale: Depends on IT lead time for registering the app with the SSO system.

features.name: Rotator and guest accounts
features.description: Accounts that expire, a sponsor who approves requests, and items owned by the sponsor by default.
features.rationale: Rotators create orphaned stock.

features.name: REST API and Python client
features.description: django-ninja with OpenAPI docs, scoped tokens for scripts, the print agent and integrations.
features.rationale: Lets the bioinformaticians script bulk changes, and avoids lock-in.

modules.name: AI & Assistants
modules.purpose: Cut data entry and lookup effort, with a person always confirming before anything is saved.

features.name: Photo intake for labels, packing slips and box lids
features.description: Claude vision with structured outputs returns vendor, catalog #, lot, expiry, quantity and grid positions, plus a confidence for each. The prefilled form highlights low-confidence fields for confirmation. Used when no barcode parses, and during migration.
features.rationale: Most legacy stock exists only as labels and handwritten box maps.

features.name: Natural-language inventory search
features.description: 'Do we have anti-GAPDH HRP validated for WB?' answered via read-only, permission-scoped tools (search_products, list_containers, open_requests), never raw SQL; answers link to records.
features.rationale: Lowers the barrier for people who won't learn filters.

features.name: SDS extraction batch
features.description: Batch API (50% off) pulls signal word, pictograms, H/P statements and storage class from SDS PDFs into a review queue.
features.rationale: Builds the chemical safety layer without typing.

features.name: Read-only MCP server
features.description: search_inventory, find_locations and list_open_requests over OAuth, using the user's own permissions.
features.rationale: Scispot, SciSure and Benchling have moved this way; start read-only.

features.name: Agent actions with sign-off
features.description: Multi-step plans ('move box 7 to freezer 2 and reorder buffer') shown as a diff that a person must approve.
features.rationale: Only after the data model and audit trail have proven stable.

modules.name: Equipment & Facilities
modules.purpose: Long tail: shared instruments and storage units, handled by linking existing tools rather than rebuilding them.

features.name: Equipment booking and maintenance via integration
features.description: Link to eLabFTW's scheduler, NEMO (Django) or Snipe-IT rather than building them. Storage units already exist as locations with a service log.
features.rationale: Secondary to duplicate orders and already solved elsewhere.

duplicate_prevention_design:
1. Policy, week 0: the PI announces the rules:
- search before requesting
- personal stock is allowed but must be visible
- give a reason to order despite a strong match
- confirm a location when your order arrives
- log non-Quartzy purchases within 24 h
Optionally set Quartzy approval steps for categories prone to duplicates (antibodies, cell lines, kits, enzymes), because auto-approved requests under the threshold skip the approver touchpoint.

2. Seed the matcher (MVP, before launch): backfill Quartzy history and current Quartzy inventory, import personal spreadsheets, and normalize vendors and catalog numbers into one product master. Then run the baseline analyzer to set thresholds and record the 'before' number.

3. Before ordering, the habit (MVP): the 'check before you buy' search (typed, or scanned in v1) shows three groups:
- In the lab: owner, location path, status, expiry, across personal and shared stock and mirrored Quartzy inventory
- On order: requester, status, age, expected date
- Bought before: who, when, price
Actions: Ask owner (MVP), Borrow (v1), Join existing request (v1), Request in Quartzy.
4. On vendor sites (v2): the browser extension reads the catalog # on Thermo/Sigma/ATCC/CST/Abcam/NEB pages and shows the same three groups before the user clicks Quartzy Connect or adds to cart.

5. When the request is created inside our app (v1): the matcher runs before POST /order-requests. A high-confidence match requires a reason. The request's notes field carries the check summary and an app link. Per-user tokens or OAuth keep the real requester attached; otherwise the app deep-links to Quartzy's Add Request form.

6. When any Quartzy request appears (MVP): poll every 5 minutes, or (v1) the order-request.created webhook, then re-fetch the request by id. This covers requests from the Quartzy web UI, mobile app, Connect extension, QBot and API. The tiered matcher checks:
- stock with status not empty
- open requests (CREATED/APPROVED/ORDERED/BACKORDERED), with their age shown
- receipts from the last 90 days, including not yet shelved
- equivalence groups (v1)
High confidence: DM/email the requester and approver within minutes, ahead of Quartzy's hourly approver email. Medium: notify the requester only. Each alert offers Cancel in Quartzy (app_url) / Borrowing / Not a duplicate / Need anyway + reason. The outcome is written to the duplicate log.

7. At approval (MVP via the alert; v1 console): the approver sees the risk badge, the requester's own holdings, other open requests and the last 3 prices. Actions are Approve, Cancel as duplicate (PUT status after sandbox verification), or Decline and borrow. Unresolved high-confidence flags are re-sent to whoever places orders before 'Mark Ordered', because nothing can be reverted from Ordered.

8. At ordering (order-request.ordered event or a poll diff): requested quantity moves to on-order in projected availability, so it isn't counted twice. If a flagged request was ordered without being resolved, it is logged as 'duplicate ordered' for metrics, and its requester is reminded to offer the surplus to the lab.

9. At receiving (MVP): RECEIVED (seen by poll or webhook), or an 'it arrived' report in the app, creates a put-away task prefilled from the order, with the requester as owner. The requester confirms a location by picking or scanning a box. The item is merged into the existing product (never a new duplicate record), linked to any matching Quartzy inventory item, and labeled. Partial receipts keep the rest open. Items still unshelved after 2 days get a nudge (v1), and until then they count as 'recently received' in all checks.

10. At point of use, ongoing (MVP/v1): Used / Low / Empty taps keep stock accurate. Empty re-runs the duplicate check before handing off to reorder. Low-stock thresholds are summed across lots so a single low lot doesn't trigger a reorder (v1). QBot's open auto-requests suppress our own prompts (v1).

11. Hygiene, ongoing (v1):
- ORDERED for more than 21 days -> 'did it arrive?' nudge
- expiry and use-first digests
- quarterly stocktake scan
- leaver handover before an account closes
- vendor alias and equivalence curation
- 'not a duplicate' feedback retunes thresholds

12. Proof, monthly (MVP dashboard; v1 report): re-run the analyzer against the baseline and report duplicates caught and $ avoided, counted only for accepted cancel/borrow/merge outcomes. Results are shown at lab level, with lenders celebrated rather than duplicators named.

quartzy_integration.approach:
Treat Quartzy as the purchasing system of record and our app as the inventory system of record and the duplicate guard. The MVP is strictly read-only against Quartzy, using only capabilities confirmed in the verification block.

(1) Auth: an Access-Token header from a Lab Admin's account (ideally the lab manager who already has a seat). Store it as a secret and monitor it via GET /user.

(2) Discovery: GET /labs (record uses_instances; treat a missing value as migrated) and GET /types.

(3) Mirror:
- every 5 min: GET /order-requests?lab_id=&page=N for the newest pages
- nightly: a full scan until an empty array comes back
- upsert by id; detect status changes by diffing status and updated_at, since there are no approved/cancelled/backordered webhooks
- nightly: GET /inventory-items, including instances
Poll politely. No rate limits are documented, and the ToS forbid unreasonable load.

(4) Alerts go outside Quartzy (Slack/Teams/email), because the API has no comment endpoint and notes can only be set at creation.

(5) v1, if the host accepts inbound HTTPS: register webhooks in the UI (Manage Labs > Developers, needs Lab Admin) for:
- order-request.created/ordered/received/deleted
- inventory-item.*
- type.*
- sales-order-item.*
- shipment.*
Acknowledge in under 3 s, de-duplicate on the CloudEvents id, and use each event only as a hint to re-fetch GET /order-requests/{id}. Enforce the HMAC-SHA256 Signature check only after empirically confirming the signed bytes and encoding. Polling stays on as reconciliation, since there are only 3 retries (10/100/1000 s).

(6) v1 writes, only after tests in a sandbox lab:
- PUT /order-requests/{id} status for approver actions, with a Lab Admin token
- POST /order-requests from the gated request form, with required fields lab_id, type_id, name, vendor_name, catalog_number, price{amount,currency}, quantity, plus notes containing our check summary. The body has additionalProperties: false.
Requester attribution needs per-user tokens or a Quartzy OAuth2 client (the flow is declared in the spec; how to register a client is undocumented). Otherwise deep-link to Quartzy.

(7) Inventory: our app creates and owns all physical records, because the API cannot create Quartzy inventory. Quartzy inventory is mirrored read-only for duplicate checks. Lab policy choice: either set Quartzy receiving to 'Do Not Add To Inventory' after launch, or keep Quartzy inventory for QBot consumables with v2 quantity sync via PUT /inventory-items/{itemId}/instances/{instanceId}.

(8) Confirm with Quartzy in writing (support@quartzy.com): (a) showing mirrored data to members without seats; (b) an OAuth client; (c) an integration account. ToS §3.2(a) frames account sharing as fee circumvention.
verified_capabilities_used: Base URL https://api.quartzy.com; Access-Token header (per-user tokens from Profile Settings > Access Tokens); API generally available to all users; pricing page lists 'APIs and webhooks' as included
GET /healthz (no auth), GET /user (id, names, email only)
GET /labs and /labs/{id} (id, name, uses_instances, organization); GET /types?lab_id&name&page (type_id needed for POST)

GET /order-requests?lab_id&page: bare array; fields status, item_name, vendor_name, catalog_number, quantity, unit_size, unit_price, total_price, requested_at, updated_at, requested_by, created_by, notes, app_url, spend_tracking_code.name, is_urgent, backordered_expected_at, tracking/PO/confirmation numbers; no status, date or updated_since filters

GET /order-requests/{id}; POST /order-requests (required lab_id, type_id, name, vendor_name, catalog_number, price Money, quantity integer; optional vendor_product_id, required_before, notes; additionalProperties false)

GET /inventory-items(?lab_id&page) and /{id} with active instances[] (quantity, lot_number, expiration_date, location.pathNames); no owner field; PUT /inventory-items/{itemId}/instances/{instanceId} quantity only; PUT /inventory-items/{id} deprecated; no inventory create/delete; no DELETE operations at all

Webhooks: CloudEvents 1.0 envelope; HMAC-SHA256 in Signature header; 2xx within 3 s; retries at 10/100/1000 s; TLS validated; exactly 17 events (order-request created/deleted/ordered/received; inventory-item created/updated/deleted; type created/updated/deleted; sales-order.placed; sales-order-item shipped/delivered/backordered/cancelled; shipment created/delivered); no order-request approved/cancelled/updated/backordered events
POST /webhooks accepts a lab_id+url or organization_id+url body (oneOf); GET returns signing_key (nullable); PUT only toggles is_enabled
OAuth2 authorization-code flow declared in the official spec (auth0.quartzy.com/authorize and /oauth/token, empty scopes) as an alternative to Access-Token
order-request.created fires for Shop and non-Quartzy vendor requests; order-request.deleted covers admin hard-deletes only, not cancellations
Native duplicate warning: same catalog #, same lab, New/Approved/Ordered/Backordered only; Add Request lookup is limited to the current lab and can be skipped; labs don't share contents
Partial receipts keep the request in the Ordered tab; receiving can be 'Do Not Add To Inventory'; Admins can revert Received -> New, but nothing reverts from Ordered
Approver emails are sent hourly; Budgets can be required; custom request fields can be required; members can mark Received; Mark Ordered and cancelling others' requests are Admin-only in the UI
Quartzy Connect Chrome extension lets any user create requests from vendor pages (no documented duplicate check)

UI exports: Requests 'Submitted + All Time' CSV (All Labs view combines labs into one file); Spend Dashboard CSV; scheduled monthly spend and weekly reconciliation emails; per-lab inventory Excel export and emailed weekly/monthly backups
ToS §3.2(a) account sharing to circumvent fees, (e) working around limits, (f) unreasonable load, (i) robots/crawlers
fallbacks: No API token or API access: weekly UI export of requests ('Submitted' + 'All Time', All Labs view), dropped into an upload page or a watched folder, plus the per-lab inventory Excel export. Duplicate alerts become batch-level (daily), and search stays fully functional.

Scheduled Quartzy email reports (monthly spend, weekly reconciliation, weekly/monthly inventory backups) sent to a dedicated mailbox and parsed over IMAP. Exact formats are unverified, so treat this as best-effort.
No inbound HTTPS (campus firewall): polling only, which still gives about 5-minute latency, ahead of the hourly approver emails.
Quartzy's native Slack app posts item requested/ordered/received messages to a channel. Our Socket Mode bot can read that channel as an event hint and then re-fetch by id. Message format unverified.
Webhook signature can't be verified: never act on webhook content; use it only as a trigger to re-fetch authoritative data through the API.

Writes blocked (role checks, required budget/custom fields, Money units): keep the app read-only; deep-link users to the Quartzy request (app_url / Request Again), and approvers to Quartzy's approval screen.
Quartzy changes the API with no versioning: weekly diff of public-api.yaml, plus the changelog RSS feed; a client generated from the spec; idempotent upserts keyed by Quartzy id.
Token owner leaves: documented token rotation, and the health panel alerts when a sync fails or no requests arrive for N hours.
unknowns: Page size and sort order of list endpoints (measure in week 1; this decides how many pages each poll must read)
Rate limits and throttling behavior (none documented)
Webhook HMAC details: what is signed, hex vs base64, meaning of is_verified, whether GET returns signing_key or null
Whether event_types takes the full string (com.quartzy.order-request.created) or the short form
Money.amount units (cents vs dollars) for POST
Whether PUT status respects approval workflows and roles; whether RECEIVED via the API creates inventory
Behavior of POST when Budget or custom request fields are required
Whether order-request.received fires on partial receipts
How UI 'Pending' and approval denials map to the API status enum
Whether the native duplicate warning normalizes catalog numbers (dashes, case)
Whether one token covers all of a user's labs, and whether tokens expire
How to register an OAuth2 client (client_id, redirect URIs)
Whether showing mirrored Quartzy data to members without seats is acceptable under the license/ToS
Mobile app regional availability (official sources conflict)
Whether the lab has been migrated to inventory instances (rollout excludes labs with inventory integrations)
Contents of the webhook 'events' array (possibly OrderRequestEvent with comments)
Column list of request CSV exports

data_model.notes: The family is the unit used for matching. Distributor SKUs are kept separate from manufacturer catalog numbers.

key_fields: key (cell_line, antibody, plasmid, strain, oligo, chemical, enzyme, kit, media_buffer, consumable, sample, equipment)
product_field_schema (JSON Schema: name, datatype, unit, enum, required, enrichment_source)
identity_rule (catalog | CAS | RRID | CVCL | Addgene | sequence)
data_model.notes: Field definitions are data, not migrations. Cadences (mycoplasma, passage limits, peroxide intervals) live in PolicySetting, also as data.

key_fields: attributes JSONB (validated by type schema: target, clone, host, conjugate, species, backbone...)
indexed identifiers: cas_number, pubchem_cid, rrid, cellosaurus_ac, addgene_id, uniprot_ac, sequence_norm
data_model.notes: Lab-made items (preps, buffers, derived lines) are Products with no SupplierProduct.

data_model.entity: SupplierProduct (how it is bought: vendor + catalog + pack)
data_model.notes: Unique (vendor_family, catalog_key). A GTIN identifies one pack, not the product family; the mapping is learned at first receipt.
Lets the matcher see that HeLa from ECACC duplicates ATCC vials already in LN2.
Unique (supplier_product, lot_number). This is where antibody, serum and enzyme lot-change alerts and per-lot QC hang.

data_model.entity: StockItem (physical container: bottle / vial / tube / aliquot / box of tips)
key_fields: quantity Decimal + unit (nullable in status_only mode)
status (available | opened | low | empty | reserved | quarantined | checked_out | discarded | lost)
attributes JSONB (per-vial: passage, freeze_date, frozen_by, cells_per_vial, conc)
data_model.notes: Partial unique index on (location_id, pos_row, pos_col) for active items. Current quantity is cached from the ledger. Never hard-deleted.

relationships: Tree: site > building > room > unit (freezer / LN2 tank / fridge / cabinet / shelf) > shelf / rack / canister > box > position
data_model.notes: LocationType carries the icon, whether it is structural (cannot hold items), whether it is a grid, default dimensions and barcode prefix. Every node gets a QR label. Moving a rack moves its subtree atomically and writes events.

key_fields: email (join key to Quartzy requested_by / created_by)
relationships: Team groups people for leaderboards and group ownership
data_model.notes: Quartzy has no members API, so people are mapped by email from request payloads.
type_id is required for POST /order-requests.

key_fields: status (CREATED | APPROVED | ORDERED | BACKORDERED | RECEIVED | CANCELLED | DELETED)
Observation: from_status, to_status, observed_at, via (poll | webhook)
data_model.notes: The API exposes only the current status, so history is rebuilt from observations. Requests with no catalog number are matched on name and type only.
Created when RECEIVED is seen or someone reports 'it arrived'. Open tasks count as 'received, not shelved' in projected availability.

key_fields: check: id, subject (order_request | draft request | search), run_at, matcher_version, max_confidence
match: candidate_type (stock_item | open_request | recent_receipt | quartzy_inventory_item), candidate_id, tier (exact_catalog | same_base_other_pack | identifier_equivalent | fuzzy_name), score
outcome (cancelled | borrowed | joined | kept_with_reason | not_duplicate | ignored | ordered_anyway)
data_model.notes: Feeds the PI dashboard and threshold tuning. Value is counted only for accepted cancel, borrow or join outcomes.

key_fields: type (receive | import | create | open | use | mark_low | mark_empty | move | split | owner_transfer | check_out | check_in | reserve | discard | stocktake_seen | adjust | quartzy_sync | undo)
reason (required for discard and cross-owner moves)
data_model.notes: Never updated or deleted. django-simple-history tracks edits to Product, SupplierProduct, Lot, Location, ItemType and Person.

relationships: writes StockEvent on approve or return
data_model.notes: The MVP sends 'Ask owner' messages only; v1 adds full records.

key_fields: target (product | lot | stock_item | location | cell bank)
kind (SDS | CoA | GenBank | SnapGene | STR | mycoplasma | photo | protocol)
data_model.notes: Stored on a local volume behind permission-checked views and backed up with restic (MinIO CE is archived).

key_fields: bank: product_id, tier (token | master | working), freeze_date, passage_at_freeze, PDL_at_freeze, vial_count, qc_summary
culture: from_vial_id, passage, cumulative_PDL, split events (ratio, date, by)
test: template (mycoplasma PCR | STR | sequencing | endotoxin), target, result, date, attachment, clastr_score
data_model.notes: Line -> bank -> vial -> culture are kept as separate entities so passage history and quality-control provenance remain possible.

key_fields: source (cellosaurus | pubchem | antibody_registry | addgene | uniprot | iclac)
data_model.notes: A cached, versioned snapshot. Changes go to a review queue and never silently overwrite curated fields.

key_fields: notification: recipient, channel, type, object, sent_at, acted_at
policy: key (matcher thresholds, stale_days, digest schedule, cadences), value, scope
friction: user, screen, object, text, status
data_model.notes: Used to measure alert fatigue and adoption, and to keep every threshold configurable.
Follows ERPNext's projected-quantity accounting; shown in search, alerts and the approver console.

fields: REQUIRED at entry: name, owner, location of vials
source collection + catalog # (ATCC CCL-2, DSMZ ACC-57, ECACC, JCRB, RIKEN)
