adoption_strategy: Week 0, PI mandate and roles: at a lab meeting the PI announces the rules: search first, personal stock stays yours but is visible, give a reason to order despite a strong match, confirm a location on arrival, and log non-Quartzy buys within 24 h. Name the roles: system owner (you), deputy maintainer (the other bioinformatician), operations owner (whoever approves and places Quartzy orders, ideally also the data steward) and 3-4 bench champions, one per bay, with a small explicit time allowance. Champions coach; they don't do other people's data entry.

Week 1, measure before building: pull 12-24 months of Quartzy requests and current inventory, run the baseline duplicate analyzer, and show the PI the $ figure and top categories. Record baseline adoption numbers: members with Quartzy seats, % of requests made from inventory, % of received items with a location. In parallel run the 2-day InvenTree spike, a barcode census of the 50 most-ordered items, and a Wi-Fi survey of the freezer rooms.

Weeks 2-4, ship the visibility layer with zero data entry: Quartzy mirror, search, in-flight board, duplicate alerts to requester and approver, PI dashboard v0. Everyone gets read access (after checking the Quartzy terms). Value arrives before anyone is asked to type anything.

Weeks 3-5, prototype tests: 3-5 bench users do real tasks (receive a package, take the last tube, find an antibody), timed against targets of 'who has X' in under 10 s, a bench update in 2 taps, and receiving in under 30 s. Cut required fields to name + owner + location.

Weeks 5-6, Inventory Amnesty Week:
- Members upload personal spreadsheets with the import wizard (ownership kept, default 'ask first'), or spend 30-60 minutes with a champion labeling a shelf or freezer.
- No judgement about what turns up.
- Freezer clean-out at the same time, with a leaderboard and small prizes.

Migration rules for personal stock:
- Use box-level locations first; record positions only for cell lines, plasmids and strains.
- Label existing vials at the next time they're handled rather than relabeling everything.
- Seed products from Quartzy history so people only add owner and location.
- Rows without a location go to a 'needs location' queue the owner clears.
- Paper box maps are handled by the v1 photo intake or a champion-assisted scan session.

From launch, receiving is the only entry path for new stock: every RECEIVED request becomes a put-away task for its requester. After a few weeks, decide whether Quartzy receiving should be set to 'Do Not Add To Inventory' (app is the inventory system of record) or keep Quartzy inventory for QBot consumables.

Train in three waves:
1. Prototype sessions.
2. 15-minute task demos at the bench for each sub-group just before each feature goes live.
3. A follow-up 2-4 weeks later to collect workarounds; this is the session most often skipped.
Put a one-page cheat sheet and an app QR code on every bench and freezer.

First 90 days:
- In-person support at the bench for 2 weeks.
- A 5-minute check-in at lab meeting weekly for a month.
- A public friction register with the top 3 fixed and announced.
- Old spreadsheets kept read-only until the app is clearly faster.
Warning signs: spreadsheets reappearing, entries batched at the end of the day, one person doing most of the entries.

Selfish hooks in v1: antibody dilution tables, primer sequence search, 'your package is in Fridge 2 shelf B' arrival messages, and borrow-instead-of-buy. People open the app for their own benefit, and the inventory stays current as a side effect.
Reporting that motivates rather than shames: a Monday digest and a monthly PI one-pager with conservative $ avoided, celebrating lenders. Per-person views are for the PI and lab manager only.

Keep it going:
- Build the app into onboarding (a 10-minute task tour + first scan) and offboarding (an account can't close until its items are transferred).
- Quarterly 1-hour stocktake by location.
- Annual freezer clean-out (join the Freezer Challenge or LEAF if your campus participates).
- Monthly analyzer re-run showing the trend against the baseline.

risks.risk: Quartzy API surprises: undocumented page size and sort order, rate limits, signature format, Money units, role enforcement, behavior when budget/custom fields are required; no API versioning.
risks.mitigation: Read-only MVP. Week-1 measurement spike. Writes only after tests in a sandbox lab. Webhooks used only as hints to re-fetch. Generated client plus weekly spec diff and changelog RSS. Polite polling with backoff.

risks.risk: License/ToS: members without seats seeing Quartzy data through our app, or one token acting for 30 people, could be read as fee circumvention (ToS §3.2(a)).
risks.mitigation: Keep the app read-only for visibility; requests still go through Quartzy seats. Ask support@quartzy.com in writing before launch. Prefer per-user tokens or an OAuth client for anything written back.

risks.risk: Too many false-positive alerts cause alert fatigue, and people stop reading them.
risks.mitigation: Confidence tiers; reason required only on high-confidence matches; negative rules (conjugate, host, pack); par-level logic for consumables; one-tap 'not a duplicate' feedback; thresholds tuned on labelled history; digests over per-event mail.

risks.risk: Adoption failure: data entry feels like a chore, or one superuser does everyone's typing.
risks.mitigation: Receiving-driven creation, status-only taps, three required fields, import as-is, champions who coach rather than type, adoption metrics on the dashboard, PI mandate, and a friction register with visible fixes.

risks.risk: Bus factor of one and scope creep against the 4-6 week MVP.
risks.mitigation: Plain Django monolith, deputy maintainer, runbook, tests on the Quartzy sync and matcher, strict MVP cut list (no grids, AI or cryo printing until v1), full CSV export as insurance.

risks.risk: Hidden stock stays hidden because people fear losing control of it.
risks.mitigation: Owned-but-visible defaults, 'ask first' and 'reserved' flags, borrowing credit for lenders, no shaming, amnesty week framed as protection for their stock.

risks.risk: Parallel inventories: Quartzy receiving creates inventory items while our app creates stock, producing double records.
risks.mitigation: Mirror and link Quartzy items at put-away. Decide one system of record within a month of launch. Set Quartzy receiving to 'Do Not Add To Inventory' or limit Quartzy inventory to QBot consumables.

risks.risk: Purchases outside Quartzy (P-card, gifts, core facilities) are invisible to the guard.
risks.mitigation: Outside-purchase form (v1), PI rule to log within 24 h, monthly reconciliation against the lab's spend reports.

risks.risk: Labels fail in LN2 or -80, codes become unreadable, and trust collapses.
risks.mitigation: Cryo-rated stock (CryoCool, B-490/B-461, laser cryo sheets), labels applied at room temperature, a one-week freezer test before rollout, a human-readable ID on every label, and support for linking existing tube barcodes.

risks.risk: Phone scanning is unreliable (iOS camera APIs, frost, small DataMatrix codes, dead Wi-Fi).
risks.mitigation: URL QR read by the native camera first; keyboard-wedge scanners at fixed stations; zxing-wasm polyfill; offline queue if the Wi-Fi survey requires it; manual search fallback.

risks.risk: Webhooks are unreachable or events are missed (3 s timeout, 3 retries).
risks.mitigation: Polling is the primary mechanism; webhooks only cut latency; nightly full reconciliation; heartbeat alerts.

risks.risk: Product identity errors: vendor rebrands, distributor SKUs, Excel-mangled catalog numbers.
risks.mitigation: Vendor alias families, separate distributor SKUs, text-typed imports, admin merge/split, GTIN learned at receipt, identifier-based equivalence (v1).

risks.risk: Regulated, MTA-bound or human-derived material is over-shared, or identifiable donor data ends up stored.
risks.mitigation: Restricted visibility level, regulated flag with escalation to the institutional officer, structured MTA/consent flags, pseudonymized IDs only, biosafety officer and EHS consulted before those modules.

risks.risk: Token owner leaves, or the token silently expires.
risks.mitigation: Token held by the lab manager or a dedicated integration account, rotation runbook, health panel alerting on sync failure or N hours with no new requests.

risks.risk: AI extraction errors or refusals corrupt records.
risks.mitigation: AI only prefills forms; a person confirms; confidence per field; read-only tools; handle the refusal stop reason with fallbacks; log usage; keep AI out of the MVP.

risks.risk: Overclaiming savings undermines the PI's trust.
risks.mitigation: Count $ only on accepted cancel/borrow/join outcomes, compare against the measured baseline, never quote unsourced vendor statistics.

open_questions_for_user: Which Quartzy plan is the lab on, how many of the 30 people have seats, and how many Quartzy 'Labs' do you use? Who is Lab Admin, and can they create an Access Token and webhooks (Manage Labs > Developers)? Can a test lab be created for sandbox tests?
Who approves and who places Quartzy orders (PI, lab manager, each member)? Is there an approval flow or an auto-approve threshold, and who marks items Received?
Does the lab also use Quartzy's Inventory module today? If so, should our app replace it, or keep it for consumables with automatic low-stock requests (QBot)?
Roughly what share of purchases bypass Quartzy (P-card, direct vendor sites, core facilities, collaborator gifts)?
Which categories drive the duplicate cost (cell lines, antibodies, kits, enzymes, FBS/media, oligos, consumables)? Any recent concrete examples to calibrate the matcher?
Slack, Microsoft Teams, or only email?

Hosting: can IT give you a university VM on the same network as the label printers? Is inbound HTTPS from the internet allowed (needed for Quartzy webhooks)? Which SSO (Shibboleth/SAML, Entra OIDC, Google), and how long does registering the app take?
Are phones allowed at the bench and in BSL-2 rooms? Is Wi-Fi available in cold rooms and freezer corridors?
Which label printers and scanners already exist (Zebra, Brother, Brady, DYMO)? Is there budget for one network label printer, cryo label stock and 2-3 2D scanners?
How many -80/-20 freezers, LN2 tanks and boxes are there? Box geometry (9x9, 10x10, canes)? Do you want tube positions for everything, or only for cell lines and plasmids?
What do personal inventories look like today (per-person spreadsheets, paper box maps, notebooks, nothing)? Roughly how many items?
Does the institution already license LabArchives, SciNote, eLabNext/SciSure or Benchling, or run openBIS, eLabFTW or a campus EHS chemical inventory (MyChem, ChemTracker, SciShield)?
Any DEA-scheduled substances, select agents/toxins, or human-derived materials with consent or MTA restrictions?
Is an ELN or equipment booking also wanted (this would point to eLabFTW or NEMO as companions), or is inventory the only scope?
Will the PI mandate visibility and reasons for overriding duplicate warnings? Who will be the non-bioinformatician data steward when you move on?
Does the PI want per-person spend views or lab-level only? Should neighboring labs or the department be in scope later?
What country is the lab in? This affects Quartzy Shop, SDS Automation and mobile app availability.
Are AI features wanted, is sending label photos and SDS PDFs to the Anthropic API acceptable under institutional data policy, and who would pay for usage?
Realistically, how many hours per week can you commit, and can the second bioinformatician act as backup maintainer and reviewer?

critique.overall:
The synthesis is well researched and mostly accurate, but one part-time maintainer can't execute it as written. What holds up: the Quartzy API facts match the verified spec (create order requests, a PUT that changes status only, no comment endpoint, no approved/cancelled webhooks, per-user unscoped tokens). The AI claims I re-checked are also correct: Opus 5.5 is $4/$20 per MTok, Sonnet 5.5 is $2/$10, and Haiku 5.5 is $0.10/$0.50 for prompts up to 100K tokens. Opus 5.5 thinking can't be disabled and effort defaults to medium. Forced tool_choice returns a 400.

Six problems:

(1) Scope. The 'MVP' has 32 features, 11 of them rated M. My estimate is 250-700 focused hours, which is months at 10-15 h/week, not 4-6 weeks. Only about 10 of those features touch the PI's two complaints. Ship 'visibility + guard' first and physical stock second.

(2) Two inventories. The MVP builds receiving and put-away in the app on day one but postpones deciding which system holds physical stock. In Quartzy, 'Do Not Add To Inventory' is chosen per receipt, not set once for the lab (support article 233434167), so running both means double data entry and duplicate records. Quartzy's own Inventory module, which the lab already pays for, never gets a spike; InvenTree does.

(3) Bench premise. 'Scan first, gloves on' with personal phones conflicts with common BSL-2 rules. LCSB: 'Do not touch your badge, phone with your gloves'. USQ: gloves off before touching a mobile phone. iOS home-screen web apps also keep their cookies separate from Safari, so links opened from the camera land in a logged-out browser. Capture has to be designed around lab-owned stations and places where people take gloves off.

(4) Hidden assumptions. 'Alert the approver' needs data the API doesn't expose: there are no users, roles or approval rules. Polling 'newest pages' every 5 minutes assumes a sort order Quartzy doesn't document, and it misses status changes on older requests. Writing back with one admin token would show the token owner as the actor in Quartzy's history.

(5) Cheap levers left unused:
- clean up stale ORDERED requests before launch (they trigger Quartzy's warning and the app's)
- put everyone in one Quartzy Lab
- make the Add Request lookup mandatory (it does show 'Found in Inventory', contrary to the executive summary)
- route alerts to whoever actually places orders
- give members without Quartzy seats a way to request

(6) Data model:
- projected availability adds incompatible units
- vendor GTINs are treated as container IDs
- lots are keyed on the supplier SKU
- one status enum mixes three separate dimensions
- inheriting the owner from the location makes ownership ambiguous

Fix those, cut the MVP to visibility + guard, and add a claim-your-history checklist, shadow-mode matching, and email-in capture of non-Quartzy purchases. Then the plan becomes credible and directly answers the PI.

missing.item: Week-0 Quartzy cleanup and configuration (no code)
missing.why: Do this before any alert goes live. Bulk-receive or cancel ORDERED/BACKORDERED requests older than about 60 days; Lab Admins can act on any request before Received (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000426253). Confirm all 30 people request in ONE Quartzy Lab, because the native warning only checks the same Lab (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/115003458074). Make the Add Request lookup mandatory: it shows 'Found in Inventory' and 'Found in Request History' but can be skipped (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/233421407). Add an approval step for Types prone to duplicates. Stale open requests trigger Quartzy's warning indefinitely, and they will trigger the app's matcher too (it checks ORDERED/BACKORDERED), so skipping this guarantees false positives on day one.

missing.item: Diagnostic baseline: classify each past duplicate by why Quartzy missed it
missing.why:
Buckets:
- same catalog #, same Lab, open (Quartzy should have warned: was it ignored, or entered via Connect, mobile or Shop?)
- different Quartzy Labs
- catalog formatting or pack-size variant
- bought outside Quartzy
- received months earlier and still in someone's box
- equivalent product from another vendor
The mix decides what to build. Mostly 'received earlier' means invest in visibility and claims; mostly 'same week, same #' means fix policy and approvals. It also gives the comparison needed for an honest '$ avoided': don't credit the app for duplicates Quartzy's own rule already catches.

missing.item: Shadow mode and a labelled evaluation set before push alerts
missing.why: Run the matcher silently for 2-4 weeks. The lab manager marks each candidate true or false, and precision is computed per tier and item type. Turn on push alerts only for tiers above a bar (e.g. 85-90%). The synthesis tunes thresholds but never makes go-live depend on measured precision, even though it rates alert fatigue as a top risk.

missing.item: Approver and purchaser routing, which the API can't supply
missing.why: The spec has no endpoints for users, roles, approval teams, budget owners or approval rules. Its only paths are healthz, inventory-items, labs, order-requests, types, user and webhooks (https://docs.quartzy.com/redocusaurus/public-api.yaml). 'Alert the approver' therefore needs a mapping kept by hand (Type, budget or $ threshold to person) or a single named purchaser. Add a daily pre-order digest timed to when that person actually places orders; that is the real last cheap point to stop a duplicate.

missing.item: Request path for members without Quartzy seats
missing.why: The Academia plan includes 3 users and extra seats cost money (https://www.quartzy.com/pricing). If most of the 30 have no seat, the real flow is 'ask the lab manager'. Then 'Request in Quartzy' buttons go nowhere, requested_by is always the purchaser (so the baseline can't tell who needed what), and seat sharing falls under ToS §3.2(a) (https://www.quartzy.com/terms-of-service). Needed: an in-app 'request to purchaser' queue that runs the duplicate check first and records a requested_for field.

missing.item: Decide which system holds physical stock before put-away ships
missing.why:
Quartzy's receive dialog already creates or updates inventory with location, lot and expiry, and sets the requester as owner (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/4407114092315). 'Do Not Add To Inventory' is a per-receipt choice; no lab-wide setting is documented (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/233434167). Running both flows from day one guarantees double data entry and duplicate records. Pick one:
(a) Quartzy holds stock and the app reads its instances. The API has no owner field, so take Owner from Quartzy's emailed weekly inventory Excel backup (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/234448328).
(b) The app holds stock. Receivers choose 'Do Not Add' every time, and the app watches for inventory-item.created after receipts.

missing.item: A spike on Quartzy's own Inventory module, not just InvenTree
missing.why: The lab already pays for it. It has owners, 7 location levels, freezer boxes, instances, QBot and a mobile app, and the MVP mirror reads it anyway. Two or three bench users on one freezer for 2-3 days will show whether the custom app must hold physical stock, or can shrink to search, the duplicate guard and the biology-specific depth.

missing.item: Look-back windows per item type for 'already received'
missing.why: The matcher only checks receipts from the last 90 days. The classic personal-stash duplicate is an antibody, kit, enzyme or cell line received 6-24 months ago and never registered. Use windows per type (e.g. 24 months for durable reagents, none for consumables). Phrase the alert as a question: 'Priya received this 11 months ago. Still have it?'

missing.item: Suppression for recurring consumables
missing.why: Par levels are v1, so in the MVP every repeat order of gloves, tips or media matches the previous one. Suppress alerts for products bought N or more times a year unless two requests are open at the same time, or exclude Types such as General Supply.

missing.item: Alert suppression during backfill and bulk imports
missing.why: The first sync, and Quartzy's order-history Excel import (rows arrive as New or Ordered: https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/233421567), would fire hundreds of alerts. Alert only when requested_at is within a few hours of first_seen_at.

missing.item: Capture designed to fit biosafety rules
missing.why:
Many institutions forbid touching personal phones with gloves or using phones while working:
- LCSB: 'Do not touch your badge, phone with your gloves' (https://howto.lcsb.uni.lu/lab/gloves)
- USQ: gloves removed before touching the mobile phone (https://policy.usq.edu.au/documents/21175PL)
- BU: phones 'should not be practiced when working in the lab' (https://www.bu.edu/research/?p=950)
Plan for lab-owned wipeable stations with hands-free presentation scanners at the freezer banks and receiving. Allow personal phones only where gloves come off. Support logging after the fact: a list of recently scanned boxes and an end-of-day 'did you take these?' prompt. Check with the biosafety officer first.

missing.item: Reachability and dead zones
missing.why: If the app runs on a campus VM that phones on cellular can only reach over VPN (common where Wi-Fi drops), QR URLs won't open, so labels fail exactly where they are used. Provide a public HTTPS hostname behind SSO (or confirm Wi-Fi coverage) and wired stations at the freezer banks. Use the scanners' offline batch mode: Zebra scanners store scans when out of range and send them on reconnect (https://docs.zebra.com/us/en/scanners/general/ds4-series/ds4678-prg/c-param-desc-radio-communications/c-param-desc-general-radio-parameters/c-param-desc-batch-mode.html).

missing.item: Identity on shared stations
missing.why: Stations need fast user switching: a badge scan or name tap plus PIN, with auto-logout after about 2 minutes. Otherwise every action is credited to whoever logged in last, which defeats 'who took the last vial' and ownership.

missing.item: Physical disaster mode, not just database restore
missing.why:
A power or freezer failure can take down the campus VM at the same moment. Needed:
- a weekly emailed PDF of each freezer's box list, taped to the door
- a one-step 'move freezer X into Y' with temporary-location flags and a return checklist
- an offline CSV on the lab manager's laptop

missing.item: Rescue after ordering
missing.why: The design logs 'duplicate ordered' and stops there. Lab Admins can still cancel a request in any status before Received (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000426253), vendors often cancel before shipment, and an unopened duplicate found at receiving can be returned or offered to a neighbouring lab.

missing.item: Handling people who leave, in a way that works with SSO
missing.why:
'An account can't be closed until its items are transferred' can't be enforced once university SSO removes the person. Instead:
- trigger from end_date about 30 days ahead (rotation students, summer students)
- move orphaned items into the PI's lab pool automatically
- hand put-away for their still-open Quartzy requests to the purchaser

missing.item: Hardware budget, lead time and label tests
missing.why: '$0-25/month' leaves out one-time costs: label printer(s), cryo label stock and resin ribbon, 2D or presentation scanners, and 1-2 lab tablets. That is likely low four figures (my estimate), and university purchasing can take weeks. Existing frozen boxes can't follow 'apply labels at room temperature'. Frozen-surface label stock such as Brady FreezerBondz is sold for applying to pre-frozen surfaces (https://www.tequipment.net/Brady/M5-112-492/Printers-and-Printing-Supplies/). Run a one-week -80/LN2 adhesion test before buying in bulk.

missing.item: Least-privilege Quartzy credentials
missing.why: The read-only MVP doesn't need a Lab Admin token, because every Lab Member can see all requests and inventory in the Lab (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/4407114092315). Tokens have no scopes and no documented expiry or revocation. A leaked admin token could cancel, approve or mark as ordered anything in the lab.

missing.item: Notice about monitoring and data protection
missing.why: Per-person event logs, 'weekly active users' and 'who took the last vial' are data about people's behaviour. In Germany, software that is objectively capable of monitoring requires works or staff council co-determination (BetrVG §87(1) Nr. 6 as applied by the federal labour court: https://cms.law/de/deu/legal-updates/einfuehrung-von-ki-im-unternehmen-einbindung-des-betriebsrats), and GDPR applies across the EU. At minimum: publish a privacy notice, set a retention period, and keep per-person views visible to the PI only.

missing.item: A lab/tenant key on the app's own data
missing.why: Sharing with neighbouring labs and core facilities (v2) is cheap if Location, StockItem, Person and visibility carry a lab foreign key from the start, and a painful migration later.

priority_changes.feature: The whole MVP (32 features, 11 rated M)
priority_changes.to: MVP-A 'visibility + guard' (about 100-200 h), then MVP-B 'physical stock'
priority_changes.why:
My estimate for the MVP as listed is 250-700 focused hours. MVP-A covers both of the PI's complaints on its own:
- baseline notebook
- poller and mirror that refreshes open requests by id
- exact-key and same-base matching
- alerts plus a daily digest for the purchaser
- an in-flight list (Django admin is fine)
- one lab-wide search page over Quartzy history, Quartzy inventory and script-imported spreadsheets
- the claim-your-history checklist
- the PI's number

priority_changes.feature: URL-QR labels, mobile item/location pages, PDF label sheets and Brother QL printing
priority_changes.why: Not needed to stop duplicates, and they depend on decisions not yet made: hardware, network reachability, and capture that fits glove rules.

priority_changes.feature: RECEIVED->put-away task, self-reported arrival, big-button actions, Empty->reorder, StockEvent ledger, projected availability
priority_changes.to: MVP-B, shipped together after the system-of-record decision
priority_changes.why: This is the physical-inventory product. The ledger should start with the first stock edit. Until the decision is made, put-away duplicates Quartzy's receive dialog.

priority_changes.feature: Item types with 11 preset field schemas
priority_changes.to: v1 (MVP-A uses the Quartzy Type plus identity fields only)
priority_changes.why: Quartzy requests carry free-text names and no structured attributes, so type schemas and the conjugate/host/clone exclusion rules can't help MVP matching.

priority_changes.feature: Matcher tiers 3-4 (shared identifiers, fuzzy names) as alert triggers
priority_changes.to: Search-only in MVP. Alert only on an exact key, same base with a different pack, or the same key across vendors; allow fuzzy alerts only after shadow mode has measured precision
priority_changes.why: No identifiers exist until enrichment (v1), and fuzzy name matches are where false positives come from.

priority_changes.feature: Spreadsheet import wizard with dedupe-preview UI
priority_changes.to: MVP: pandas scripts run by the bioinformatician, plus django-import-export in the admin; build the wizard in v1 only if people keep importing on their own
priority_changes.why: About 30 one-off files in different layouts, many of them box grids, are faster to script than a general-purpose wizard is to build.

priority_changes.to: MVP: the lab's one chat tool plus an email digest
priority_changes.why: Three adapters triple the testing for no extra reach.

priority_changes.feature: Amnesty leaderboard and the 'This is annoying' button
priority_changes.to: No code at first (a manual tally, a chat channel or a form link); build later if they get used
priority_changes.why: Little value per hour of code at this stage.

priority_changes.to: MVP, plus a one-time cleanup in week 0
priority_changes.why: Stale ORDERED requests pollute both Quartzy's warning and the app's matcher from day one.

priority_changes.feature: Write-back to Quartzy (PUT status from the approver console)
priority_changes.to: v2, only if conditions are met; the v1 approver console is read-only with deep links
priority_changes.why: Quartzy's request history records who changed each status (support article 115000746334), so every app action would appear as the token owner. Whether PUT respects approval steps is undocumented.

priority_changes.to: v2 only if Quartzy issues an OAuth client; otherwise drop it, except a purchaser-only POST for members without seats
priority_changes.why: Per-user tokens have no scopes, budget and custom fields can't be set, and the request body rejects extra fields (additionalProperties: false).

priority_changes.to: Optional; run a Quartzy Inventory spike first
priority_changes.why: The tool the lab already pays for is the realistic alternative, and the synthesis already prefers a custom build over InvenTree.

priority_changes.to: MVP-B minimal version (orphan queue plus end_date trigger)
priority_changes.why: Owners are created during amnesty week, and rotations orphan those items within weeks.

priority_changes.to: MVP-A if the baseline shows meaningful spend outside Quartzy, built as email-in or a 30-second form
priority_changes.why: Those purchases are invisible to the duplicate guard.
Polling that refreshes open requests by id gives a few minutes' latency, which is enough for 30 people. Webhooks need inbound HTTPS, and the signature format is unverified.

priority_changes.to: v1 as cycle counting: the Monday digest assigns 2 random boxes per freezer each week
priority_changes.why: Small, continuous checks keep the data trusted without a dreaded quarterly event that gets skipped.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.claim: Executive summary: 'Quartzy's own check ... matches only an identical catalog #, only within the same lab, only against open requests, and never looks at inventory.'
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: Overstated. Quartzy's Add Request lookup shows 'Found in Inventory' and 'Found in Request History' for the current lab, although users can skip it (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/233421407). The duplicate-warning article says nothing about how catalog numbers are normalized, and the verification marked 'exact catalog #' as unverifiable.
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: Rephrase: the duplicate warning matches on catalog # (normalization unknown) against same-lab requests that are New, Approved, Ordered or Backordered. The lookup shows same-lab inventory and history but can be skipped or bypassed (Connect). Make 'use the lookup' a lab rule.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: Nothing supports this. The modules list 32 MVP features, 11 rated M, which I estimate at 250-700 focused hours. The adoption timeline (amnesty week in weeks 5-6) inherits the same error.
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: Estimate each feature, cut to MVP-A, and move amnesty week to after the import path and claim checklist exist.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: This assumes newest-first ordering, but sort order and page size are undocumented. Polling only the newest pages also misses status changes (APPROVED/CANCELLED) on older requests until the nightly full scan, so the in-flight board can be about a day out of date.
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: Each cycle, re-fetch GET /order-requests/{id} for every request the app holds as open, find new ids by probing pages, and measure the ordering in week 1.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.claim: 'alert the requester and approver within minutes'
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: The API can't tell you who the approver is. There are no endpoints for users, roles, approval teams, budget owners or approval rules (https://docs.quartzy.com/redocusaurus/public-api.yaml).
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: Keep an approver/purchaser mapping in the app (or one named purchaser) and add a daily pre-order digest.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: An inference, and beside the point when requests are auto-approved below a threshold or the lab has no approval flow, where New goes straight to Ordered (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/4411829390875).
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: Set the target as 'before the purchaser's next ordering batch' and measure it.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.claim: 'Approval is the last cheap point ... Once a request is Ordered, Quartzy cannot revert it.'
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: 'Revert' isn't the same as 'cancel'. Lab Admins can cancel a request in any status before Received (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000426253), and vendors often cancel orders or accept returns.
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: Add a post-order rescue path, and keep approval as the main point of interception.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.claim: 'Lab policy choice: either set Quartzy receiving to Do Not Add To Inventory after launch...'
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: This is an option chosen in the receive dialog for each receipt; no lab-wide setting is documented (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/233434167). It works only if every receiver remembers it every time.
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: Treat it as training plus monitoring (flag inventory-item.created after receipts), and decide where physical stock lives before put-away ships.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: The help centre says automatic requests appear in the New tab 'by QBot' (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/38547448619547). How QBot shows up in the API's created_by and requested_by fields is unverified.
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: Check with a test item in a sandbox lab before building suppression logic.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.claim: 'Write-back ... PUT /order-requests/{id} status (CANCELLED/APPROVED/RECEIVED) from the approver console' using a Lab Admin token
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: Quartzy's request history records who changed each status (support article 115000746334, cited in the verification), so app actions would be credited to the token owner. Whether PUT respects approval steps or budget-owner rules is undocumented, so the app could become a way around approval.
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: Stay read-only and deep-link to Quartzy for approvals and cancellations, unless Quartzy confirms per-user OAuth and that the API enforces approvals.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.claim: 'Requests are attributed through per-user tokens or Quartzy's declared OAuth2 flow'
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: OAuth2 is declared in the spec, but how to register a client is undocumented. Per-user tokens have no scopes and no documented expiry or revocation, so collecting about 30 of them creates a valuable store of credentials.
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: Make in-app request creation v2, and only if Quartzy provides an OAuth client.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.claim: '(1) Auth: an Access-Token header from a Lab Admin's account' for the read-only MVP
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: More privilege than needed. Every lab member can see the lab's requests and inventory (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/4407114092315), while an unscoped admin token can cancel or approve anything.
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: Use a Lab Member token for reads, and use admin rights only for one-time setup in the Quartzy UI.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.claim: 'Scan first, gloves on' with personal phones, and 'Any phone camera opens a big-button page'
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: This conflicts with common biosafety rules. LCSB says 'Do not touch your badge, phone with your gloves' (https://howto.lcsb.uni.lu/lab/gloves); USQ requires removing gloves before touching a mobile phone (https://policy.usq.edu.au/documents/21175PL); BU discourages phone use while working (https://www.bu.edu/research/?p=950). On iOS, home-screen web apps keep cookies and storage separate from Safari (https://wwdcnotes.com/documentation/wwdc23-10120-whats-new-in-web-apps/), so being logged in to the installed app doesn't carry over to links opened from the camera. That last part is my inference; test it.
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: Design capture around lab-owned stations and places where gloves come off, and make Safari the main entry point on iOS.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.claim: 'Quartzy (2026) and LabCollector had to migrate to this model'
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: The research shows only that LabCollector gives each lot its own ID, not that it migrated.
True for hosting only. It leaves out one-time hardware and consumables (label printers, cryo labels and ribbons, scanners, tablets) and AI usage.
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: Add a line for one-time hardware costs and one for AI usage based on the eval.

unsupported_or_wrong_claims.claim: AI gotcha: 'check stop_reason and enable server-side fallbacks', presented as general advice across Opus, Sonnet and Haiku 5.5
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.issue: Right for Opus 5.5, whose 'bio' safety classifier is confirmed. But Claude Haiku 5.5 has no server-side fallback for refusals, and its $0.10/$0.50 price applies only to prompts up to 100K tokens ($0.50/$2.50 above that). The other AI figures check out: Opus 5.5 $4/$20, Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, Opus 5.5 thinking can't be disabled and effort defaults to medium, and forced tool_choice returns a 400.
unsupported_or_wrong_claims.fix: If the eval picks Haiku 5.5, retry refusals on another model from the client side.

friction_risks.point: Touching personal phones with gloves on, which many BSL-2 manuals forbid (LCSB, USQ, BU).
friction_risks.mitigation: Put lab-owned wipeable tablets with hands-free presentation scanners at the freezer banks and receiving. Allow personal phones only where gloves come off. Let people log afterwards: box scans build a 'recently touched' list, and an end-of-day prompt asks 'did you take these?'

friction_risks.point: Holding the freezer door open to scan, and handling LN2 vials.
friction_risks.mitigation: Plan the pick on screen (box and position) before opening. Pull the box, close the door, scan the box label at the station, then tap the vial. Never scan individual vials inside a -80 or a dewar.

friction_risks.point: Frosted, unreadable labels, and existing frozen vials that can't be relabelled.
friction_risks.mitigation: Scan room-temperature labels on the side of the box and pick the vial from the box list. Put frozen-surface label stock on existing boxes. As a fallback, accept a short ID typed on a numeric keypad (use an unambiguous Crockford-style alphabet if it has to include letters).

friction_risks.point: On iOS, a QR scanned with the camera opens in Safari, but the user is logged in only inside the home-screen app, which has its own cookies and storage (WWDC23).
friction_risks.mitigation: Make Safari the main way in on iOS, with long sessions and SSO or passkeys, and don't push a home-screen install. Test the camera-to-Safari path on the lab's own phones.

friction_risks.point: No Wi-Fi in cold rooms, and the campus VM is VPN-only from cellular.
friction_risks.mitigation: Use a public HTTPS hostname behind SSO, wired stations, and scanner batch mode for dead zones. Do the Wi-Fi survey before printing a single QR code.

friction_risks.point: Two receiving dialogs: Quartzy's 'add to inventory', then the app's put-away task.
friction_risks.mitigation: Keep stock in one system. If the app holds stock, train receivers to choose 'Do Not Add To Inventory' and flag any inventory-item.created that follows a receipt. If Quartzy holds it, read the location from the Quartzy instance and drop the app's task.

friction_risks.point: Put-away assigned to the requester while a dry-ice box sits on the bench.
friction_risks.mitigation: Whoever opens the box takes the put-away at the receiving station, and the requester gets a message like 'your item is in Freezer 2 / Box 4'. Flag perishables from their Type or storage temperature.

friction_risks.point: The duplicate alert arrives after submission, and members can cancel only their own requests while they are still New.
friction_risks.mitigation: Send high-confidence alerts to the purchaser or admin who can cancel. Give the requester a one-tap 'ask purchaser to cancel' message that includes app_url, and add a daily pre-order digest.

friction_risks.point: Noise from fuzzy name matches and repeat orders of consumables.
friction_risks.mitigation: Use shadow mode, gate alerts by tier, suppress recurring items, and offer a one-tap 'not a duplicate' that silences that pair for good.

friction_risks.point: Amnesty week asks 30 people to type or upload their inventories.
friction_risks.mitigation: Use the claim-your-history checklist (taps, no typing), track at box level only, run 30-minute sessions led by champions, and have the bioinformatician script the imports. Photo intake can come later.

friction_risks.point: On shared stations, every action is credited to the last person who logged in.
friction_risks.mitigation: Badge scan or name tap plus PIN, with auto-logout after 2 minutes. Low-risk events (used some, moved) need no re-login.

friction_risks.point: Members without Quartzy seats hit 'Request in Quartzy' links that go nowhere.
friction_risks.mitigation: Add an in-app 'request to purchaser' that runs the duplicate check first.

friction_risks.point: Emailed login codes on phones at the bench.
friction_risks.mitigation: After the first login, use SSO or passkeys and 90-day sessions on personal devices. Stations should never need email.

friction_risks.point: The quarterly stocktake becomes a dreaded event that gets skipped.
friction_risks.mitigation: Cycle counting: the Monday digest assigns 2 random boxes per freezer, and batch-mode scanners make each check take about 2 minutes.

standout_ideas.idea: Claim-your-history checklist (migration in reverse). Each person gets a list of durable items they requested or received in the last 24 months (from Quartzy history) that aren't registered. One tap each: Still have it (which box?) / Used up / Gave to X / Not mine. Repeat monthly for new receipts.
standout_ideas.value: Brings hidden personal stock into view with taps instead of typing and creates owner + product records immediately. It goes straight at the PI's complaint about personal inventories.

standout_ideas.idea: 'Ask the lab' fallback. When search finds nothing, one tap posts 'Does anyone have X?' to the lab channel. An 'I have it' reply creates a pending record for that person to confirm.
standout_ideas.value: At launch most stock is unregistered. This catches it and turns each answer into a registration.

standout_ideas.idea: Shadow-mode matcher. For two to four weeks matches are found silently, the lab manager labels each candidate, and precision per tier and item type is published before alerts go live.
standout_ideas.value: Earns trust from day one and gives evidence for the thresholds and for the PI.

standout_ideas.idea: Email-in for purchases outside Quartzy. A mailbox where people forward (or auto-forward) vendor order and shipping confirmations. Claude, using structured outputs, extracts vendor, catalog #, quantity and price into a purchase-outside-Quartzy record that a person confirms.
standout_ideas.value: Closes the blind spot for P-card, direct and core-facility orders without any forms.

standout_ideas.idea: Shared pools proposed from the data. The analyzer flags products bought at least twice a year by at least two people and proposes a lab-shared stock with a named steward, a par level and a kanban card.
standout_ideas.value: Fixes repeat duplicates at the source instead of catching them one at a time.

standout_ideas.idea: Freezer-bank station: a wall-mounted lab tablet, a hands-free presentation scanner and badge login. Scan the box, tap the vial, done.
standout_ideas.value: Fits glove rules, is fast, and records who did what. Removes the need for personal phones and Wi-Fi at the freezer.

standout_ideas.idea: NFC stickers on freezer doors, racks and shelves. iPhone background tag reading offers to open the URL in Safari after a tap on the notification (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corenfc/adding-support-for-background-tag-reading).
standout_ideas.value: Gives location context without aiming a camera at a frosty label. Works best on lab-owned station devices.

standout_ideas.idea: Door sheets and emergency mode. A weekly auto-generated PDF lists each freezer's boxes and owners. One action moves freezer X into freezer Y with temporary locations, a 'return when fixed' checklist and notices to owners.
standout_ideas.value: Turns the worst day in a lab into a routine, even when the server is down.

standout_ideas.idea: Post-order rescue. A duplicate found after ORDERED alerts the purchaser while the order can still be cancelled. At receiving, an unopened duplicate prompts a return or an offer to neighbouring labs.
standout_ideas.value: Recovers money that the current design writes off as 'duplicate ordered'.

standout_ideas.idea: Departure 'estate sale'. Thirty days before a member's end date, their items are posted to the lab with claim buttons. Unclaimed items go to the PI's pool or the discard queue.
standout_ideas.value: Prevents mystery boxes and turns turnover into redistribution.

standout_ideas.idea: Sequence-level checks on oligo and gene order pages (IDT, Twist). The browser extension reads pasted sequences and checks the lab's oligo and plasmid registry for exact, reverse-complement and near matches.
standout_ideas.value: Uses the bioinformatician's core skill. Catches re-ordered primers and gene fragments that name matching misses.

standout_ideas.idea: Batch-mode stocktake in dead zones. Scan box labels with no signal; Zebra-class scanners store the scans and send them when back in range, and the app reconciles them against expected contents.
standout_ideas.value: Handles dead zones without building the large offline web app.

standout_ideas.idea: Hands-free voice logging. 'Hey Siri, log: took the last HeLa P12 vial from box 4.' A Shortcut posts the text, an LLM proposes the event, and the person confirms it later at a station.
standout_ideas.value: Logging without touching a phone with gloves on. Experimental: noisy rooms and accuracy are open questions.

data_model_issues: Projected availability adds incompatible units. Quartzy's quantity is a whole number of purchase units and unit_size is free text ('500 mL', '10 x 500 mL'). StockItem.quantity is an amount with a unit, or empty for status-only items. Requested and on-order figures come from Quartzy, while in-stock comes from the app. Use pack-equivalents (count of unopened and opened containers) as the common unit. Add SupplierProduct.containers_per_pack and amount_per_container, parse unit_size, and keep amounts as optional detail. Gibco shows why pack size has to be explicit: 11965092 is 1 x 500 mL, 11965084 is 1 x 1000 mL, and 11965118 is 10 x 500 mL (https://www.fishersci.com/shop/products/dmem/11965084, https://thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/jp/ja/11965118).

Catalog numbers are normalized before they are parsed. catalog_key strips separators before catalog_base is worked out, which throws away the delimiter the per-vendor pack rules rely on. Parse vendor rules on the raw string first (for Gibco, the last 3 digits are the pack), then normalize. The first matching tier also shouldn't depend on resolving a vendor family from Quartzy's free-text vendor_name. Instead, match catalog_key across vendors when it has 7 or more characters, and treat agreeing vendors as extra confidence. Fisher US lists Gibco 11965092 as 11-965-092, which normalizes to the same key.

Lot is unique on (supplier_product, lot_number), but one manufacturing lot is sold in several pack sizes and through distributors. Key lots on (product or the manufacturer's catalog base, lot_number) so a re-validation alert for a new lot fires once.

external_barcodes[] mixes codes that identify one container (lab labels, pre-barcoded 2D tubes, GS1 codes with an AI 21 serial) with codes that describe a product (a GTIN, or GTIN plus lot, is the same on every bottle in a lot). The planned duplicate-barcode check would reject the second bottle, and scanning a vendor code is ambiguous. Split them into unique container identifiers and non-unique product/lot codes; scanning a product/lot code opens a picker.

StockItem.status mixes three separate things: lifecycle (available, opened, empty, discarded, lost), holds (reserved, quarantined, checked out) and stock level (low). A vial can be opened, reserved and low all at once. Split these into a lifecycle_state, hold records with an expiry, and a level indicator.

Ownership is ambiguous. Location.owner says contents inherit the owner, but StockItem also has its own owner_id, so moving a tube into a shared box can quietly change who owns it. Store a custodian on the item itself (call it custodian rather than owner, since purchases are lab or grant property), use the location's owner only as the default at put-away, and record owner_transfer events.

The same bottle can exist twice, as a mirrored Quartzy instance and as an app StockItem, which doubles search hits and counts. Store mirrored instances as StockItems with source='quartzy' and a unique quartzy_instance_id, and have put-away claim them instead of creating new ones.

Self-reported arrivals are counted twice: stock shelved while Quartzy still says ORDERED appears in both in-stock and on-order. Subtract shelved quantity linked by source_order_request_id from on-order.

Positions are row/column only. LN2 canes and numbered rack slots are linear, and some boxes are labelled 1-81. Put a position scheme on LocationType (grid, linear or none) and store each position as a label plus a sequence number.

Matching an OrderRequest to a Product needs an 'unresolved' state and a queue for a person to review. Merging automatically on fuzzy names ('never a new duplicate record') creates wrong merges that then cause false alerts. Merges also need redirect records so links in old alerts still work.

Mapping people by email breaks with email aliases and former members, and requested_by is the purchaser for members without seats. Add a PersonAlias table (emails, Quartzy user IDs) and a requested_for field so the baseline and alerts reach the person who actually needs the item.

OrderStatusObservation is only as fine-grained as the polling. With nightly full scans, approval and cancellation times can be up to a day late, which skews lead-time and time-to-cancel metrics. Record how late each observation is, and refresh open requests by id.

DuplicateCheck has no 'would Quartzy have caught it' field. Store whether Quartzy's own rule would have fired (same catalog #, same Lab, open status) so '$ avoided' leaves out duplicates Quartzy already flags.

A single EquivalenceGroup foreign key assumes substitution is universal and transitive. In practice it is limited: an FBS lot may be qualified for cell line X only, and an antibody may be equivalent for Western blot but not immunofluorescence. Use many-to-many substitute links that carry a scope.
The app's own tables have no lab/tenant key, so the planned sharing with neighbouring labs would mean a migration. Add a lab foreign key now.

'Existence and owner always visible' needs visibility rules per field. DEA-scheduled or select-agent items shouldn't broadcast their location to 30 people. Restricted items should be able to hide their location while still showing that they exist and whom to ask.

research.summary:
I surveyed all 13 required platforms (Quartzy, Benchling, eLabNext/SciSure, LabArchives Inventory, Labguru/Cenevo, LabCollector, SciNote, Labstep/STARLIMS, Genemod, Scispot, CloudLIMS, Freezerworks, ChemInventory) and six newer or adjacent players (RSpace Inventory, Labviva, Labii, Sapio Elain, Colabra, ZAGENO). Most of the material came from vendor docs, API references, changelogs and pricing pages.

The commercial tools agree on a core design:
- **Data model:** a product or definition record, with separate physical instances (lot, expiry, quantity, location, owner) underneath it.
- **Storage:** a location tree of any depth, ending in box grids you can see.
- **Barcodes:** a unique barcode on every object, printed with ZPL, BarTender or DYMO templates.
- **Ordering:** request, approve, order, receive, where receiving creates or tops up inventory.
- **Alerts:** low-stock thresholds and expiry windows.

How they stop duplicate orders is usually simple. Labguru, Genemod, eLabNext and LabArchives use one shared request queue or shopping list. Quartzy shows matches from your request history and current inventory while you type a new request. ChemInventory shows items already on order in the same search as items in stock. None of them documents fuzzy matching across vendors, which is a gap a custom app could fill.

For this lab, Quartzy's public API and webhooks are the key facts. The API can list, create and update the status of order requests, and it can update inventory quantities. It cannot create inventory items or locations. Webhooks use the CloudEvents format, are signed with HMAC-SHA256, and retry 3 times. The 'received' webhook does not link to the inventory item it creates. So the realistic setup is: Quartzy stays the purchasing system, and the custom app becomes the physical-inventory system and the duplicate check, kept in sync by webhooks.

Benchling's free academic plan does not include Inventory or Registry. LabArchives Inventory, at $99 per user per year for academics, is the cheapest full-featured product to compare a custom build against.

Bench-friendliness is weak across the market. Quartzy's iOS app is rated 3.2/5 with crash and slow-scan complaints, and reviews of Labguru and Quartzy complain about too many clicks and the effort of logging every use. AI work in 2024-2026 is mostly MCP servers (Scispot in private beta, SciSure, Benchling connectors), agents that act only after a human signs off (Scispot, Genemod), and converting documents into structured records (Benchling, SciNote). Very little AI is aimed at inventory itself.

Limits of this research: the shared WebSearch budget ran out partway through. G2, Capterra, GetApp, several Zendesk help centers and Reddit blocked direct fetches. User sentiment therefore comes from search-result excerpts and app-store listings, and I could not survey r/labrats directly.

products.name: Quartzy
products.license_or_pricing: The pricing page lists Academia at $50/month billed annually for up to 3 users, Industry at $250/month (5 users), and custom Enterprise. The homepage separately says it is free for labs with 3 or fewer members, which conflicts. Paid add-ons: automated SDS collection, PO generation, 3-way invoice matching, PunchOuts, Benchling integration, custom SAML/OIDC, procurement services.
products.activity: Very active. API changelog entries on 2024-12-19, 2026-06-17 and 2026-07-01 (inventory item instances). iOS app at v1.8.x.
products.stack: SaaS. REST API at https://api.quartzy.com with an Access-Token header. Webhooks use CloudEvents 1.0.
strengths: The whole purchasing loop sits in one place: request, approval, PO, receipt, invoice, plus the Quartzy Shop (20M+ products, Quartzy as distributor of record)

Public REST API: GET/POST /order-requests, PUT /order-requests/{id} to change status (CREATED, CANCELLED, APPROVED, ORDERED, BACKORDERED, RECEIVED), GET /inventory-items, PUT /inventory-items/{itemId}/instances/{instanceId}
Signed webhooks: HMAC-SHA256 in a Signature header, CloudEvents envelope, 3 retries at 10 s, 100 s and 1000 s, 3-second timeout
Item instances (2026): one item can hold several quantities, lots, expiry dates and locations, with up to 7 location levels stored as pathNames
Mobile app: scan to add or remove stock, create a request when stock is low, scan packing slips to receive, capture lot/expiry/CAS on receipt (v1.8.4)
Interactive freezer boxes, SDS automation, Excel and FileMaker import, freezer-box import from Excel

Approval rules by budget, site, project, grant or dollar threshold. Spend tracking codes. Slack and Microsoft Teams integration. PunchOut via cXML/OCI to SAP Ariba, Coupa and Jaggaer. Ordering from inside Benchling and SciNote
G2 rating 4.3/5 from 93 reviews. Reviewers praise ease of use and support
weaknesses: The inventory API cannot create items, locations or sublocations. It only lists, gets and updates quantity, so an outside app cannot write inventory records into Quartzy
List endpoints filter only by page and lab_id. No search, date or status filters are documented
The order-request.received webhook payload has no received quantity, location or link to an inventory item
The documented POST /order-requests body has no requested_by field, so requests created through one service token would probably be attributed to the token owner (my inference)

iOS app rated 3.2/5 from 17 ratings. Reviews mention freezes ('crashes CONSTANTLY') and a scanner that 'takes forever to read barcodes'. App Store availability is US and Canada only; Google Play is US only

Review complaints: logging every use is 'less realistic in academic labs', importing inventory was not easy, multiple search boxes in odd places, and users want a condensed ledger and a dashboard of active orders and low stock
IntuitionLabs reports the inventory audit trail only started recording in March 2024. Legacy labs had only 2 location levels and had to migrate to instances
standout_features: The Add Request search groups matches into Request History, Quartzy Shop and Inventory ('Found in Inventory')
A help-center article titled 'Duplicate request notification' (I could not read its contents)
Scanning the barcode of a low-stock item creates a request immediately
'Amount Adding To Stock' on receipt adds to the current level instead of overwriting it
products.fit_notes: The lab already buys through Quartzy, so treat it as the purchasing system and integrate rather than replace it. The API's write limits mean the custom app must own physical inventory (locations, boxes, aliquots, owners) and sync order requests in through webhooks plus periodic polling. Check whether the lab's plan includes API and webhook access; the docs do not say which tier does.

products.name: Benchling (Inventory + Registry)
products.license_or_pricing: The free academic plan includes only Notebook and Molecular Biology. Inventory and Registry are excluded ('built for industry requirements, not academic'). Competitor Scispot reports Professional at about $20k/year with a 5-user minimum; I could not verify this.
products.activity: Very active. May 2026 launches: One-Click Ordering (Twist, Adaptyv, Ginkgo), Benchling Biologics, and a Data Analysis skill for Benchling AI.
products.stack: SaaS. REST API v2 (stable) and v3 (early access). Python SDK. Container transfers run as async tasks.
strengths: Separates the registered entity (what a thing is) from the container (where it is and how much is left)
Location schemas (building, room, freezer, rack, shelf) with barcode prefixes such as FRZ001. Every box, container and location has a barcode that is unique across the registry
Box schemas with fixed grids (for example 10x10), one container per position
Label printing for boxes, plates, containers and entities, using ZPL or BarTender templates
Check-out with an Assignee and optional comment, plus reservations for future use. Check-in/out is audit-logged and can trigger availability notifications
Sample owners and 'restricted sample parties' on containers. Apps must be designated as restricted parties before they can write

Transfers API: POST /api/v3/container:transfer subtracts transferQuantity from the source container, recalculates concentration and supports a finalQuantity dilution. You poll the task until it finishes
Registry uniqueness rules on sequence or structure, and parent-child lineage for batches and aliquots
Benchling AI: Notebook Check, SQL Writer, Q&A across data, PDF/CRO-report import as structured data, MCP connectors to Teams, SharePoint and Slack
weaknesses: Inventory is not available to academic labs on the free plan
The 2019 check-out/reservation feature had to be switched on by support
No mobile app is mentioned. Scanning relies on connected scanners
Schema configuration is heavy and industry-oriented. Benchling itself says academic labs 'often change data formats'
standout_features: Barcode prefixes defined per location schema
Restricted sample parties and sample owners
Async transfer API that tracks concentration
products.fit_notes: A reference design to copy, not a realistic purchase for this lab, because Inventory is excluded from the academic plan.

products.name: eLabNext / eLabInventory (now SciSure Research)
products.license_or_pricing: Prices are not published. Data points: academic list price of $13.80/account/month (LIMSwiki, about 2021); UNMC institutional license at $115-120/user/year; an EU directory lists from EUR 12.95/user/month; G2 shows an 'Academic $0' tier whose meaning is unclear.
products.activity: eLabNext merged with SciShield in January 2025 to form SciSure, which acquired LabFolder in September 2025. Releases V2.75.0 (Nov 2025, bulk quantity updates), V2.76.0 (Dec 2025, bulk compartment selection and sorted label printing), V2.87.0 (2026, grid/list views for storage units).
products.stack: SaaS, private cloud or on-premises. REST API v1 (for example GET /api/v1/sampleTypes and /sampleTypes/{id}/meta). eLabSDK2 add-ons. Marketplace.
strengths: Storage units for freezers, LN2, safety cabinets, cold rooms and custom structures, with compartments, racks and boxes
Sample types with custom meta fields (RADIO, COMBO and CHECKBOX defaults), and sample series that support bulk actions
Drag-and-drop of several samples within a box. Multi-location placement when a batch is larger than the free space in a box
Full location path shown in lists. Custom column views that can be shared. Export to PDF, Excel or CSV. Import of up to 400 samples
Change-owner action, a required reason when archiving, Assignments for storage units and Bookings for equipment
Supplies module with shared shopping lists and low-stock alerts. Chronological audit log positioned for 21 CFR Part 11
eLABInventory mobile app: scan 2D/1D barcodes, move or archive, check in/out (since v3.4, 2023), update quantity
Marketplace add-ons: FLUICS Print cloud cryo labels, DYMO LabelWriter 550, Thermo VisionMate HSX reader, Elemental Machines monitoring
SciSure MCP server at https://<instance>/api/v1/mcp with OAuth 2.1, for ChatGPT, Claude, LM Studio and Open WebUI
weaknesses: The MCP server is only available on Private Cloud and On-Premises installs, not the shared cloud
Expiry email notifications, multiple parents per sample and cross-group sample sharing were listed as planned, not released, in the new-inventory blog post
The mobile app has a single rating, and release notes show repeated fixes for setting sample quantity
Merger and rebranding churn. No Quartzy or punchout integration found
products.fit_notes: A strong freezer and sample model to copy. Ordering is less developed than Quartzy's.

products.name: LabArchives Inventory
products.license_or_pricing: $99/user/year academic ($199 corporate). ELN+Inventory bundle at $360/user/year academic, which adds automatic inventory debiting from the notebook. 90-day free trial. Developer API and SAML SSO are listed only for ELN Enterprise.
products.activity: Active. Its only AI is Proofig image-integrity screening, through a partner integration.
strengths: Default Lab Manager and Lab Member roles, custom roles, and order-management privileges
Reorder from the inventory list or an item page. Requests go Approve/Cancel, then Ordered, then 'Mark Received', which creates the inventory item, with an option 'I will add this item to inventory'
Requesters can opt in to emails when a request is approved, cancelled, ordered or received
Approved orders can be exported as a shopping list for the institution's procurement system
Reports: expiration (30/60/90 days), low quantity, orders summary, freezer box capacity, most-used categories
Freezer box view, aliquots created in batches, parent/child lineage
Scan barcodes or QR codes with the in-app Camera button or a phone camera. Bulk upload from spreadsheets and bulk updates. Links to ELN entries
weaknesses: Purchasing happens outside the tool, in institutional systems
API and SSO need Enterprise
No native mobile app documented
The integrations page lists no vendor, Quartzy or Slack/Teams connections
products.fit_notes: Cost benchmark: about $2,970/year for 30 users on Inventory alone. Check whether the university already has a LabArchives site license.

products.name: Labguru (Cenevo / BioData)
products.license_or_pricing: Quote-based. Competitor Scispot estimates $1,000-1,500/user/year for ELN plus inventory (unverified).
products.activity: Active. Labguru Assistant launched April 3, 2024. The help center has moved to labguru-support.cenevo.com.
products.stack: SaaS. REST API at https://my.labguru.com/api/v1 with a token parameter.
strengths: Customizable collections with predefined or custom fields
Storage from rooms down to tubes. Boxes have a configurable rows-by-columns grid, a name and a barcode
Label Wizard prints 1D/2D labels. The mobile app scans and prints labels on demand
'Mark as consumed' for used-up stocks. A third-party API mirror lists POST /api/v1/stocks/{id}/mark_as_consumed
Notifications for low stock and expiry

Shopping list: a central queue meant to avoid duplicate orders, a 'Can approve orders' permission, budgets, CSV export or PDF purchase orders per vendor, and 'mark as arrived' that records where the item was put and emails the person who ordered it
Avantor VWR access with on-demand replenishment
Labguru Assistant runs on every page: natural-language retrieval across modules, plus protocol and troubleshooting help
weaknesses: G2 complaints (4.6/5 from 164 reviews): speed, bulk actions, limited tables, and uptake hurt by 'software that requires a lot of clicking'
Pricing is opaque
The Assistant's availability depends on account configuration
standout_features: Central shopping list with an approval permission
Arrival recorded with storage location and an email to the requester
products.fit_notes: Shows that a central request queue alone does not stop duplicates; the queue has to be visible at the moment someone decides to order.

products.name: LabCollector (AgileBio)
products.license_or_pricing: G2 (May 2025): Inventory Pack from $500/user/year, LIMS/LIS from $1,250, ELN from $900. Sold in packs of 5 users. Perpetual on-premises license or annual SaaS. Add-ons have a fixed price regardless of user count.
strengths: Reagents, Chemicals & Supplies module: each lot has its own ID, barcode (for example 67/LT) and available quantity
Alerts under Admin > Preferences > Alerts: a days-before-expiry threshold, and a quantity threshold that can 'Use the SUM of all lots'
Storage browser (facility, equipment, rack or drawer, box), box map viewer, custom box templates, box finder, and Autofill to create racks and boxes
Purchase Order Manager: automatic batch creation on receipt, partial deliveries, PO form templates, alerts for minimum quantities
Central Store Android app for orders, Equipment Scheduler, graphical workflow designer
weaknesses: Capterra 4.2 from 24 reviews: 'the box system is sometimes hard to use', 'not so easy to find empty spaces', notebook not optimized
The UI is described as cluttered or outdated when many modules are enabled
Migrating from an existing database needed substantial vendor help
standout_features: Low-stock threshold summed across all lots
products.fit_notes: Good ideas for alerts and lots. Its UX complaints are what to avoid.

products.name: SciNote
products.license_or_pricing: Free plan for individuals, without collaboration. Premium is quote-based. Storage Locations, Stock Management and Item Relationships are paid inventory add-ons that customer success must enable (30-day trial).
products.activity: Very active, with 2025 releases from CORE 1.39 to 1.45.2. First AI feature: Import with AI (Beta) on Oct 1, 2025.
products.stack: SaaS with an API. There is an unofficial Python client, scinote-client.
strengths: Stock column with Set, Add and Remove, a preview of the new total, units locked when adding or subtracting, and low-stock reminders
A Consume button on a task's assigned items deducts stock. Consumption exports to CSV with the user, date, task and stock balance after each update
Prebuilt templates (May 2025): Default, Cell Lines, Equipment, Chemicals & Reagents
Inventory access management (Aug 2025): Viewer, User and Owner per inventory. Items you cannot access show as private. Access changes are logged
Storage boxes: select several positions or a whole row or column, and 'Find item' shows every location holding an item (Mar 2025)
Inventory items can be created from a task and marked as outputs. Parent/child item relationships
A 203 dpi ZPL label template. API endpoint for assigning items to tasks, with access enforced
weaknesses: Core inventory features are add-ons
The docs disagree about which plan includes barcodes (Advanced vs Professional)
The mobile app is limited (mostly fixes in release notes)
IntuitionLabs reports a Premium export limit of 5 requests per user per day
standout_features: Consumption ledger with balance after each event
products.fit_notes: Good patterns for stock ledgers and permissions.

products.name: Labstep (STARLIMS)
products.license_or_pricing: Three industry editions (Pro and Enterprise by enquiry) plus an Academia sign-up. Sales contact is at starlims.com.
products.activity: Part of STARLIMS. The public help-center collections did not load.
strengths: Inventory with multiple layers down to batch or aliquot. Custom location hierarchies and position maps
Scanning a QR code records which samples and reagents were used. Low-quantity and expiry alerts in the app or by email
Lineage is tracked automatically for items created in experiments

Order Management: request templates with required fields, tracked from Requested to Approved, Ordered and Received, requests grouped into purchase orders with shipping/handling costs, inventory updated automatically on receipt, @mentions and delivery alerts
Chemistry tools (Ketcher or MarvinJS, PubChem import, hazard pictograms) and plasmid maps with .gb import/export
weaknesses: Few public docs. No budget or duplicate checks documented. Pricing is opaque
products.fit_notes: Ordering patterns are worth copying.

products.name: Genemod
products.license_or_pricing: Free for up to 10 users (base caps, 3 months of history, AI Agent included, no custom types or export). Business for 10-25 users. Enterprise adds audit log and export, roles and permissions, Microsoft SSO, e-signatures, and API on request. No per-seat charges. Academic discounts by application.
products.activity: Active. The site is now AI-first ('AI LIMS', 'AI ELN').
strengths: Virtual freezers: freezers, racks, shelves and cryoboxes, with custom grids (9x9, 10x10 or your own). You can move any layer
8 preset item types: Cell Line, Enzyme, Plasmid, Chemical Probe, Chemical, Antibody, Strain, Primer
Search across all freezers by name, vendor, lot, catalog number or notes
Visual lineage tree for aliquots, pools and derived samples
Barcode check-in/out. CSV and Excel import and export

Orders: shared queue, requests started from low-stock consumables, role-based approval with a timestamped record. On receipt you pick a freezer, cabinet or shelf, the details carry over, and stock updates. Spend tracked by project and lab

AI Agent ('Run your whole lab by command') that plans steps across notebook, inventory, equipment and orders and saves only after sign-off. AI Global Search. 'Works with Claude, ChatGPT, or Copilot'. 'Your data never trains a model'
weaknesses: A 30-person lab exceeds the Business band (10-25), and the audit log and API are Enterprise-only
The free tier keeps only 3 months of history and has no custom fields
Duplicate detection is not mentioned
products.fit_notes: Close to the target UX. Could be trialed free with a subgroup.

products.name: Scispot
products.license_or_pricing: Custom annual pricing in four relative tiers. Unlimited users. Implementation by Scispot's own scientists and engineers.
products.activity: Active. MCP server in private beta.
products.stack: Labsheets (configurable tables) and Manifests. API base https://cloudlab.scispot.io. MCP at https://mcp.scispot.io
strengths: Labsheet API: add, update and filter rows, and look rows up by an ID_BARCODE column
Manifests (plates, boxes, racks) that can be assigned to a location and a position. Bulk location creation
Link External Barcode
Inbound webhooks with a Scispot-Event-Type header
Scibot: 7 specialist agents coordinated by Scibot Omega. Proposed record changes wait for human approval

features.name: Product vs physical instance (lot) data model
