key_insights: Duplicate prevention in commercial tools comes from visibility at the moment of ordering, not clever matching (verified). Quartzy groups matches into Request History, Shop and 'Found in Inventory' while you type a request, and has a 'Duplicate request notification' article. ChemInventory shows items on order in inventory search. Labguru, Genemod, eLabNext and LabArchives each use one shared queue. None documents fuzzy matching across vendors or catalog numbers, so a custom app has room to do better here (my inference).

Vendors are converging on a product-to-physical-instance model (verified). In June-July 2026 Quartzy moved quantity, lot, expiry and location from items to instances, with up to 7 location levels and a pathNames array, which was a breaking API change. Benchling separates entities from containers. LabCollector gives each lot its own barcode. Design for multiple lots and deep locations from the start.

Quartzy is easy to read from and limited to write to (verified from docs.quartzy.com). You can list, create and change the status of order requests, and list inventory items and update their quantities. There are no endpoints to create inventory items, locations or sublocations, and list filters are only page and lab_id. So the custom app has to own physical inventory and use Quartzy for purchasing data.

Quartzy webhook details (verified): CloudEvents 1.0 envelope; data.order_request carries vendor_name, catalog_number, quantity, unit_price, requested_by, spend_tracking_code, is_urgent and backordered_expected_at; HMAC-SHA256 'Signature' header; success means 2xx within 3 s; 3 retries at 10, 100 and 1000 s. Events include order-request created, ordered, received and deleted; inventory-item created, updated and deleted; shipment created; shop order placed; shop order item backordered; inventory-type created and updated. The received event does not link to an inventory item, so matching has to use vendor plus normalized catalog number.
Benchling's free academic plan excludes Inventory and Registry (verified on benchling.com/academic), so the best-known platform is effectively out of reach for this lab.

Rough yearly cost for about 30 users (from pricing pages; totals are my arithmetic): LabArchives Inventory $99/user/yr, about $2,970 ($10,800 for the ELN bundle). LabCollector Inventory Pack from $500/user/yr, about $15,000. CloudLIMS $100/user/month at 25 users, about $30-36k. Labguru is quote-only (a competitor estimates $1,000-1,500/user/yr). Genemod is free up to 10 users, but audit and API are Enterprise-only. ChemInventory is $99/yr for 50 users, chemicals only. Quartzy Academia is $50/month for up to 3 users. These give a build-vs-buy baseline.

Many key features sit behind add-ons or enterprise tiers (verified): SciNote Storage Locations and Stock Management are paid add-ons; Quartzy SDS automation, PO generation, PunchOut and the Benchling integration are paid; Genemod audit log and API are Enterprise; LabArchives API and SSO are Enterprise; CloudLIMS inventory is Enterprise edition only. A custom app avoids these feature gates.

Mobile is the weakest part of the market (verified). Quartzy's iOS app is rated 3.2/5 from 17 ratings, with crash and slow-scan complaints, and is limited to the US and Canada. eLabNext's app has one rating. LabArchives uses an in-app Camera button. Benchling, Freezerworks, CloudLIMS and ChemInventory have no native app. A reliable phone-first web app that scans with the camera would stand out (my inference).

Data entry is the main reason adoption fails (from review excerpts). A Quartzy reviewer said logging usage is 'less realistic in academic labs'. Labguru reviewers cite speed, weak bulk actions and 'a lot of clicking'. LabCollector reviewers found the box system hard and empty spaces hard to find. The fixes vendors use are scan-to-deduct, 'mark as consumed', reordering from a low-stock scan, and receiving with lot and expiry capture.

Receiving that creates inventory is standard (verified): LabArchives 'Mark Received' creates the item; Genemod asks for a freezer, cabinet or shelf on receipt; Labguru records the location on arrival and emails the requester; Labstep updates automatically; Quartzy adds the received amount to stock. This is where a Quartzy-synced app can capture the location and owner of every new purchase.

Visible ownership is how vendors handle personal inventory (verified): Benchling has sample owners and restricted sample parties; SciNote has per-inventory Viewer/User/Owner and private items; ChemInventory has Full/Restricted/None sharing; Freezerworks marks aliquots locked, requested or available; eLabNext has a change-owner action. Letting people keep ownership but making stock visible lowers resistance to centralizing (my inference).

AI from 2024 to 2026 (verified): MCP servers (Scispot with 33 tools in private beta; SciSure on private cloud and on-prem only; Benchling MCP connectors); agents that need human approval (Scispot Scibot, Genemod AI Agent 'saves only after sign-off'); document-to-structured import (Benchling, SciNote Import with AI, Oct 2025); assistants (Labguru Assistant, Apr 2024). Inventory-specific AI is rare: only CloudLIMS reagent optimization and Labviva forecasting.

Vendors are consolidating and pivoting (verified): eLabNext and SciShield became SciSure in Jan 2025, which bought LabFolder in Sep 2025; Labguru is under Cenevo; Labstep is under STARLIMS; colabra.app now redirects to an M&A due-diligence product. This supports full export and an open API in a custom build.

Small, concrete UX details that recur (verified): low-stock threshold summed across lots (LabCollector), expiry reports at 30/60/90 days (LabArchives), selecting a whole row or column of a box (SciNote, Mar 2025), 'Find item' across every location (SciNote), required reason when archiving (eLabNext), a shared box-template library such as 9x9 and 10x10 (Genemod), barcode prefixes per location type (Benchling FRZ001), and consumption export with the balance after each event (SciNote).
recommendations: Split the systems: Quartzy stays the purchasing system and the new app becomes the physical-inventory system. Subscribe to Quartzy webhooks (order-request.created, ordered, received, deleted, backordered; inventory-item.*), check HMAC-SHA256 signatures, respond within 3 s and process from a queue, and reconcile nightly with GET /order-requests?lab_id=...&page=... because only 3 retries are guaranteed.

Make duplicate prevention a gate on every request. On a new Quartzy request (webhook) or an in-app Reorder, search active instances, open requests (CREATED, APPROVED, ORDERED, BACKORDERED) and receipts from the last 60-90 days. Match on normalized vendor and catalog number, CAS, fuzzy name, and target, clone and conjugate for antibodies. Show grouped results the way Quartzy does (In inventory with owner and location / On order / Recently received), and send a Slack or Teams message to the requester and lab manager when a new Quartzy request matches, with a 'cancel or keep' choice.

Use this schema from day one: Product (type, vendor, catalog number, CAS, unit size), Instance (lot, expiry, quantity and unit, status, owner, visibility, location_id, position), a self-referencing Location tree of any depth (room, freezer or tank, shelf, rack, box) with a box-type grid (rows, columns), a Lineage edge table (parent, child, relation: aliquot, passage, derived, pooled), and an append-only Event table (consume, move, check-out, owner change, receive, archive with reason).

Win over people with personal stashes without taking their stock: every instance has an owner, everything is visible to the whole lab by default, owners can mark items 'reserved' or 'ask before use', and add 'request to borrow' and check-out with an assignee, as Benchling does. Report how many duplicates were avoided so the PI can see the effect.

Build a phone-first web app with camera scanning and large buttons. Each flow should take three taps or fewer: Scan, then Use, Empty (which proposes a reorder), Move or Check out. Receive: scan the packing slip or request, enter lot and expiry, take the suggested free box slot, print a label. Support manual search for unlabeled items, and record events like opened, low or empty rather than exact volumes for consumables.

Copy the proven alerts: low-stock thresholds summed across lots, expiry reports at 30/60/90 days, alerts only to owners and users of an item, and a weekly digest to each owner of what is expiring or unclaimed in their boxes.

Make freezers easy to read: box grids with multi-select, row and column selection, drag-and-drop, color by owner or expiry, a next-free-slot suggestion, a capacity report per freezer, and 'Find item' across all locations. Seed box templates (9x9, 10x10, 5x5 LN2 boxes) and add Autofill for racks.

Support labels with ZPL templates for Zebra at 203 dpi, PDF sheets for any printer, and DYMO if the lab has one. Use typed ID prefixes (FRZ-, BOX-, CL-, AB-) and allow linking existing vendor or tube barcodes.

Speed up onboarding: prebuild the product catalog from Quartzy order history (GET /order-requests gives vendor_name, catalog_number, unit_size, unit_price), so people only add location and owner when they inventory. Provide Excel templates per type and a box-map import with a dry run.

Add AI only with a confirmation step: first, extracting fields from photos of packing slips and labels into the receiving form; second, natural-language search over inventory; later, an MCP server with read tools first and writes that need approval (the Scispot pattern), so lab members can ask Claude whether the lab has an item.

Before committing build time, trial cheap commercial baselines, such as LabArchives Inventory's 90-day free trial ($99/user/yr) or Genemod Free (up to 10 users), with a few bench users to see which flows they actually use. Use the results to set the scope of the first custom version.
Offer full CSV/Excel export and a documented REST API from the first release, given how often vendors in this space have merged or pivoted.
pitfalls: Designing quantity at the item level with two location levels. Quartzy had to make a breaking migration to instances with up to 7 levels in 2026.
Assuming Quartzy can hold your inventory data. Its API cannot create inventory items or locations, and webhooks for received orders don't link to inventory items.
Treating webhooks as reliable delivery. Quartzy expects a response within 3 s and retries only 3 times (10, 100, 1000 s), so you need a queue plus polling to reconcile.

Losing who actually requested an item. The documented POST /order-requests body has no requested_by field, so requests made through one service token may show the token owner as the requester (inferred from the schema). Consider per-user OAuth or tokens, or keep the real requester in notes.

Requiring exact volume logging for every use. Reviewers call this unrealistic in academic labs. Use status events (opened, low, empty) for consumables and exact amounts only where they matter (aliquots, vials).
Too many clicks, weak bulk actions, slow pages. These are Labguru's main complaints, and they hurt uptake among wet-lab members.
An unreliable mobile scanner. Quartzy's app reviews (crashes, slow barcode reads) show how fast field users lose trust.
No way to find empty box spaces. A LabCollector reviewer complaint, and it leads people to put samples in random spots.
Starting the audit log late. Quartzy's inventory history only begins in March 2024, according to IntuitionLabs. Log events from the first import.
Hard migrations. Reviewers of Quartzy and LabCollector found importing existing inventory painful. Budget time for spreadsheet cleanup and box-map import tools.
Over-building industry features such as Benchling-style schemas and compliance. Benchling itself says academic labs change data formats often, so keep fields configurable and lightweight.
Comparing against commercial tools without noticing that key features (storage locations, audit, API, punchout) are paid add-ons or enterprise-only.
Vendor churn and lock-in: SciSure, Cenevo and STARLIMS mergers and Colabra's pivot. Avoid by exporting everything and owning the data.
Relying on competitor blog posts (Scispot publishes many comparisons) for price and feature claims about rivals. Treat those as unverified.
open_questions: Which Quartzy plan is the lab on, and does it include Public API and webhook access? (The docs don't say which tier.) Who is the Quartzy admin who can create an Access-Token and set up webhooks under Manage Labs > Developers?
Do all purchases go through Quartzy (Shop and non-Quartzy vendors), or do some go through university procurement or punchout (Ariba, Jaggaer)? Duplicate detection only covers what the app can see.
Does the lab use Slack or Microsoft Teams for alerts?
Which label printers are available (Zebra, DYMO, Brady, or only office printers for sheet labels)? Are cryo-resistant labels needed for LN2?
Does the university already license LabArchives (often site-wide), SciNote or eLabNext/SciSure? An existing license could change build vs buy, or point to an ELN integration.
Does the institution's EHS office already run a chemical inventory (for example SciShield/SciSure EHS)? If so, should chemicals stay out of scope or be synced?
How detailed should freezer tracking be: every tube position for cell-line banks and aliquots, or box level for personal boxes?
Hosting and login: university server or VM vs cloud, and campus SSO (Shibboleth/SAML) availability.
What data exists today (spreadsheets per person, Quartzy inventory module records, paper freezer maps) and roughly how many items and boxes?
Any compliance needs (biosafety or IBC registration for plasmids and strains, MTA restrictions on cell lines, controlled substances)?

Research limitation: the shared WebSearch budget ran out, and G2, Capterra, GetApp, Reddit and several help centers blocked direct fetches. r/labrats sentiment was not gathered and review sentiment comes from search-result excerpts. A follow-up pass could fill this in.

tech_components.recommended: Quartzy Public API (https://api.quartzy.com, Access-Token header) plus Quartzy webhooks (CloudEvents, HMAC-SHA256 Signature header) into a webhook endpoint that verifies, stores and enqueues. Nightly reconciliation through GET /order-requests and GET /inventory-items, paged and scoped by lab_id.
tech_components.rationale: The lab already buys through Quartzy. Webhooks give near-real-time order visibility for duplicate alerts, and polling covers missed deliveries.
alternatives: Polling only (simpler, but slower duplicate alerts)
gotchas: List filters are only page and lab_id
No create endpoints for inventory items or locations
Order-request.received carries no inventory link or received quantity
Webhooks need HTTPS with a valid certificate, a 2xx within 3 s, and get 3 retries
The webhook-creation docs are inconsistent (organization_id vs lab_id)
Detect instance-migrated labs with lab.uses_instances; treat a missing field as migrated

tech_components.recommended: Server-side ZPL templates (203 dpi) for Zebra printers, plus PDF label sheets as a printer-agnostic fallback, and DYMO if the lab has one
tech_components.rationale: ZPL is what Benchling and SciNote use, and sheet labels cover labs without thermal printers (ChemInventory)
alternatives: Cloud cryo-label printers such as FLUICS (eLabNext add-on)
gotchas: Long names overflow small labels (SciNote shipped a fix in July 2025)
Labels for LN2 and -80 need cryo-rated stock

tech_components.need: Letting AI assistants use inventory data
tech_components.recommended: An MCP server on the app's API with OAuth. Read-only tools first (search_inventory, find_locations, list_open_requests). Write tools require the user's own permissions and an explicit approval step.
tech_components.rationale: Scispot, SciSure and Benchling have all moved this way, and Scispot's docs advise starting read-only and reviewing writes
alternatives: An in-app chat search box only
gotchas: SciSure limits MCP to private cloud and on-prem, which is a reminder to scope permissions carefully
Agents should save changes only after sign-off (Genemod and Scispot patterns)

tech_components.recommended: A globally unique ID for every location, box, instance and aliquot, with a type prefix (FRZ-, RCK-, BOX-, CL-, AB-), encoded as a QR code, plus support for linking an external or vendor barcode to a record
tech_components.rationale: Benchling uses prefixed barcodes unique across its registry, and Scispot can link external barcodes. Together they allow both printed and pre-existing labels.
gotchas: Check new barcodes for duplicates (ChemInventory does)
Keep IDs stable when items move

research.angle: opensource: open-source lab inventory, LIMS, ELN and general inventory systems, evaluated both as feature/data-model inspiration and as possible foundations (build on one vs. build from scratch)
research.summary:
I evaluated the 11 required systems plus about 15 smaller or adjacent projects, using official docs, source code, GitHub API metadata and the Quartzy API reference. No open-source tool does this lab's core job out of the box. At the moment of requesting, it should say "we already have 2 vials in −80 #3, owned by A" and "B requested this in Quartzy yesterday."

InvenTree is the only realistic base to build on:
- **License and stack:** MIT, Python/Django + DRF, React UI.
- **Health:** 7,764 stars, last push 2026-10-27, release 1.6.3 on 27 Oct 2026.
- **Mobile:** native iOS/Android apps with camera scanning and purchase-order receiving.
- **Data model:** Part → SupplierPart → StockItem (batch, expiry_date, owner, status, purchase_price) and a StockLocation tree with location types. The Part API exposes an "On Order" (`ordering`) annotation.
- **Plugins:** 21 mixins, including AppMixin (custom DB tables), UserInterfaceMixin (UI panels), ScheduleMixin, BarcodeMixin, LabelPrintingMixin and NotificationMixin.
- **Gaps:** manufacturing vocabulary (Parts/BOM/Build orders), no freezer-box grid model, no parameters on StockItem, and its purchase orders overlap Quartzy.
- **Risk:** 1.6.0 shipped breaking changes.

eLabFTW (AGPL, PHP) is the best adopt-as-is option, especially if an ELN is also wanted. It has resource categories with custom fields, a booking scheduler (recurring bookings in 6.1-alpha), storage units plus containers with quantity/unit, a PubChem-backed compounds DB, and procurement requests since 5.1. It is a poor base for a Python developer.

openBIS has the most lab-appropriate model: life-science object types, Request→Order with requests locked once ordered, and freezer/rack/box positions. It is a heavy Java system, too much for one person unless the institute already runs it.

Poor bases, but useful sources of ideas:
- **SENAITE:** runs on Python 2.7 and targets analytical labs.
- **Baobab LIMS:** no pushes since June 2022.
- **MISO:** sequencing-focused, but its box and rack-scanning model is excellent.
- **LabKey CE:** freezer management sits in the commercial Sample Manager/LIMS editions.
- **Chemotion:** chemistry-only; useful chemical-inventory fields.
- **SampleDB:** Flask metadata DB with no stock tracking.
- **Snipe-IT:** equipment assets.
- **Grocy:** consumable semantics (opened date, shelf life after opening, minimum stock → shopping list).

ERPNext's Projected Qty formula and RSpace's grid-container API are the two best ideas to copy.

Frank call: run a short InvenTree pilot and prototype the Quartzy duplicate-flagging job, which is needed on either path. I expect a focused Django app built from scratch, copying InvenTree's data model and dependency stack, to fit the bench-UX and Quartzy-first goals better (this is inference).

Caveat: the shared WebSearch budget ran out midway. Later facts came from direct fetches of primary URLs, and LabKey, SciNote, OpenSpecimen and Aquarium details are only partly verified.

features.name: Three-layer catalog model: Product -> SupplierProduct -> StockItem
features.description: Product = what it is (e.g., 'anti-GAPDH rabbit mAb clone 14C10'; type, category, typed attributes). SupplierProduct = how it is bought (vendor, catalog_number, pack_size + unit, list price, URL, Quartzy link). StockItem = one physical vial, bottle or box (product, supplier_product, lot/batch, quantity + unit, expiry_date, opened_date, status, owner, location, position, parent for aliquots, source order). Product totals are aggregates of active StockItems.
features.why_it_matters: Duplicate checks and 'do we have it?' searches must match at the product/catalog level, while freezers hold individual tubes. Mixing the two levels is why personal spreadsheets fail. This is the pattern every mature tool uses.

features.name: Projected availability panel (in stock + requested + ordered)
features.description: For every Product compute and show: in_stock (sum of active StockItems), requested (mirrored Quartzy order requests in CREATED/APPROVED), on_order (ORDERED/BACKORDERED, with backordered_expected_at), and received-but-not-shelved. projected = in_stock + requested + on_order. When a request becomes an order, its quantity moves from requested to on_order, so it is never counted twice. Shown on product pages, search results and the request form.
features.why_it_matters: This directly addresses the PI's complaint: anyone about to order sees that the item exists or is already on its way.
seen_in: ERPNext Projected Qty = Actual + Planned + Requested + Ordered - Reserved

features.name: Duplicate-request guard (pre-submit and approver queue)
features.description: Before submitting a request from the app (which POSTs to Quartzy /order-requests), match it in two ways: exact match on normalized vendor + catalog_number, and fuzzy match on name (RapidFuzz token_set_ratio or PostgreSQL pg_trgm). Search StockItems, open Quartzy requests from the last N days, and recent receipts. Show messages such as 'Lab has 2 vials (−80 #3, owner A)' or 'B requested this 2 days ago (APPROVED)', and require a reason to proceed. Because people will keep using Quartzy directly, also scan newly mirrored CREATED requests and flag likely duplicates to the approver before approval.
features.why_it_matters: Quartzy has an approval step, so a flag raised at CREATED status catches duplicates even when users bypass the app.
seen_in: openBIS (requests cannot be added to additional orders once ordered)

features.name: Quartzy sync service
features.description: A scheduled job sends the Access-Token header and calls GET https://api.quartzy.com/order-requests?lab_id=&page=. It mirrors id, status, item_name, vendor_name, catalog_number, quantity, unit_size, unit_price, total_price, requested_by, requested_at, spend_tracking_code, is_urgent and backordered_expected_at. Optionally it also receives Quartzy webhooks (POST /webhooks; verify is_signed/signing_key). Status mapping: CREATED → requested, APPROVED → approved, ORDERED/BACKORDERED → on order, RECEIVED → 'awaiting shelving' task, CANCELLED → closed. If the lab also keeps Quartzy inventory, push quantities back with PUT /inventory-items/{itemId}/instances/{itemInstanceId}.
features.why_it_matters: Quartzy stays the purchasing system of record and the app becomes the inventory system of record, with no double entry. The Quartzy API cannot create inventory items, so the app must own inventory.
seen_in: eLabFTW maintainer's suggestion to script against GET /api/v2/teams/current/procurement_requests

features.name: Receive → label → put-away flow
features.description: When a mirrored request turns RECEIVED, it lands in a 'To shelve' list on the phone. The receiver picks the request (or scans the package), confirms lot and expiry (prefilled from the product's shelf-life default), prints one label per vial or bottle, then scans the destination location or box position. This creates StockItems linked to the order and notifies the requester ('in Fridge 2, shelf B').
features.why_it_matters: Most inventory systems decay because new items never get entered. Tying entry to the moment of delivery captures stock at its source with almost no extra work.
seen_in: InvenTree PO receive-into-stock (location, serials, unit cost) and mobile app 'Receive purchase orders and check in stock items'

features.name: Typed storage hierarchy with location types
features.description: Tree: building → room → storage unit (−80, −20, 4 °C, LN2 dewar, RT shelf, flammables cabinet) → shelf/rack/tower/canister → box. A LocationType carries icon, temperature, structural (cannot hold items directly), capacity and grid dimensions. Implement with a materialized-path tree (django-treebeard) so queries like 'everything in freezer B' are fast.
features.why_it_matters: People need to find things physically. Typed nodes support capacity warnings and the correct UI per node (a grid for boxes, a list for shelves).
seen_in: eLabFTW storage units (root elements cannot hold containers)
MISO rooms → freezers → shelves/stacks/racks/tray racks/loose storage

features.name: Freezer box grid maps with positions
features.description: A box is a location with rows × cols and a labelling scheme (A1–I9 or 1–81). A Position(box, row, col) has at most one occupant. Click an empty cell to place an item, drag to move, colour cells by owner, type or expiry, show occupancy %, and offer 'next free slot'. Optional per-position barcodes (box prefix + A01 suffix).
features.why_it_matters: Cell-line vials, glycerol stocks and plasmid preps live in −80/LN2 boxes. Without positions, people keep private paper box maps, which is the 'personal inventory' problem.
seen_in: RSpace GridContainerPost(name, rows, columns, can_store_samples) + add_items_to_grid_container ByRow/ByColumn
MISO boxes (rows/columns, scannable sizes, Fill by Barcode Pattern)
LabKey Sample Manager box grids up to 50 rows (commercial)

features.name: Freezer templates and bulk structure creation
features.description: One form creates e.g. a −80 with 5 shelves × 4 racks × 7 boxes of 9×9, with auto-generated names and labels. A configurable validation level (rack only / rack + box / rack + box + position) lets less critical storage stay coarse.
features.why_it_matters: Setup effort is a major adoption barrier, and coarse levels avoid over-modelling fridges.
seen_in: RSpace client example freezer.py (freezer → shelf → rack → tray → box)
openBIS storage configuration (shelves, racks, boxes per rack, validation level)

features.name: Aliquots and lineage
features.description: StockItem.parent FK. A 'split' action creates N children with quantities that inherit product, lot and owner. Derivations (glycerol stock → miniprep DNA; cell vial → culture → new vials at passage+1) are recorded as lineage edges, and the parent shows remaining volume.
features.why_it_matters: Aliquoting is constant in wet labs. Lineage answers 'which lot did this aliquot come from?' when an experiment fails.

features.name: Ownership without hiding (personal stock stays visible)
features.description: Every StockItem and Location has an owner (user or group), inherited from its location (e.g., 'Priya's box' sets Priya as owner for its contents). Owners control edits and consumption, but everyone can see and search everything. An optional 'reserved, ask owner' flag covers sensitive stocks.
features.why_it_matters: People keep personal inventories to protect their stuff. Explicit ownership lets them keep control while ending duplicate purchases, which makes adoption more likely than confiscation would.
seen_in: InvenTree stock ownership (user or group owner, inherited from location)

features.name: Borrow / 'ask the owner' requests
features.description: A 'Can I use 20 µL of your anti-FLAG?' button notifies the owner, who approves. The app records home location vs current location and who has the item (borrower).
features.why_it_matters: It turns hidden personal stock into shared stock without conflict, which directly reduces duplicate orders.
seen_in: Chemotion inventory location host/current with 'by' borrower field

features.name: Consumable semantics: opened, shelf life after opening, minimum stock
features.description: Product fields: default_shelf_life_days, default_days_after_open, min_stock_qty, treat_opened_as_out_of_stock. StockItem.opened_date. Verbs: consume (partial), open, transfer, stocktake (set count), discard. Projected stock below the minimum triggers a reorder suggestion (one click creates a Quartzy request).
features.why_it_matters: Shared buffers, media, kits and plastics run out unexpectedly. Opened-date logic matters for enzymes, antibiotics and media.
seen_in: Grocy (default_best_before_days_after_open, treat_opened_as_out_of_stock, min_stock_amount, /open /consume /transfer /inventory, shopping list add-missing-products)

features.name: Expiry and stale-stock digests with subscriptions
features.description: A daily job finds items expiring or expired within N days and sends each subscriber one email or Slack digest. Users subscribe to products or categories ('antibodies', 'my boxes'). A weekly digest of new and pending requests goes to the lab manager.
features.why_it_matters: It prevents waste and silent reorders of expired reagents, and digests avoid notification fatigue.
seen_in: InvenTree STOCK_ENABLE_EXPIRY + STOCK_STALE_DAYS daily grouped emails to part/category subscribers
eLabFTW maintainer's weekly procurement email suggestion

features.name: Item-type templates with typed, unit-aware fields
features.description: Each item type has a JSON-schema or model-backed field set: Antibody (target, host, clonality, clone, isotype, conjugate, reactivity, applications, RRID, dilution), Cell line (species, tissue, RRID, BSL, passage, mycoplasma status), Plasmid (backbone, insert, resistance, Addgene ID, GenBank file), Strain, Oligo, Chemical (CAS, GHS, storage class), Kit, Buffer. Units are validated and converted with pint, and the list is filterable by attributes.
features.why_it_matters: Generic 'name + notes' inventories are unsearchable. Typed fields enable real duplicate detection (same clone, same conjugate) and trustworthy records.
seen_in: openBIS Life Sciences types (Antibodies, Chemicals, Enzymes, Media, Solutions and Buffers, Plasmids, Oligos, RNA, Bacteria, Cell lines, Flies, Yeasts, Plants)
InvenTree parameter templates (units, choices, selection lists, parametric filtering)

features.name: QC test records on lots and vials
features.description: Test templates per type (Mycoplasma PCR, STR authentication, Sanger verification, endotoxin), each with required / requires value / requires attachment flags. Results attach to specific vials or lots, and an item cannot be marked 'available' until required tests pass.
features.why_it_matters: Cell-line authentication and mycoplasma status are what people most want to know before thawing someone else's vial.
seen_in: InvenTree test templates/results (Required, Requires Value, Requires Attachment, Enabled)

features.name: Opaque native barcodes + linking vendor barcodes
features.description: Every StockItem, Location and Box gets a short opaque ID encoded as QR, Micro QR or DataMatrix (e.g., a short URL /s/7F3K2). Never encode mutable data. Existing vendor or GS1 barcodes can be linked to items. Scanning opens the object page directly ('scan-to-context').
features.why_it_matters: Labels stay valid when items move or change, and scanning replaces typing for gloved users.
seen_in: InvenTree native barcodes + linking third-party barcodes

key_insights: No open-source system combines inventory with Quartzy-style purchasing and duplicate prevention. The closest built-in ordering flows: (1) openBIS Requests → Orders: setting an order to 'Ordered' updates all linked requests, which then cannot be added to additional orders. (2) eLabFTW procurement requests (since 5.1): resources marked 'procurable' with a price, and a Team > Procurement requests tab. As of Feb 2025 the maintainer said routing these to a purchaser 'hasn't been implemented yet' and suggested scripting GET /api/v2/teams/current/procurement_requests. (3) InvenTree's Part API 'ordering' (On Order) annotation, which only counts InvenTree's own purchase orders. The Quartzy-aware duplicate check has to be custom code on any path.

All mature tools share one model: a catalog definition (InvenTree Part, openBIS Product, Grocy product, RSpace Sample) separate from physical instances (StockItem, stock entry with stock_id, Subsample, eLabFTW container), stored in a location tree. Box grids appear only in LIMS/biobank-style tools.

Box grid positions are first-class only in openBIS (STORAGE_POSITION with rack row/column, box name, box size, box position), MISO (rows/columns, scannable box sizes, rack scanning), RSpace (GridContainerPost rows/columns + ByRow/ByColumn placement), LabKey Sample Manager (box grids up to 50 rows, commercial) and OpenSpecimen. InvenTree has only a location tree, and eLabFTW documents storage units + containers with quantity/unit/multiplier but no grid.

Verified InvenTree internals relevant to customization: StockItem fields include part, supplier_part, location, quantity, batch, serial, expiry_date, purchase_price, packaging, owner, status, purchase_order, parent, delete_on_deplete and stocktake_date. StockItem has no InvenTreeParameterMixin; it has MetadataMixin, tags, attachments and notes. StockLocation does support parameters and has structural/external/location_type. InvenTree has 21 plugin mixins, including AppMixin for custom Django models (documented as a 'danger zone').

Maintenance health:
- Healthy, with pushes in Oct 2026: InvenTree, eLabFTW, MISO (v4.0.0, 22 Oct 2026), Snipe-IT, SampleDB, Chemotion, RSpace, OpenSpecimen, NEMO, ERPNext.
- Slower: Grocy (last push Sep 2026), Aquarium (Dec 2025).
- Stale: JBEI ICE (May 2024), LImBuS (Aug 2024), Baobab LIMS (June 2022), ExperimentDB (2014).
- SENAITE: last release 2.6.0 on 2025-04-04, and its docs state 'SENAITE 2.x runs on Python 2.7'.

openBIS versioning is in flux: 20.10.12 is the production line, 6.x releases were early access (6.7 in April 2025, 'must NOT be used in production'), and 7.0.0 early access was posted July 2026. pyBIS 1.37.5 shipped 19 Aug 2026, with 7.0.0rc6 on 21 Oct 2026. Self-hosting through a major-version transition is a real burden for one person.

LabKey Community Edition is free, but the storage features that appear in Sample Manager release notes are listed against commercial editions (SM Starter/Professional, LIMS Starter/Enterprise, Biologics). These include terminal storage barcodes, box grids, check-in/out and reason-required storage changes. Premium LabKey Server lists $310 (Starter) and $446 (Professional) per user/month, assuming 10 users billed annually.

Quartzy API constraints shape the architecture:
- The base is https://api.quartzy.com with an Access-Token header (per-user tokens).
- Order requests can be listed, created and status-updated (CREATED, CANCELLED, APPROVED, ORDERED, BACKORDERED, RECEIVED).
- Inventory items can be read, but only their quantity can be updated (instance-level PUT). There is no endpoint to create inventory items.
- Webhooks exist (url, event_types, is_signed, signing_key), but the event types are not documented.
- Pagination is page-number only.
- Conclusion: the app should own inventory and mirror procurement.

Bench-UX lessons from the projects:
- Scan-to-context with opaque IDs (BrrrCode labels encode only '/b/003'; InvenTree native barcodes).
- Camera scanning requires HTTPS (Grocy).
- USB laser scanners beat cameras in bad light (Grocy author).
- Offline edit queue in IndexedDB for cold rooms (BrrrCode).
- Micro QR for tiny labels (openBIS).
- Nothing hard-deleted, so mis-scans can be undone (BrrrCode, Grocy transaction undo).

The 'personal inventory' problem is mainly about ownership and visibility. Existing tools handle it with explicit owners rather than central control:
- InvenTree: stock ownership by a user or group, inherited from the location.
- SampleDB: a responsible user confirms each location assignment.
- Chemotion: host vs current location plus a 'by' borrower field.

Grocy and ERPNext model consumable quantities better than LIMS tools do. Grocy has default_best_before_days_after_open, treat_opened_as_out_of_stock and min_stock_amount → shopping list (add-missing-products). ERPNext uses Projected Qty = Actual + Planned + Requested + Ordered − Reserved…, and converting a Material Request into a Purchase Order moves quantity out of Requested so it is not counted twice. That accounting is exactly what duplicate-order prevention needs.

License summary:
- MIT: InvenTree, SampleDB, Grocy, Aquarium, BrrrCode.
- Apache-2.0: openBIS, LabKey platform.
- BSD: OpenSpecimen (BSD-3), JBEI ICE (modified BSD).
- GPL: SENAITE (GPL-2.0); MISO, Baobab, iSkyLIMS, LImBuS, ERPNext (GPL-3.0).
- AGPL-3.0: eLabFTW, Snipe-IT, Chemotion, RSpace, Part-DB, HomeBox.
- Also: OpenBoxes EPL-1.0, SciNote MPL-2.0.
- AGPL is fine for internal hosting, but modified versions must be offered to their network users. brother_ql is GPL-3.0.

The GitHub topic sweep found no mature lab-specific Django/Flask inventory app. 'lab-inventory' lists only 6 repos (all tiny), 'plasmid' is almost entirely sequence-analysis tools, and 'freezer' is mostly unrelated or home-freezer projects. Useful Python lab apps exist only in adjacent niches: NEMO (Django, equipment reservations/interlocks, 185 stars), iSkyLIMS (Django, sequencing, 96 stars), Parkour2 (sequencing, 37 stars) and LImBuS (biobank, stale). Lab-specific small projects found were tiny or stale: ExperimentDB (2014), freezerbox (0 stars).

InvenTree's own dependency list is a strong ready-made 'build from scratch' stack: django<6.0, djangorestframework, drf-spectacular, django-allauth[mfa,socialaccount,saml,openid], django-auditlog, django-q2, django-fsm-2, django-money, django-taggit, django-ical, pint, rapidfuzz, python-barcode, qrcode, ppf.datamatrix, weasyprint and tablib. It still uses django-mptt, whose README says 'This project is currently unmaintained'.

Research-process caveat: the shared WebSearch budget ran out midway, so later facts came from direct fetches of primary docs, code and GitHub API URLs. Not verified: SciNote inventory features, the Aquarium object model, OpenSpecimen container details beyond its README and a curated list, LabKey's exact Community vs commercial feature boundary, and Quartzy webhook event types.
recommendations:
Frank verdict on bases:
- InvenTree is the only credible build-on foundation for a lab maintained by one Python developer: MIT, Python/Django, very active, native mobile apps, and a plugin system that adds database tables, API endpoints, UI panels, scheduled jobs, barcode handlers and label printers without forking.
- eLabFTW is the best adopt-as-is option if the PI also wants an ELN and equipment booking with near-zero development. It is PHP, and its inventory is shallow: no grid positions, simple procurement.
- openBIS has the most lab-appropriate model, but only use it if your institute already operates it.
- Do not use these as bases: SENAITE (Python 2.7, analytical-lab domain), Baobab (abandoned 2022), MISO (sequencing), LabKey CE (storage is commercial), Chemotion (chemistry), SampleDB (no stock tracking), Snipe-IT (IT assets) or Grocy (household).

Suggested decision process:
1. Run a 2–3 week InvenTree pilot in Docker: one −80, one shared 4 °C fridge, two imported personal inventories, the mobile app on 3–4 phones, and one Brother QL printer.
2. In parallel, build the Quartzy mirror plus duplicate-flagging job as a standalone Python package. It is needed on either path.
3. Stay on InvenTree if bench users accept its UI and vocabulary, and box grids can wait or a plugin covers them.
4. Go from scratch if users balk at Parts/BOM/Build terminology or the generic app, or if box maps and a Quartzy-first request screen are the heart of the product.

My expectation (inference): given the 'ambitious' brief and the gloves-on UX requirement, from-scratch Django wins, with InvenTree as the reference design.

If building on InvenTree, customize this way:
- **Data mapping:** PartCategories = item types (Antibodies, Cell lines, Plasmids, Strains, Oligos, Chemicals, Kits, Buffers, Consumables). Part parameter templates (unit-aware) hold catalog attributes. SupplierPart holds vendor + catalog number + pack size. StockItem = vial/bottle, with batch = lot, expiry_date and owner. StockLocation plus location types (Freezer, Rack, Box) form the storage tree.
- **Settings:** enable STOCK_ENABLE_EXPIRY, STOCK_STALE_DAYS and stock ownership. Give members no Build/Sales/Return/Transfer roles so those modules are disabled or hidden.
- **Plugin 1, 'quartzy':** ScheduleMixin + APICallMixin poll /order-requests; an AppMixin model mirrors requests; UrlsMixin provides a webhook endpoint; NotificationMixin sends duplicate alerts; a UserInterfaceMixin panel on Part pages shows open Quartzy requests.
- **Plugin 2, 'boxes':** an AppMixin Position(location, row, col, stock_item) model, a UserInterfaceMixin grid panel, and BarcodeMixin for box/position codes.
- **Per-vial attributes** (passage, freeze date, concentration): StockItem.metadata JSON or a plugin model, because StockItem has no parameters.
- **Labels:** cryovial label templates plus inventree-brother-plugin.
- **Login:** SSO via allauth SAML/OIDC.

InvenTree upgrade and fork risk:
- Never fork core or the Flutter app. Keep all lab logic in an out-of-tree pip-installable plugin.
- Pin InvenTree versions and upgrade on a schedule (e.g., quarterly), only after the plugin test suite passes against the new release in CI.
- Expect breaking changes: 1.6.0 alone moved to FSM-based states, HMAC-hashed API tokens and a notes refactor. AppMixin is documented as a 'danger zone', and UI panels are written in JS/TS against a React UI that evolves.
- Budget about a day per upgrade (inference).
- Accept the generic mobile app as-is. If the bench needs a tailored scan flow, build a small PWA against InvenTree's REST API rather than forking the Dart app.

If building from scratch, copy these model shapes:
- **Product:** type, typed attributes in JSONB validated by per-type schemas, default_shelf_life_days, default_days_after_open, min_stock_qty.
- **SupplierProduct:** vendor, catalog_number_normalized, pack_size, unit, price, url, quartzy_type.
- **StockItem:** product, supplier_product, lot, quantity Decimal + unit, status, owner (user or group), location, position, parent, expiry_date, opened_date, source_request.
- **Location:** treebeard MP_Node, with a LocationType carrying structural, capacity, rows, cols, label_scheme and temperature.
- **Position:** unique (box, row, col).
- **StockEvent:** append-only ledger with user, delta, from/to, reason, source.
- **ProcurementRequest:** a Quartzy mirror with status FSM CREATED/APPROVED/ORDERED/BACKORDERED/RECEIVED/CANCELLED.
- **Availability:** a ProjectedAvailability view or query using the ERPNext formula.
- **QC:** TestTemplate/TestResult as in InvenTree.
- **Ownership:** inheritance from location as in InvenTree, with a responsible-user confirmation on moves (from SampleDB).

Library stack to adopt even if not using InvenTree (these mirror InvenTree's choices where possible):
- Core: Django 5 + DRF or django-ninja, PostgreSQL (JSONB, pg_trgm).
- Trees and history: django-treebeard rather than the unmaintained django-mptt; django-simple-history or django-auditlog.
- Workflow and jobs: django-fsm-2, django-q2 (or Celery).
- Data: django-import-export + tablib, pint, RapidFuzz.
- Auth: django-allauth (SAML/OIDC/MFA).
- Barcodes and labels: segno (QR + Micro QR), python-barcode (Code128), ppf.datamatrix; WeasyPrint for PDF labels; brother_ql for Brother QL printers.
- Browser scanning: zxing-wasm or the barcode-detector polyfill. Both are MIT and active; html5-qrcode's last push was Dec 2025.
- UI: server-rendered pages + HTMX for desktop, plus one PWA scan screen with an IndexedDB offline queue (HTMX choice is my inference, not verified).

Quartzy integration design, independent of the base:
- Treat Quartzy as the purchasing system of record and the app as the inventory system of record.
- Mirror order requests every few minutes, and use webhooks if their event types cover order-request changes. Verify signatures.
- Create requests from the app's duplicate-checked form via POST /order-requests.
- Flag duplicates on CREATED requests so the approver sees them before APPROVED.
- On RECEIVED, generate a 'to shelve' task that creates labelled StockItems.
- Push quantities to Quartzy instances only if the lab keeps using Quartzy Inventory. The API cannot create inventory items, so a two-way inventory sync is not possible.

Do not build an ELN, an equipment-booking system or an IT-style asset manager in v1. If those are wanted later, deploy eLabFTW (ELN + scheduler; API v2 with /items, /events, /storage_units and the elabapi-python client), NEMO (Django; reservations and interlocks) or Snipe-IT (equipment assets, audits, maintenance), and link to them by URL or API.

Adoption tactics from the evaluated tools:
- Run an 'inventory amnesty' week with spreadsheet templates per item type (the openBIS/eLabFTW import pattern).
- Keep personal ownership but make everything searchable (InvenTree ownership, Chemotion borrower model).
- Label existing boxes first: box-level location only (openBIS validation level 'rack + box'), with positions only for cell lines and plasmids.
- Put a USB scanner and label printer at the freezers and the receiving bench.
- Send weekly digests instead of constant alerts (InvenTree's stale-stock digest pattern).

Licensing guidance:
- Building on MIT InvenTree imposes no obligations on your plugin.
- Modifying an AGPL app (eLabFTW, Snipe-IT, Chemotion, RSpace) means lab users must be able to get your modified source. That is easy internally, but keep modifications in a public or internal repo.
- Using GPL brother_ql inside a server you don't distribute triggers no distribution obligations.
- Prefer MIT/BSD/Apache libraries for anything you might share with other labs later.

tech_components.recommended: Django 5.x + Django REST Framework (or django-ninja) on PostgreSQL
tech_components.rationale: Same stack as InvenTree (its requirements pin django<6.0), so its patterns and code are directly reusable. Admin, auth and migrations come built in, which suits a single maintainer.
gotchas: Put domain logic (moves, splits, request matching) in a service layer so it survives a later switch to or from InvenTree

tech_components.recommended: django-treebeard (MP_Node materialized path)
tech_components.rationale: Apache-2.0, 1,226 stars, pushed Oct 2026. Efficient subtree queries.
alternatives: django-mptt (README: 'This project is currently unmaintained'; InvenTree still uses it)
gotchas: Moving a rack must move all descendants atomically and write ledger events

tech_components.recommended: Explicit append-only StockEvent table + django-simple-history (BSD-3) or django-auditlog (InvenTree's choice)
tech_components.rationale: InvenTree records a tracking event with the user for every stock adjustment, and LabKey Sample Manager can require a reason for storage changes. Model history covers non-stock edits.
gotchas: Index history by item and date; history tables grow quickly

tech_components.need: Background jobs (Quartzy polling, digests, expiry scans)
tech_components.recommended: django-q2 (used by InvenTree)
tech_components.rationale: Database/Redis-backed queue and scheduler that is simple for one maintainer.
gotchas: Make Quartzy sync idempotent (upsert by Quartzy id) and tolerant of page-based pagination

tech_components.recommended: django-fsm-2
tech_components.rationale: InvenTree 1.6.0 moved to a formal FSM approach. Maps cleanly to Quartzy statuses CREATED/APPROVED/ORDERED/BACKORDERED/RECEIVED/CANCELLED and to openBIS-style locking once ordered.

tech_components.recommended: RapidFuzz + PostgreSQL pg_trgm trigram indexes + normalized catalog numbers
tech_components.rationale: RapidFuzz is MIT, 4,182 stars, active, and an InvenTree dependency. Trigram indexes make 'did you mean' instant.
gotchas: Normalize vendor aliases (e.g., Thermo/Invitrogen/Life Technologies) and catalog-number suffixes; exact catalog matches should outrank fuzzy name matches
Tune thresholds against real Quartzy history

tech_components.recommended: pint
tech_components.rationale: InvenTree uses pint for unit-aware parameters and pack-size conversion. Prevents µL vs mL errors.
gotchas: Store a Decimal in a base unit plus a display unit
GitHub does not auto-detect pint's license file; verify before redistribution

tech_components.need: Spreadsheet import/export for onboarding personal inventories
tech_components.recommended: django-import-export + tablib
tech_components.rationale: BSD-2, 3,334 stars, active. Column mapping, validation and dry-run preview. InvenTree also uses tablib.
alternatives: Custom import wizard modelled on openBIS XLS batch-registration templates

tech_components.recommended: segno (QR + Micro QR, BSD-3) + python-barcode (Code128) + ppf.datamatrix (DataMatrix); WeasyPrint for HTML→PDF label sheets
tech_components.rationale: Mirrors InvenTree's stack (python-barcode, qrcode, ppf.datamatrix, weasyprint). Micro QR and DataMatrix fit cryovial labels, and openBIS supports Micro QR. WeasyPrint is BSD-3 with 9,736 stars.
gotchas: Encode only opaque IDs or URLs, never mutable data
Use cryo-rated label stock for −80/LN2

tech_components.recommended: brother_ql (Brother QL raster protocol)
tech_components.rationale: 725 stars, pushed Jan 2026. The InvenTree Brother plugin (MIT) shows a working integration.
gotchas: brother_ql is GPL-3.0 (fine for internal servers; matters only if you distribute)

tech_components.recommended: zxing-wasm or barcode-detector polyfill (ZXing-C++ via WebAssembly)
tech_components.rationale: Both MIT and pushed Oct 2026. Reads QR, DataMatrix and Code128 and exposes the standard BarcodeDetector API.
gotchas: Camera access requires HTTPS (Grocy README)
Native BarcodeDetector is missing in some browsers such as iOS Safari, hence the polyfill (inference)
Frosted tubes and poor light favour hardware scanners

tech_components.need: Server-side barcode decoding (photos of racks or labels)
tech_components.recommended: zxing-cpp Python bindings
tech_components.rationale: Apache-2.0, 2,070 stars, pushed Oct 2026.
alternatives: pylibdmtx for DataMatrix (MIT; last push Aug 2025)

tech_components.recommended: django-allauth with SAML and OIDC + MFA
tech_components.rationale: InvenTree uses django-allauth[mfa,socialaccount,saml,openid]. Universities typically offer SAML or OIDC.
gotchas: Map SSO groups to app roles (member, approver, admin)

tech_components.recommended: Server-rendered Django templates + HTMX for desktop, plus one installable PWA scan screen with an IndexedDB offline queue
tech_components.rationale: Least JavaScript for a single maintainer (my inference; not verified in this research). BrrrCode demonstrates the PWA + IndexedDB queue pattern.
alternatives: React + Mantine + TanStack Query (InvenTree's UI stack)
Using the InvenTree mobile app when on the InvenTree path
gotchas: Large touch targets and minimal typing for gloved users

tech_components.recommended: httpx/requests client against https://api.quartzy.com with the Access-Token header
tech_components.rationale: The only documented integration path. Endpoints: GET/POST /order-requests, GET/PUT /order-requests/{id}, GET /inventory-items, PUT /inventory-items/{itemId}/instances/{itemInstanceId}, GET /types, GET /labs, GET/POST /webhooks.
gotchas: No endpoint to create inventory items
Tokens are per user
Webhook event_types are undocumented; verify is_signed/signing_key
Only page-number pagination
Labs with uses_instances must use the instance-level quantity endpoint

tech_components.recommended: Out-of-tree pip-installable plugin using AppMixin, ScheduleMixin, APICallMixin, UrlsMixin, UserInterfaceMixin, BarcodeMixin, LabelPrintingMixin, NotificationMixin, ValidationMixin
tech_components.rationale: Covers the Quartzy sync, box grids and lab-specific labels without forking core.
gotchas: AppMixin is documented as a 'danger zone'
Plugin APIs change across releases (1.6.0 breaking changes)
UI panels are JS/TS

open_questions: Does the lab use Quartzy only for ordering, or also Quartzy Inventory? The API exposes inventory items with instances (lot_number, expiration_date, location/sublocation) and a lab.uses_instances flag, which affects whether we push quantities back.
Can we get a Quartzy API Access-Token (tokens are per user), and which webhook event types does the lab's plan expose? They are not documented on the public API page.
Who approves Quartzy requests (PI, lab manager)? The approver dashboard for flagging duplicates depends on this.
Hosting and identity: can we run Docker on a university VM or must we use central IT? Which SSO is available (SAML/Shibboleth, OIDC, LDAP)?
Does the institute already run openBIS, eLabFTW, LabKey or RSpace centrally? Joining an existing service could change the build-on answer.
Is an ELN or equipment booking also wanted? If so, eLabFTW as a companion becomes attractive.
Which item types and storage are in scope for v1 (cell lines, antibodies, plasmids/strains, oligos, chemicals, kits)? How many freezers, LN2 dewars and boxes need position-level maps?
What label printer and cryo-label stock are available or affordable (Brother QL vs Zebra), and is a USB scanner at each freezer acceptable?
How much development time per week can the bioinformatician commit, and can the second bioinformatician act as backup maintainer?
What compliance must be supported: EHS chemical inventory by room, controlled substances, BSL-2 cell-line records, MTAs for plasmids and cell lines?
Do existing personal inventories live in spreadsheets, paper box maps, or other tools? This determines the import tooling for onboarding week.
pitfalls: Forking InvenTree core or its Flutter app. Release 1.6.0 alone shipped breaking changes (FSM states, HMAC tokens, notes refactor), so forks rot quickly; keep everything in plugins or a separate service.
Building a second purchasing system. People will keep using Quartzy directly, so the duplicate check must also work on requests mirrored from Quartzy, not only on requests made in the app.

Choosing platforms on dead or obsolete stacks or behind commercial gates: SENAITE 2.x on Python 2.7, Baobab (no pushes since 2022), JBEI ICE (stale since May 2024), LabKey storage features (commercial editions).
Depending on unmaintained libraries: django-mptt says it is unmaintained; html5-qrcode's last push was Dec 2025. Prefer django-treebeard and zxing-wasm.

Over-modelling on day one. Position-level tracking of every fridge item and dozens of mandatory fields will kill adoption. Start with box-level locations, use positions only for −80/LN2 cell lines and plasmids, and require only a few fields.
Encoding mutable data (names, owners, locations) in barcodes, and printing on labels that fail at −80/LN2.

Duplicate detection that only does exact name matching. Vendor names and catalog numbers vary (pack-size suffixes, reseller vs manufacturer), so normalize and combine exact catalog matching with fuzzy name matching, then tune on real Quartzy history.
Camera scanning without HTTPS, or relying on the native BarcodeDetector API that some browsers lack. Ship a WASM polyfill and support USB scanners.

Quartzy API surprises: no inventory-item creation, per-user tokens, undocumented webhook event types, page-number-only pagination, and at least one documentation error (the 404 text for GET /inventory-items/{id}).
AGPL obligations if you modify eLabFTW, Snipe-IT, Chemotion or RSpace and expose them to users; GPL if you ever distribute code that bundles brother_ql.
Bus factor of one. Without docs, tests and a second maintainer, the app dies when the builder leaves; this argues for a smaller codebase on InvenTree or a tightly scoped from-scratch app.
Treating eLabFTW's procurement requests or InvenTree's purchase orders as a duplicate-prevention solution. Neither sees Quartzy activity or matches duplicates by default.

research.summary: Quartzy has an official REST API (https://docs.quartzy.com/api/, base https://api.quartzy.com). It uses a per-user `Access-Token` header and has 17 operations. The docs say it is 'generally available to all users' with an active account, and the pricing page lists 'APIs and webhooks to build your own integration' as included rather than as an add-on. Our app can read labs, types, inventory items (with instances) and order requests. It can create order requests (POST) and set an order request's status (PUT, status enum only). It can update inventory quantity, but only per instance; it cannot create, delete or move inventory items. It can also manage webhooks. There is no endpoint for comments or notes after creation, users or roles, locations, vendors, budgets, POs or invoices. Webhooks are CloudEvents v1, signed with HMAC-SHA256 in a `Signature` header, with a 3-second timeout and 3 retries at 10 s, 100 s and 1000 s. Order requests only get created, deleted, ordered and received events; there is no approved, cancelled or backordered event, so a polling job is still needed. List endpoints paginate only with `page` and return bare arrays. No rate limits or API versioning are documented. Quartzy's own duplicate protection is narrow. It warns only on an exact catalog # match against requests in the same lab in New/Approved/Ordered/Backordered status. The Add Request search also shows 'Found in Inventory' and 'Found in Request History' sections, but nothing checks personal stocks, other labs, fuzzy names or recent receipts. That gap is what our app should fill: read new requests in near real time and alert people outside Quartzy, because the API cannot add a comment to a request.
research.auth:
VERIFIED (https://docs.quartzy.com/api/, https://docs.quartzy.com/samples/curl, support article 14669414545435):
- Send the token in the `Access-Token` header, e.g. `curl -H 'Access-Token: <token>' https://api.quartzy.com/user`. The docs say: "Quartzy's API supports AccessTokens generated for specific users in an Organization."
- To create a token: Profile icon > Profile Settings > Access Tokens tab (https://app.quartzy.com/profile/access-tokens) > 'Add Access Token', then copy it.
- Who can create one: the API page says the Public APIs are "generally available to all users. If you have an active user account in Quartzy, then you can start using this API right away." No admin-only restriction is documented.
- Lab ID and Org ID: Manage Labs (gear icon next to the lab) > Developers tab (https://docs.quartzy.com/guides/org-and-lab-ids).
- The reference shows a security scheme label 'AccessToken__OAuth2' but documents no OAuth flow, client registration or scopes. Third-party catalogs (apis.io, api-evangelist) claim OAuth2 is supported; Quartzy's docs do not confirm this.

INFERRED / UNVERIFIED:
- No token scopes are documented. A token most likely acts as its user: it sees that user's labs and carries that user's Lab Admin or Lab Member permissions. Whether one token covers every lab the user belongs to is not documented.
- GET /user returns only id, first_name, last_name and email, so the API cannot tell us the user's role.
- Webhook setup in the UI needs Lab Admin, per the Slack guide ('You should be a Lab Admin of the Lab…', article 5356346153883), the Power Automate guide (article 14709172900763) and the Zapier guide (article 13890715937307). Status changes through the API (approve, cancel, order) will likely need a Lab Admin's token, since in the UI only Admins mark Ordered or cancel other people's requests (article 115000426253).
- Webhooks are scoped per lab in the UI (Manage Labs > Developers), but the API's GET /webhooks filters by organization_id.
