webhooks.details:
VERIFIED (https://docs.quartzy.com/webhooks/ and the per-event pages):
- Format: 'All Quartzy Webhooks follow the Cloud Events v1 specification.' Envelope fields are specversion '1.0', id (uuid), source 'https://quartzy.com', type, datacontenttype 'application/json', time (date-time) and data. 'Every event will contain only a single key within the data matching the resource type': data.order_request, data.inventory_item, data.type, data.sales_order, data.sales_order_item or data.shipment.
- Payloads: order_request payloads use the same fields as the API, plus `events` (an undocumented array; the example shows [null]) and `updated_by`. inventory_item payloads have included `instances` since 2026-07-01. Instance changes (for example quantity or lot) are delivered as inventory-item.updated with the full item.
- Delivery: sent as HTTP POST. 'By default, Quartzy includes an HMAC-SHA256 signature in the Signature header of all webhook requests', using a secret generated when the webhook is created. The UI shows the secret once ('This will not be accessible again', per the webhook PDF guide), but GET /webhooks/{id} documents `signing_key` in its response.
- Not documented: what bytes are signed, the encoding (hex or base64), the meaning of `is_verified`, ordering guarantees, and duplicate delivery.
- TLS: the receiver's certificate is validated for https URLs.
- Timeout and retries: 'any request taking longer than 3 seconds will be considered an error'. Responses outside 2xx are errors. Failed deliveries are retried up to 3 times, at 10 s, 100 s and 1000 s.
- Setup: in the UI under Manage Labs > Developers > 'Add webhook' (Name, URL, Event Types; options 'Flatten Output?' and 'Set null values to an Empty String?'). Lab Admin is required per the integration guides. Webhooks can also be created with POST /webhooks.

GAPS (verified by the complete event list in the 2024-12-19 changelog): there are no order-request approved, cancelled, backordered or updated events. Backordered and cancelled exist only for Quartzy Shop line items (sales-order-item.*).

UNKNOWN: whether `event_types` in POST /webhooks takes the full type string or the short form shown in the UI (for example 'sales-order.placed').
events: com.quartzy.order-request.created (fires for Quartzy Shop and non-Quartzy vendor requests)

integration_capabilities.capability: (a) Read new order requests in near real time and flag duplicates against inventory and other open requests before approval
integration_capabilities.how: Reading is supported. Subscribe to com.quartzy.order-request.created, which fires for Shop and external-vendor requests and carries item_name, vendor_name, catalog_number, quantity, unit_size, unit_price, requested_by, lab, type, spend_tracking_code and app_url. Our app compares that against its own mirror of open requests and inventory (GET /order-requests and GET /inventory-items have no search filters). Flagging inside Quartzy is not possible: there is no comment API, and notes can only be set at creation. The flag has to reach approvers through our app, Slack/Teams or email. The only in-Quartzy action is PUT /order-requests/{id} status=CANCELLED, which is drastic. Quartzy sends approver emails hourly (article 4411829390875), so an instant alert from us should usually land first (inference). Approved/cancelled changes have no webhook, so a polling job is needed to keep the 'open requests' set accurate.

integration_capabilities.capability: (b) Create order requests in Quartzy from our app
integration_capabilities.how: POST /order-requests with lab_id, type_id, name, vendor_name, catalog_number, price {amount, currency} and quantity; optionally vendor_product_id, required_before and notes. Returns 201. The body has no requested_by, unit_size, is_urgent, budget or custom request fields. Inference: the request will be attributed to the token's owner, so either use per-user tokens or deep-link users to Quartzy's Add Request form. The same pattern is used by the Benchling, SciNote and Scispot integrations.

integration_capabilities.capability: (c1) Update order request status from our app
integration_capabilities.how: PUT /order-requests/{id} with body {"status": one of CREATED, CANCELLED, APPROVED, ORDERED, BACKORDERED, RECEIVED}. Not documented: whether this respects approval workflows and role checks, or whether RECEIVED through the API creates inventory. Test in a sandbox lab with a Lab Admin token.

integration_capabilities.capability: (c2) Add comments or notes visible in Quartzy to an existing request
integration_capabilities.how: No comment endpoint exists, and PUT accepts only status. Notes can only be set at creation (POST field 'notes'). In the UI, Comments (with @mentions and email notifications) and Notes are separate, and only Notes are exported to Excel (article 115002467013). Workaround: when our app creates the request, put the duplicate-check result and a link to our app in 'notes'.

integration_capabilities.capability: (d) When items are received, create inventory in our app
integration_capabilities.how: Subscribe to com.quartzy.order-request.received; partial receipts keep the request in ORDERED until fully received (article 115005303888). Also subscribe to com.quartzy.inventory-item.created and .updated, whose payloads include instances with lot_number, expiration_date and location.pathNames, and which carry serial_number. Receiving into Quartzy inventory is optional ('Do Not Add To Inventory'), and the order-request payload has no inventory-item id. Our app should therefore treat 'received' as the trigger and match inventory events by vendor, catalog number and timing (inference). Back this up by polling for status RECEIVED.

integration_capabilities.capability: (e) Read and update Quartzy inventory quantities
integration_capabilities.how: Reading: GET /inventory-items and GET /inventory-items/{id}. Writing: quantity only, via PUT /inventory-items/{itemId}/instances/{itemInstanceId} with quantity as a string; negative or non-numeric values return 400. Labs where uses_instances is present and false use the deprecated PUT /inventory-items/{id}; treat a missing uses_instances as migrated. There is no API to create or delete items or instances, or to change location, lot, expiration or owner. Creating inventory in Quartzy still needs the UI or Excel import.

integration_capabilities.capability: (f) Bulk historical export of past orders to seed our product catalog
integration_capabilities.how: API: page through GET /order-requests?lab_id=<id>&page=1..N until an empty array comes back. Page size and ordering are undocumented, so the empty-page stop is an inference. UI: Requests > Export Requests > Filter by Date 'Submitted' + 'All Time' exports every request ever added to the lab (article 234660947); the All Labs view combines labs into one file. The Spend Dashboard also exports CSV for Admins and Members. Inventory exports to Excel one lab at a time.

integration_capabilities.capability: Detect approvals, cancellations and backorders of order requests in real time
integration_capabilities.how: There are no webhook events for these on order requests. Poll GET /order-requests and compare status and updated_at. Quartzy Shop line items do emit sales-order-item.backordered and .cancelled.

integration_capabilities.capability: Register and manage webhooks from code
integration_capabilities.how: POST /webhooks (name, url, event_types, is_enabled, is_signed); GET returns signing_key; PUT /webhooks/{id} toggles is_enabled. The docs disagree on whether to send lab_id or organization_id, so test both.

integration_capabilities.capability: Enumerate lab members and roles via API
integration_capabilities.how: Only GET /user (the token owner) exists. Inference: map people by email from requested_by, created_by, added_by and updated_by in payloads.

integration_capabilities.capability: Read or write locations, vendors, budgets, POs, invoices or custom request fields
integration_capabilities.how: There are no endpoints for these. A budget is visible read-only as spend_tracking_code.name on order requests (Quartzy renamed spend tracking codes to Budgets, per article 4411829390875). Location is visible read-only on inventory items and instances (name, pathNames).

integration_capabilities.capability: OAuth2 delegated per-user authorization for a multi-user app
integration_capabilities.how: The docs show a security label 'AccessToken__OAuth2' but document no flow. Only personal access tokens are documented. Ask support@quartzy.com.

There is no native Zapier app. Quartzy publishes templates that consume Quartzy webhooks: Zapier to Google Sheets (needs Lab Admin and a Zapier Professional, Team or Company plan), Power Automate (needs Premium connectors), Slack Workflow Builder, and Teams. All are outbound only.

integration_capabilities.capability: Native ELN/LIMS and finance integrations (Benchling, SciNote, Scispot, NetSuite, QuickBooks)
integration_capabilities.how: Benchling (add-on) syncs inventory to Benchling and creates Quartzy requests from Benchling. SciNote and Scispot are included in the Professional, Enterprise and Academic plans. NetSuite and QuickBooks are Enterprise/Academic or an add-on. These are plan-dependent and outside our app.

research.native_duplicate_detection:
YES, BUT NARROW (verified).

1) 'Duplicate request notification' (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/115003458074-Duplicate-request-notification; created and last updated Nov 2017). It is shown to members 'when they try to add a request for an item that is already in an active stage'.
- Trigger: 'if a request with the same catalog # is in the New, Approved, Ordered, or Backordered status' and only 'in the Lab where it's being requested'. A match in Received or Cancelled status does not trigger it.
- The notification 'is only based on the status of an existing request', so a two-month-old Ordered request still triggers it.
- Matching is exact catalog # only. There is no name, vendor, CAS or fuzzy match, and inventory is not checked.
- The article does not say whether the warning can be dismissed or whether approvers see it. The screenshot has no text, so the UI form (banner or popup, and whether it links to the existing request) is unknown.

2) The Add Request lookup (https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/233421407-Add-a-request-to-your-Lab) groups search results into 'Found in Request History' ('items shown here have been requested/ordered in your lab before'), 'Found in Inventory' ('items shown here exist in your lab's Inventory module'), 'Found in Quartzy Shop' (US labs only) and 'Available from other vendors'. This is passive visibility within the current lab only, and users can bypass it with 'Skip Lookup' or 'Use Request Form'. Search requires a full catalog # or item name; partial and mid-word searches don't work (article 115001974747).

3) Auto-requests from QBot do not create a second automatic request while one is in New or Pending status for the same low-stock event (article 38547448619547).

Not covered by Quartzy: other labs, since 'The contents of each lab are not shared between labs' (article 216561068); personal stocks never entered into Quartzy; requests with no or differently formatted catalog numbers; equivalent products from other vendors; recently received items sitting in someone's freezer. Mostly ~2020 reviews on Capterra/Software Advice (seen only as search snippets, pages blocked) complained that Quartzy didn't warn when someone had already requested the same undelivered item. The warning may have improved since, so test it in the lab's own instance.
order_request_statuses: UI tabs (verified, support articles): 'New' (inferred to be API CREATED), 'Approved' (only when an approval flow exists: 'New (or Approved if you have an approval flow)'), 'Ordered', 'Received'; 'Backordered' and 'Cancelled' sit under 'Other Statuses'; 'All Requests' shows everything

UI 'Pending' is used for requests awaiting approval (PO lifecycle and auto-request articles). There is no PENDING value in the API enum; it is probably reported as CREATED (unverified). No DENIED/REJECTED status is documented; a denial is probably CANCELLED (unverified)

Without an approval workflow a request goes New -> Ordered (article 4411829390875). Admins can revert Received -> New, but nothing can be reverted from Ordered, and reverting does not remove the inventory item (article 115001517327)
PO statuses (separate object, not exposed in the API): Draft, Pending, Open, Closed
research.pagination_and_rate_limits:
VERIFIED (https://docs.quartzy.com/api/):
- Pagination: list endpoints (/inventory-items, /order-requests, /labs, /types, /webhooks) take a single integer `page` parameter ('The page of results to retrieve') plus filters: lab_id; organization_id for /labs and /webhooks; name for /types.
- Responses are bare JSON arrays with no total count, next link or page-size metadata. Page size, sort order and a page-size parameter are not documented.
- There is no status, date or updated_since filter.
- Rate limits: none documented, and no 429 response is documented on any endpoint.
- ToS §3.2(f) forbids imposing 'an unreasonable or disproportionately large load on Quartzy's infrastructure', and §3.2(i) forbids access via 'spiders, robots, crawlers, data mining tools' (https://www.quartzy.com/terms-of-service).
- Versioning: none. Paths have no version prefix, and changes and deprecations are announced only in https://docs.quartzy.com/changelog (RSS/Atom available), e.g. PUT /inventory-items/{id} deprecated 2026-06-17.

INFERRED:
- Loop pages until an empty array comes back.
- Measure page size and check whether results are sorted by requested_at or updated_at. If they are not sorted, every reconciliation poll needs a full scan per lab, so poll every 10-15 minutes with exponential backoff and rely on webhooks for low latency.
- Monitor for 429/5xx responses and the Retry-After header.
research.pricing_and_access:
VERIFIED:
- Current pricing (https://www.quartzy.com/pricing):
  - Academia: $50/month billed annually, 3 users included.
  - Industry: $250/month billed annually, 5 users included.
  - Enterprise: custom price, unlimited users, PunchOut/ERP, custom SAML/OIDC.
  - 'additional seats can be added at any time'; no per-seat price is shown.
- The capabilities table says items are included 'unless marked as an add-on' and lists 'APIs and webhooks to build your own integration' as included. Also included: low-stock alerts, mobile barcode scanning, customizable approval routing, real-time spend reporting, customizable request fields, and collaboration tools (Slack, MS Teams, Google Suite, Asana).
- Add-ons: Benchling, PunchOuts, QuickBooks/NetSuite, SDS Automation, custom analytics.
- API docs: the API is 'generally available to all users' with an active account. Neither source suggests the API depends on the plan tier.
- Subscription FAQ (article 4405994277147, updated 2026-06-05): US organizations can choose Professional, Enterprise or Academic plans (these names differ from the pricing page). Price depends on plan and number of seats. There is a 14-day free trial; with no plan chosen the account goes read-only, but open orders are still fulfilled and data can still be viewed and exported.
- History: Quartzy was free for academia until July 1, 2023. The Jan 2023 blog post set $99/seat/year for existing labs and $149/seat/year for labs joining later (https://blog.quartzy.com/changes-at-quartzy-new-subscription-structure); current seat prices may differ.
- Only US labs can buy from the Quartzy Shop. The mobile app is on iOS in the US and Canada and on Android in the US only.

INFERENCE: seat count matters for a 30-person lab. If not everyone has a Quartzy seat, our app could act as the front door, but ToS §3.2(a) forbids 'the sharing of login credentials or the sharing of accounts between multiple users', so confirm with Quartzy before sending many people's requests through one token.
research.export_import_options:
VERIFIED (support.quartzy.com):

EXPORT
- Requests: Requests > Export Requests (article 234660807). Filter by status-change date (Submitted, Approved, Ordered, Received or Cancelled) and by range (All Time, Custom, Last 12 Months, This/Last Month, Quarter, Year). Three modes: (A) current view and filters, (B) date range within the current view, (C) date range regardless of view.
- Full history: 'Submitted' + 'All Time' with the checkbox unselected exports 'All requests that have ever been added to the lab' (article 234660947). The All Labs view puts all labs in one file.
- Selected requests: Group Actions > Export CSV (article 115005489868).
- Spend Dashboard: CSV export for Lab Admins and Members, filterable by Type, Lab, Month, Requester, Supplier and Budget (article 19552088311707).
- Email reports: a scheduled monthly spend report and a weekly reconciliation report (article 234438148).
- Inventory: Excel export per lab only ('There is no option to export the Inventory when viewing All Labs'), for the whole lab or the filtered set. Weekly or monthly backups can be emailed (article 234448328).
- Inventory reporting: CSV Audit Report (Event Time, Event Type, Field Name, Before, After, Event Data), Detailed Consumption Report, and Summary Consumption Report (Beginning Qty, Consumed, Restocked, Ending Qty) (article 38529710860571). The audit trail only exists from March 2024.
- Column lists for the request and inventory exports are not documented, so inspect a real export.

IMPORT (Excel templates; individual lab only, not All Labs)
- Inventory: 'Item Name' required; Amount in Stock numeric; worksheet names = Types, 31-character limit (article 234448288).
- Freezer boxes: locations must exist first; positions as Letter-Number such as A1; paths separated by '>' (article 234451328).
- Order history: Item name, Vendor, Catalog # and Quantity required; Date Ordered and Date Received as MM/DD/YYYY. Imported rows go to Ordered if not received, or to New if both dates are blank (article 233421567).
- Bulk edit of items and instances: keyed on Serial Number (article 35739193825819).
- Bulk delete: 'Delete? (Y/N)' column (article 234450488).
- Bulk new requests (article 233421187).
- Excel import is the only bulk way to create inventory in Quartzy; the API cannot create it.

native_features.name: Request lifecycle and Requests module
native_features.description: Requests move New -> (Pending/Approved if an approval flow is set) -> Ordered -> Backordered -> Received, or Cancelled. When marking Ordered, the user enters confirmation, PO and requisition numbers and fees, and requesters are emailed. Group Actions cover Mark Ordered, Receive, Cancel and Delete. Every status change is logged in the request's History. Requests can be flagged urgent.
native_features.limitations: Group actions require all selected requests to share one status. Nothing can be reverted from Ordered. Search needs a full catalog # or item name. Members can only edit or cancel their own requests while they are New.

native_features.name: Duplicate request notification
native_features.description: Warns a member adding a request when a request with the same catalog # is New, Approved, Ordered or Backordered in the same lab.
native_features.limitations: Catalog # only, same lab only, ignores inventory and received items; article dates from 2017.

native_features.name: Add Request lookup
native_features.description: Searching by term, vendor + catalog # or CAS shows 'Found in Request History', 'Found in Quartzy Shop', 'Found in Inventory' and 'Available from other vendors'. Items can be re-requested from inventory (Actions > Request) or from order history ('Request Again').
native_features.limitations: Current lab only, and users can bypass it with Skip Lookup or a blank form.

native_features.name: Request approvals
native_features.description: Configured under Lab Settings > Approvals; only Lab Admins edit it. Options: auto-approve below a threshold, multi-step approval ('+Add Step'), Approval Teams, and routing by hazardous Type, budget owner or dollar limit. Approvers get hourly emails. Separately, PO approvals use dollar tiers.
native_features.limitations: Hourly email batching. Denial behavior is not documented. PO approvals are not available for labs on QuickBooks or NetSuite.

native_features.name: Budgets (formerly spend tracking codes)
native_features.description: Lab Admins create budgets labelled Grant ID, Project, Fund or Account (one label per lab) and can assign an owner. A budget can be required on every request, used to route approvals, and copied when an item is re-requested.
native_features.limitations: No documented budget amounts, remaining balances or overspend alerts. The API exposes the budget read-only, as spend_tracking_code.name.

native_features.name: Receive into inventory and GRNs
native_features.description: Receiving offers 'Do Not Add To Inventory', 'Create New Inventory Item' or 'Update Existing Inventory Item' (the last only when the request came from inventory or request history). Partial receipts are supported. Each receipt creates an immutable Goods Received Note (GRN) PDF, and barcodes can be printed on save. The requester becomes the item owner.
native_features.limitations: Adding to inventory is optional. The help article does not list which fields carry over to the inventory item.

native_features.name: Inventory: types, custom fields, item instances
native_features.description: Each Type has standard fields plus custom fields, which can be required. Built-in types include General Supply, Chemical and Chemical - Hazardous; duplicate types can be merged. Item instances track lot, expiration, location and quantity per batch, and receiving into a matching location, lot and expiration updates that instance instead of creating a new one.
native_features.limitations: Deleting a Type deletes all its items. Labs are migrated to instances gradually (the uses_instances flag).

native_features.name: Locations and freezer boxes
native_features.description: Locations nest up to 7 levels. The last level can be a Freezer Box with a user-defined rows x columns grid and A1-style positions. An item can be copied into several cells. Box maps can be printed, and a location can be duplicated with its whole nested structure.
native_features.limitations: No documented aliquot model, cell-level volume or parent-child sample lineage. Labs not yet migrated to instances have only 2 location levels.

native_features.name: Low stock and auto-request (QBot)
native_features.description: Each item can have Min/Max stock levels. Below Min the item shows as Low Stock and its owner is emailed. 'Auto-Request When Low' makes QBot create a New request, sized up to Max or 1 by default, and it won't create another while one is New or Pending.
native_features.limitations: Needs vendor and catalog # on the item. Not available to organizations with required custom request fields or required budget codes.

native_features.name: Expiration reminders
native_features.description: 'Send Expiration Reminder' emails the item owner 1 week, 2 weeks or 1 month before expiry.

native_features.name: Audit trail and inventory reports
native_features.description: Item History tracks quantity, lot, expiration and vendor changes. Lab-wide Audit, Detailed Consumption and Summary Consumption reports export as CSV.
native_features.limitations: Logging only from March 2024. Archiving is not tracked in the consumption report.

native_features.name: Ownership and edit permissions
native_features.description: Every item has an owner who receives its notifications. A lab setting can limit edits to owners and Admins. Lab Admins can reassign owners, individually or in bulk.
native_features.limitations: Owners don't restrict visibility: 'All users in an individual Quartzy Lab can see each other's requests, orders, and inventory data.'

native_features.name: Department / shared lab pattern
native_features.description: Create a department-level lab for shared stock and invite people to both their own lab and the department lab.
native_features.limitations: 'The contents of each lab are not shared between labs. You must be a member of a lab in order to see the contents.'

native_features.name: Barcodes and mobile app
native_features.description: Quartzy generates 1D or QR labels (Avery 2x4-inch sheets, 10 per page, or label printers via Label LIVE), and USB or Bluetooth scanners work in inventory search. The mobile app scans to deduct stock, creates requests by scan, and receives orders with a packing-slip photo. Any barcode matching a catalog #, serial #, location, PO # or tracking # returns results.
native_features.limitations: Barcodes can only be generated on the web app. The app is designed for Quartzy-generated barcodes. iOS is US and Canada only; Android is US only. Sessions expire after 7 inactive days.

native_features.name: Comments vs Notes on requests
native_features.description: Comments support @mentions and email notifications, and the requester is notified automatically. Notes hold order details and are exported to Excel; comments are not.
native_features.limitations: Neither can be written through the API, except notes at creation.

native_features.name: Spend Dashboard and spend exports
native_features.description: Real-time spend by Type, Lab, Month, Requester, Supplier and Budget, with CSV export open to Admins and Members.
native_features.limitations: Spend data only; nothing on duplicates or avoided cost.

native_features.name: Quartzy Shop, quotes, PunchOut, POs and invoices
native_features.description: A marketplace with '10M+ products', quotes and offers, PunchOut for institutional eProcurement, a PO module (Draft/Pending/Open/Closed), and an Invoices module with email forwarding.
native_features.limitations: Only US labs can buy from Quartzy. POs and invoices are not in the API.

native_features.name: SDS Automation and safety details
native_features.description: Files can be attached to items (25 MB each). Safety Details hold the SDS, CAS number and hazard symbols. The paid SDS Automation add-on links manufacturer SDS files automatically.
native_features.limitations: SDS Automation is US only and a paid add-on.

native_features.name: Integrations and SSO
native_features.description: Webhook-based Slack, Teams, Zapier and Power Automate templates. Native Benchling, SciNote, Scispot, NetSuite and QuickBooks integrations. Okta, Microsoft and Google SSO on all plans; custom SAML/OIDC on Enterprise.
native_features.limitations: Many integrations are add-ons or limited to certain plans. Setup needs a Lab Admin.

gaps_our_app_fills: Cross-lab and personal visibility: Quartzy shares everything within a lab, sees nothing across labs, and has no notion of 'my personal stock' that is still discoverable. Personal inventories that were never entered into Quartzy are invisible to its duplicate check, which is the PI's core problem.

Real duplicate prevention: match on normalized catalog # with vendor aliases, CAS number, fuzzy item name, equivalent products and pack sizes; check open requests in all labs and accounts, stock on hand including personal freezers, and items received recently. Quartzy matches only an exact catalog # among active requests in the same lab.

Alerts at the moment of request: send the requester and the approver/orderer a Slack/Teams/email/in-app warning within seconds of order-request.created, before Quartzy's hourly approver email. This has to happen outside Quartzy because the API cannot write comments.

One bench-friendly search across inventory, open and in-transit orders, and purchase history, showing who has the item and its exact freezer position. Quartzy search is per module and needs a full catalog # or name.

Biological materials Quartzy lacks: cell line passage number, parental line, mycoplasma and STR test dates, vial- and aliquot-level positions, plasmid and strain metadata (none found in Quartzy's help center), all linked to the original Quartzy order.
Enforced put-away: every received order ends up with an owner and a precise location, even when Quartzy's receiver picked 'Do Not Add To Inventory'.
Quick consumption logging (scan, then -1) synced back to Quartzy instance quantities, so QBot low-stock auto-requests stay accurate without double reordering.
A report for the PI on avoided cost: duplicates caught times unit_price, repeat purchases across people, and spend per requester or budget. Quartzy reports spend but not avoided duplicates.
Mobile access outside the US/Canada, since the Quartzy mobile app is limited to those regions, if the lab is elsewhere.

features.name: Quartzy webhook ingestion service
features.description: A webhook endpoint per lab (for example FastAPI), registered via POST /webhooks or Manage Labs > Developers. Subscribe to order-request.created/ordered/received/deleted, inventory-item.created/updated/deleted, type.* and the Shop events. Verify the HMAC-SHA256 `Signature` header with hmac.compare_digest (test empirically what is signed). Return 2xx within 3 s and process asynchronously through a DB-backed queue, deduplicating on the CloudEvents `id`. Keep raw payloads for replay, and leave 'Flatten Output' off so the JSON stays nested.
features.why_it_matters: Seeing every new request in real time is the basis for stopping double orders. With a 3 s timeout and only 3 retries (10/100/1000 s), a slow handler silently loses events.

features.name: Reconciliation poller for requests and inventory
features.description: A scheduled job that pages GET /order-requests?lab_id&page=N until an empty page, upserts by id and diffs status and updated_at. This catches APPROVED, CANCELLED and BACKORDERED changes (which have no webhooks) and any missed deliveries. A nightly full mirror of GET /inventory-items, including instances, completes the picture.
features.why_it_matters: The duplicate checker needs an accurate set of open requests, and Quartzy only emits created, deleted, ordered and received for requests.

features.name: Instant duplicate alert on every new Quartzy request
features.description: On order-request.created, score the request against open requests in all labs, central and personal inventory with quantity > 0, and items received in the last N days. Match on normalized vendor + catalog_number, CAS number and fuzzy item_name (e.g. RapidFuzz token_set_ratio), allowing for different unit_size. Notify the requester and the Lab Admin/approver with the Quartzy app_url and our item page, offering 'cancel my request' or 'still needed (reason)'. Record the outcome.
features.why_it_matters: This directly targets the PI's money loss. Quartzy's native check is exact catalog #, same lab, and ignores inventory.
seen_in: Quartzy Add Request 'Found in Inventory' section

features.name: Unified 'check before you buy' search, mobile-first
features.description: One search box (scan a Quartzy or vendor barcode, or type catalog #, name or CAS) that shows in-stock items with owner and freezer > rack > box > A1 position, in-flight Quartzy requests with requester and ETA (backordered_expected_at, tracking_number), and past purchases with last price. Large buttons 'Ask owner / borrow' and 'Request in Quartzy' (deep link or API) work with gloves on.
features.why_it_matters: People double-order because they can't see personal stocks and in-flight orders. Quartzy search is per module and needs exact terms.
seen_in: Capterra reviewers asking for search across inventory and requests

features.name: In-flight orders board
features.description: A lab-wide board of CREATED, APPROVED, ORDERED and BACKORDERED requests with requester, vendor, catalog #, ETA and tracking. Quartzy Shop shipment events (sales-order-item.shipped/delivered, shipment.created/delivered) add delivery status.
features.why_it_matters: It closes the 'didn't know someone already ordered it' gap. A G2 reviewer wanted a dashboard of active, backordered and new requests.

features.name: Receive-to-inventory sync with put-away prompt
features.description: On order-request.received, create a 'pending put-away' record (item_name, vendor_name, catalog_number, quantity, unit_size, unit_price, requested_by as owner, lab). Merge in the inventory-item.created/updated payload when present (serial_number, instance lot_number, expiration_date, location.pathNames). Prompt the requester on their phone to scan the box and position. Handle partial receipts and 'Do Not Add To Inventory' receipts.
features.why_it_matters: Everything bought becomes visible and locatable, which prevents new hidden personal stocks.

features.name: Historical backfill and normalized product master
features.description: A one-time per-lab backfill from GET /order-requests (all pages), plus the UI 'Export all previously requested items' file (Submitted, All Time; the All Labs view gives one file) and inventory Excel exports. Normalize into Product (vendor, catalog_number, name, unit_size, CAS) and PurchaseHistory tables, and compute reorder intervals and 'usual buyer'.
features.why_it_matters: This seeds duplicate detection and lets us show the PI past double purchases and what they cost.

features.name: Personal inventory registry with visibility controls
features.description: A fast way for members to register personal stocks (cell lines, antibodies, kits): scan a barcode, take a photo, record the freezer position. Items are lab-visible by default with an owner contact and a 'reserved' flag. Shared stocks can optionally be mirrored to a Quartzy department or shared lab through Excel import, since the API can't create inventory.
features.why_it_matters: Quartzy visibility is all-or-nothing per lab, and stock outside Quartzy is invisible to its checks.

features.name: Quartzy credentials and webhook admin panel
features.description: Store Access-Tokens and signing secrets in a secrets store. Show the token owner (GET /user), lab IDs (GET /labs) and API health (GET /healthz). Enable or disable webhooks (PUT /webhooks/{id}). Alert if no events arrive within X hours, and support token rotation.
features.why_it_matters: Tokens act as a user, and a failed webhook would silently reopen the duplicate gap. Webhook setup needs a Lab Admin.

features.name: Approver console with Quartzy status actions
features.description: A queue of CREATED requests with a duplicate-risk badge, budget (spend_tracking_code.name), price and links. Actions call PUT /order-requests/{id} with status APPROVED or CANCELLED using a Lab Admin token, and each action is audit-logged with a reason. First confirm in a test lab whether the API respects approval workflows.
features.why_it_matters: It puts the duplicate signal where the decision is made. Quartzy can't display our flags because the API has no comments.

features.name: Create Quartzy requests from our app
features.description: POST /order-requests (lab_id, type_id from GET /types, name, vendor_name, catalog_number, price, quantity, required_before, notes with our duplicate-check summary and link), only after the duplicate check passes. Prefer per-user tokens for correct attribution; otherwise deep-link to Quartzy's Add Request.
features.why_it_matters: The duplicate check then happens before the request exists. Caveats: no requested_by, budget, unit_size or urgency in the API, and a possible ToS issue with shared accounts.
seen_in: Benchling, SciNote and Scispot integrations create Quartzy requests

features.name: Two-way quantity sync for Quartzy-tracked items
features.description: Consumption logged in our app is mirrored with PUT /inventory-items/{itemId}/instances/{itemInstanceId} (quantity as a string) for migrated labs, falling back to the deprecated PUT /inventory-items/{id} where uses_instances is false. Suppress echo loops from inventory-item.updated, and resolve conflicts with updated_at.
features.why_it_matters: Keeps Quartzy low-stock and QBot auto-requests accurate, so the two systems don't both reorder.

features.name: Avoided-cost and spend analytics for the PI
features.description: Monthly report of duplicates caught (unit_price x quantity), repeat buys across people, spend by type, requester and budget, and top reordered products, with CSV export.
features.why_it_matters: Shows the return on the app and keeps people using it. Quartzy's Spend Dashboard doesn't measure duplicates.

features.name: Targeted Slack/Teams/email notifications
features.description: Arrival notices that include the storage location, duplicate warnings, backorder alerts and a daily digest for the Lab Admin, with per-user settings.
features.why_it_matters: Reviewers complain that Quartzy sends a lot of email, so fewer, targeted alerts work better for bench scientists.

features.name: Type/category mapping sync
features.description: Sync GET /types and the type.created/updated/deleted webhooks, and map Quartzy Types (e.g. General Supply, Chemical - Hazardous, Antibody, Cell Line) to our richer schemas.
features.why_it_matters: POST needs a type_id, and Type drives hazardous-item approval routing.

features.name: Barcode interoperability with Quartzy labels
features.description: Our scanner resolves Quartzy 1D/QR labels by serial_number and vendor barcodes by catalog #. Our app prints its own labels for vials and aliquots that Quartzy doesn't model.
features.why_it_matters: The lab keeps its existing Quartzy labels and avoids double labeling.

features.name: Cell line and aliquot extensions linked to Quartzy orders
features.description: Track passage number, parental line, source catalog # (e.g. ATCC), mycoplasma and STR dates, vial positions and aliquot splits, each linked to the Quartzy order or item it came from.
features.why_it_matters: Cell lines are among the items being double-ordered, and Quartzy treats them only as a generic Type.
seen_in: Gap found in Quartzy help-center search

features.name: QBot auto-request coordination
features.description: Recognize requests created by QBot (creator identity inferred) and suppress our own reorder suggestions for those items. Warn when a person requests an item that already has an open QBot request.
features.why_it_matters: Avoids a new duplicate source when Quartzy auto-requests are switched on.

caveats: support.quartzy.com HTML pages returned 403 to the fetcher, so articles were read through the public Zendesk Help Center JSON API (/api/v2/help_center/en-us/articles/<id>.json). Same content, but quotes are short excerpts.

Inconsistencies in Quartzy's own docs: POST /webhooks schema requires lab_id while the sample sends organization_id. The 404 text for inventory and lab endpoints says 'No matching Order Request'. The help article on instances (updated 2026-10-08) still calls API and webhook support 'upcoming', but the developer changelog says it shipped on 2026-06-17 (API) and 2026-07-01 (webhooks).
Webhook signature details are undocumented (what is signed, hex or base64 encoding), and so is the meaning of is_verified. Test against a real delivery before enforcing verification.
It is unknown whether `event_types` in POST /webhooks takes the full string (com.quartzy.order-request.created) or the short UI form (e.g. sales-order.placed).
No order-request webhook exists for approved, cancelled, backordered or updated, so polling is required. Undocumented ordering and page size may force full scans.
Webhooks give up after 3 retries spread over about 18.5 minutes. A receiver outage longer than that loses events unless the poller backfills.

The API cannot add comments, change notes after creation, set the requester or budget, read or write custom request fields, create, delete or move inventory, or list users, locations, vendors, POs or invoices.

Inference: requests created with a shared service token will probably show that account as requester. ToS §3.2(a) forbids 'the sharing of login credentials or the sharing of accounts between multiple users', so confirm the integration design with support@quartzy.com.
It is undocumented whether PUT status changes respect Quartzy approval workflows and member/admin permissions, or whether status=RECEIVED via the API touches inventory. Test in a sandbox lab.
Receiving into Quartzy inventory is optional, and order-request payloads carry no inventory-item id, so linking orders to inventory needs heuristic matching.

Labs are being migrated to instances (uses_instances). In migrated labs the parent lot, expiration and location fields are empty and slated for removal, and a missing uses_instances must be treated as migrated, not as false.
Money and quantity values arrive as strings (price.amount, quantity); parse with Decimal.
The duplicate request notification article dates from 2017. Current in-app behavior may differ, so test it in the lab's Quartzy.
Regional limits: Shop buying is US-only, SDS Automation is US-only, and the mobile app is iOS US/Canada and Android US only. The lab's country is unknown.

The pricing page names plans Academia/Industry/Enterprise while help articles say Academic/Professional/Enterprise. Seat prices for 30 users aren't published; the $99/$149 per seat per year figures are from 2023.
Claims that Quartzy supports OAuth2 come only from third-party catalogs (apis.io, api-evangelist) and are unverified by Quartzy's docs.

ToS §3.2(i) and §3.2(e) forbid robots/crawlers and tools that 'enable features or functionalities that are otherwise disabled'. Use only the public API and webhooks, with no scraping and no browser overlays without asking Quartzy.
User sentiment from Capterra, G2 and Software Advice was seen only through search snippets (pages blocked; Reddit not reachable), and many reviews are from around 2020.
