verification.overall_assessment:
Most of the researcher's claims hold up. I checked them against Quartzy's machine-readable OpenAPI file (https://docs.quartzy.com/redocusaurus/public-api.yaml, the download link on the API reference page), the per-event webhook pages, the changelog, the official webhook PDF guide, and about 50 help-center articles. The help-center HTML returns 403, so I read those articles through Quartzy's public Zendesk JSON API.

What the duplicate-prevention design depends on is confirmed:
- **Endpoints:** all 17 endpoints exist with the documented fields.
- **List filters:** list endpoints filter only by page and lab_id (organization_id for /labs and /webhooks, name for /types). There is no status, updated_since or per_page filter.
- **Responses and limits:** responses are bare arrays, and no rate limits or 429 responses are documented.
- **Inventory writes:** the only inventory write is a quantity PUT. There are no DELETE operations at all.
- **Statuses:** the status enum is exactly CREATED, CANCELLED, APPROVED, ORDERED, BACKORDERED, RECEIVED, with no PENDING, DENIED or REJECTED.
- **Webhook events:** the 17 webhook event strings are exact. There is no order-request approved, cancelled, updated or backordered event; the docs pages for approved, cancelled and updated return 404.
- **Webhook delivery:** the HMAC-SHA256 'Signature' header, the 3-second timeout and the retries at 10 s, 100 s and 1000 s are all confirmed.
- **Native duplicate warning:** it matches only on catalog #, only within the same lab, and only against requests in New, Approved, Ordered or Backordered, regardless of how old they are.

Errors and outdated claims:
1. **OAuth2 (refuted).** 'AccessToken__OAuth2' is two separate scheme labels run together when the page was converted to text. The official spec declares an OAuth2 authorization-code flow (https://auth0.quartzy.com/authorize and /oauth/token, scopes {}) as an alternative to the Access-Token header on every operation. Getting a client_id is undocumented.
2. **POST /webhooks lab_id vs organization_id (not a docs inconsistency).** The request schema accepts either a lab_id+url body or an organization_id+url body, so organization-wide webhooks can be created.
3. **Slack (outdated).** The help-center article, updated 2026-10-16, now describes a native 'Add to Slack' app, not the older Workflow Builder template.
4. **Smaller corrections.** The mobile-app country limits are contradicted by another official article. The March 2024 audit-trail start comes from article 26276073436955, not 38529710860571. Inventory export columns are partly documented.

Inference-based claims stay unverifiable. These are: token role inheritance, whether API status changes need an Admin token, who requests are attributed to, how 'Pending' and denials map to API statuses, and whether the duplicate warning normalizes catalog numbers.

Design-critical facts the researcher missed:
- **Required fields.** Labs can make the Budget field and custom request fields required. POST /order-requests can set neither, and its body rejects unknown properties (additionalProperties: false).
- **Price units.** Money.amount is a string with format integer, and whether it is in cents or dollars is undocumented.
- **New request channel.** The Quartzy Connect Chrome extension (Sep 2026) lets any user create requests from any vendor page, with no documented duplicate check.
- **Deleted is not cancelled.** order-request.deleted covers only Admin hard-deletes, never cancellations.
- **Instance rollout.** Inventory item instances are rolling out only to labs without inventory integrations.
- **Terms of service.** §3.2(a) frames account sharing as fee circumvention, which matters if one token stands in for 30 people.

Test in a sandbox lab before building on these: the event_types string format, the Money units, API behavior when budget or custom fields are required, and role enforcement on PUT /order-requests/{id}.

claims.claim: AUTH: An API is available. Docs are at https://docs.quartzy.com/api/ and the base URL is https://api.quartzy.com.
claims.evidence: The API reference lists 17 operations. The OpenAPI file it links for download (public-api.yaml) declares one server, `https://api.quartzy.com` (Production). Paths have no version prefix.

claims.claim: AUTH: The token is sent in the `Access-Token` header (curl -H 'Access-Token: <token>' https://api.quartzy.com/user). 'Quartzy's API supports AccessTokens generated for specific users in an Organization.'
claims.evidence: Spec: components.securitySchemes.AccessToken = {type: apiKey, in: header, name: Access-Token}. The API page has the quote verbatim, plus 'Provide this AccessToken to your API calls under the `Access-Token` header'. The curl sample is `curl -X GET -H 'Access-Token: some-access-token' https://api.quartzy.com/user` and the Python sample uses headers = {'Access-Token': 'some-access-token'}.

claims.claim: AUTH: To create a token, go to Profile icon > Profile Settings > Access Tokens tab (https://app.quartzy.com/profile/access-tokens) > Add Access Token, then copy it.
claims.evidence: Article 14669414545435 (updated 2026-02-09): 'Click on your profile icon in the upper right corner and click Profile Settings.' and 'Click the Access Tokens tab, then click Add Access Token.' On the API page, the 'AccessToken Settings' link points to https://app.quartzy.com/profile/access-tokens. No token expiry, revocation process or token-count limit is documented.

claims.claim: AUTH: The API is 'generally available to all users. If you have an active user account in Quartzy, then you can start using this API right away.' No admin-only restriction is documented.
claims.evidence: The quote appears on the API page and in the spec's info.description ('Quartzy's Public APIs listed here are generally available to all users.'). Article 14669414545435 states no role requirement for creating tokens.

claims.claim: AUTH: Lab ID and Org ID are found under Manage Labs (gear icon next to the lab) > Developers tab.
claims.evidence: Docs guide: 'open the Lab selection menu and click the gear icon next to the appropriate Lab' and 'The Lab ID and Organization ID will be displayed at the top of the Developers page.' No role requirement is stated.

claims.claim: AUTH: The reference shows a security scheme labeled 'AccessToken__OAuth2' but documents no OAuth flow, client registration or scopes. Only third-party catalogs say OAuth2 is supported; Quartzy's docs do not.
claims.evidence: The official OpenAPI file defines two separate schemes. AccessToken is {type: apiKey, in: header, name: Access-Token}. OAuth2 is {type: oauth2, flows: authorizationCode: {authorizationUrl: https://auth0.quartzy.com/authorize, tokenUrl: https://auth0.quartzy.com/oauth/token, scopes: {}}}. Each operation lists `security: - AccessToken: [] - OAuth2: []`, which means either one is accepted. 'AccessToken__OAuth2' is the two italic labels joined when the Redoc page was converted to markdown; it is not a scheme name.
claims.correction: Quartzy's own spec does declare OAuth2 (authorization-code flow, empty scopes) as an alternative to Access-Token. Not documented: client registration (client_id/secret), redirect URIs and token lifetimes. The live discovery document at https://auth0.quartzy.com/.well-known/openid-configuration lists authorization_code, refresh_token and PKCE S256, but that is observed behavior, not documentation. Ask support@quartzy.com for a client.

claims.claim: AUTH (inferred): No token scopes exist. A token acts as its user with that user's Lab Admin or Member permissions. Whether one token covers all of the user's labs is undocumented.
claims.evidence: The missing scopes are confirmed: the spec has `scopes: {}` and no scope text. Nothing official describes role inheritance or how many labs a token covers. That GET /labs accepts an organization_id filter suggests one token can list several labs, but this is inference.

claims.claim: AUTH: GET /user returns only id, first_name, last_name and email, so the API cannot reveal the user's role.
claims.evidence: The spec's User schema is {id, first_name, last_name, email}. None of the 29 schemas contains a role, membership or member field.

claims.claim: AUTH: Setting up a webhook in the UI needs Lab Admin, per the Slack (5356346153883), Power Automate (14709172900763) and Zapier (13890715937307) guides.
claims.evidence: Slack: 'You should be a Lab Admin of the Lab you'd for which you'd like to configure notifications.' Power Automate lists the 'Lab Admin' role as required. Zapier lists 'Quartzy: Lab Admin role'. The Teams article (13921305119643) and the Benchling setup guide (12312389576731) also require Lab Admin. Caveat: the generic Webhooks Management article (14848438327067) and the docs.quartzy.com guides give no role requirement, so this is a stated prerequisite rather than a documented permission rule.

claims.claim: AUTH: In the UI, only Admins can mark requests Ordered or cancel other people's requests (article 115000426253).
claims.evidence: Lab Admin vs. Lab Member table (updated 2026-06-24): Mark Ordered is Admin-only. Both roles can 'Cancel requests in New status submitted by themselves'. Only Admins can 'Cancel requests in any status before received submitted by any member'. Both roles can Mark Received. 'Members can approve requests when an approval step is created (by an Admin) with them as the approver.' Separately, 115001517327 says 'Members can't revert the status of a request.'
claims.correction: Members can also mark Received, and can approve when an Admin names them as the approver.

claims.claim: AUTH (inferred): Changing status through the API (approve, cancel, order) will need a Lab Admin's token.
claims.evidence: PUT /order-requests/{id} documents only 200/401/404/500. No 403 is listed, and nothing describes role checks or whether approval workflows are enforced through the API. This must be tested.

claims.claim: AUTH: Webhooks are set up per lab in the UI (Manage Labs > Developers), but GET /webhooks filters by organization_id.
claims.evidence: GET /webhooks (webhookList) takes only organization_id (uuid) and page; it has no lab_id filter. Article 14848438327067 describes adding webhooks in the Developers tab of each lab. The spec's CreateWebhook is also a oneOf of a lab_id body or an organization_id body, so the API can create organization-wide webhooks too.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT GET /healthz: health check; 200 = healthy, 500 = unhealthy.
claims.evidence: operationId 'health'. Responses: 200 'healthy' and 500 'unhealthy' (Health schema, sample `{ }`). The operation has no `security` key, so it is unauthenticated.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT GET /user: returns the token owner; id, first_name, last_name, email; 200/401/404/500.
claims.evidence: operationId 'me'. Responses: 200, 401, 404 ('No matching user') and 500. The body is the User schema.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT GET /labs: query organization_id (uuid) and page; fields id, name, uses_instances, organization{id,name}; bare JSON array.
claims.evidence: operationId 'labList'. The 200 response is `type: array, items: $ref Lab`. Lab.uses_instances is boolean with the description 'Temporary field during the inventory item instances rollout.'

claims.claim: ENDPOINT GET /labs/{id}: returns one lab.
claims.evidence: operationId 'labRetrieve'; path id is a required uuid. Responses: 200/401/404/500. The 404 description 'No matching Order Request' is a copy-paste error in the docs.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT GET /types: query lab_id (uuid), name ('The Type Name to filter on') and page; fields id, name, lab{...}. A type_id is required to create order requests.
claims.evidence: operationId 'typeList'. The name parameter's description is exactly 'The Type Name to filter on'. Items are TypeWithLab. CreateOrderRequest.required includes type_id.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT GET /inventory-items: query page and lab_id only (no search); instances[] include only active instances; in migrated labs the parent lot, expiration, location and sublocation are empty and parent quantity = sum of instances; no owner field.
claims.evidence: operationId 'inventoryItemList'. Parameters are only page (integer) and lab_id (string, 'The Lab ID to filter on'). All listed fields are present. Instances use the InventorySubitem schema {id uuid, quantity string, expiration_date nullable date, lot_number nullable, location nullable}. The guide says the array 'includes only active instances', that in migrated labs the parent fields 'are deprecated and always empty' (deprecated: true in the spec), and that parent quantity 'represents the sum of the item's active instance quantities'. There is no `owner` property. quantity and price are nullable strings.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT GET /inventory-items/{id}: same schema as the list; 404 if not found.
claims.evidence: operationId 'inventoryItemRetrieve'. Responses: 200/401/404/500. The 404 description wrongly reads 'No matching Order Request'.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT PUT /inventory-items/{id}: DEPRECATED quantity update (body quantity as a string), deprecated in the 2026-06-17 changelog; use only where uses_instances is present and false.
claims.evidence: The spec marks it `deprecated: true`; the body is {quantity: string} with additionalProperties: false. The API page says 'Deprecated in favor of Update inventory item instance quantity' and 'This endpoint remains available for labs that have not been migrated'. Changelog 2026-06-17: 'Update inventory item quantity (PUT /inventory-items/{id}) is deprecated in favor of the instance endpoint.' The guide says to use it only when uses_instances is present and false, and to treat a missing field as migrated.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT PUT /inventory-items/{itemId}/instances/{itemInstanceId}: sets an instance's quantity (string); 400 for invalid input; returns the full parent item; the only inventory write.
claims.evidence: operationId 'inventoryItemInstanceUpdate'. The 400 reads 'Invalid request (e.g. malformed body, non-numeric quantity, negative quantity)'. The guide says the response returns the full parent item including the updated `instances` array. The spec has no other inventory write: no POST for inventory, and no DELETE operation anywhere in the API.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT GET /order-requests: query page and lab_id only (no status, date or updated_since filter); listed fields; no link to an inventory item and no custom request fields.
claims.evidence: operationId 'orderRequestList'. A search of the spec finds no status query parameter and no 'updated_since', 'per_page' or 'limit'. The response is OrderRequests (an array of OrderRequestWithType). Fields match the claim, including spend_tracking_code{name}, backordered_expected_at and is_urgent. In responses, quantity, unit_price and unit_size are nullable strings.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT POST /order-requests: required lab_id, type_id, name, vendor_name, catalog_number, price (Money), quantity (integer); optional vendor_product_id, required_before, notes; returns 201; cannot send requested_by, unit_size, is_urgent, budget or custom fields.
claims.evidence: operationId 'orderRequestCreate'. The required list matches. quantity is an integer and required_before is a date. Money is {amount: string with format integer, currency: string}, and both are required. CreateOrderRequest has `additionalProperties: false`, so extra fields cannot be sent and may be rejected. Responses: 201/401/500.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT GET /order-requests/{id}: returns one request; 404 'No matching Order Request'.
claims.evidence: operationId 'orderRequestRetrieve'. Responses: 200/401/404/500.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT PUT /order-requests/{id}: status is the only writable field (enum CREATED|CANCELLED|APPROVED|ORDERED|BACKORDERED|RECEIVED); sample {"status": "CREATED"}; 200/401/404/500.
claims.evidence: operationId 'orderRequestUpdate'. The UpdateOrderRequest schema has the status enum and `additionalProperties: false`. The sample matches. How it interacts with approval workflows is not documented.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT GET /webhooks: query organization_id and page; fields id, name, url, event_types, is_enabled, is_verified, is_signed.
claims.evidence: operationId 'webhookList'. The spec's Webhook schema also includes signing_key (string, nullable: true), though the rendered sample omits it.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT POST /webhooks: the schema requires lab_id and url, but the request sample sends organization_id instead (a docs inconsistency).
claims.evidence: In the spec, CreateWebhook is a `oneOf` of two objects. One requires [lab_id, url] and the other requires [organization_id, url]. Both accept name, event_types (an array of strings with no enum), is_enabled, is_verified and is_signed. Redoc shows only the first variant, and the sample uses the second. The 201 response is a Webhook including signing_key.
claims.correction: This is not an inconsistency. Both a lab-scoped (lab_id) and an organization-scoped (organization_id) webhook body are valid by design. Still undocumented: what is_verified means and whether is_signed=false turns off signatures.

claims.claim: ENDPOINT GET /webhooks/{id}: the response includes signing_key.
claims.evidence: operationId 'webhookRetrieve'. Webhook.signing_key is {type: string, nullable: true}. Because the UI says the secret 'will not be accessible again', the API may return null here (inference; test it).

claims.claim: ENDPOINT PUT /webhooks/{id}: enables or disables a webhook (body is_enabled boolean).
claims.evidence: operationId 'webhookUpdate'. UpdateWebhook accepts only is_enabled, with `additionalProperties: false`, so the API cannot change a webhook's url or event_types. There is no DELETE /webhooks.

claims.claim: WEBHOOK: Events follow Cloud Events v1. Envelope: specversion '1.0', id (uuid), source 'https://quartzy.com', type, datacontenttype 'application/json', time, data. data has a single key matching the resource type.
claims.evidence: The overview says 'All Quartzy Webhooks follow the Cloud Events v1' and 'Every event will contain only a single key within the data matching the resource type for the given event.' The per-event pages mark all envelope fields required with those values. The data keys are order_request, inventory_item, type, sales_order, sales_order_item and shipment.

claims.claim: WEBHOOK: order_request payloads carry the API fields plus `events` (undocumented; the example shows [null]) and `updated_by`.
claims.evidence: The order-request created, ordered, received and deleted pages list updated_by and events, with example `[ null ]`. The API's OrderRequest schema has neither. The spec also contains an OrderRequestEvent schema that nothing references: {type (required string), comment (nullable string), created_at (date-time), created_by (User)}. It may be the element type of `events` (inference).

claims.claim: WEBHOOK: inventory_item payloads have included instances since 2026-07-01, and instance changes arrive as inventory-item.updated with the full item.
claims.evidence: The 2026-07-01 changelog entry says instances are now in inventory-item payloads for create, update and delete. The guide says instance changes are 'delivered as `inventory-item.updated` with the full inventory item payload', 'not only the instance that changed'.

claims.claim: WEBHOOK: Delivered by HTTP POST. 'By default, Quartzy includes an HMAC-SHA256 signature in the Signature header of all webhook requests', using a secret generated when the webhook is created.
claims.evidence: The overview has that quote verbatim, plus 'When creating a webhook, a secret will be generated and displayed to the user.' The official PDF guide says webhooks 'receive events as HTTP POST requests'.

claims.claim: WEBHOOK: The UI shows the secret once ('This will not be accessible again'), but GET /webhooks/{id} documents signing_key.
claims.evidence: The 'New webhook' modal screenshot in the official PDF guide reads: 'New webhook created. Copy and use the secret key provided here. This will not be accessible again.' The spec has Webhook.signing_key as a nullable string.

claims.claim: WEBHOOK: Not documented: what bytes are signed, the encoding (hex or base64), what is_verified means, ordering, and duplicate delivery.
claims.evidence: The webhooks page covers none of these. In the spec, is_verified and is_signed are booleans with no descriptions. The curl, NodeJS and Python samples contain no verification code.

claims.claim: WEBHOOK: TLS certificates are validated for https URLs; requests over 3 s count as errors; non-2xx responses are errors; up to 3 retries at 10 s, 100 s and 1000 s.
claims.evidence: Quotes: 'any request taking longer than 3 seconds will be considered an error'; 'a status code in the 200-299 range'; 'The first retry will be attempted after 10 seconds, the second after 100 seconds, and the third after 1000 seconds.'; Quartzy 'will validate the TLS Certificate of the server'.

claims.claim: WEBHOOK: UI setup is Manage Labs > Developers > 'Add webhook' (Name, URL, Event Types), with options 'Flatten Output?' and 'Set null values to an Empty String?'.
claims.evidence: Article 14848438327067: 'Developers tab in the Manage Labs section', 'Add webhook', with Name, URL and Event Types mandatory. The Zapier article 13890715937307 and the docs Slack guide name both options. The Power Automate article notes 'only one Event Type can be selected' for that flow.

claims.claim: WEBHOOK: The 17 events are: com.quartzy.order-request.{created,deleted,ordered,received}; com.quartzy.inventory-item.{created,updated,deleted}; com.quartzy.type.{created,updated,deleted}; com.quartzy.sales-order.placed; com.quartzy.sales-order-item.{shipped,delivered,backordered,cancelled}; com.quartzy.shipment.{created,delivered}.
claims.evidence: Each per-event page gives that exact `type` value. The type events use 'com.quartzy.type.*', not inventory-type. The 2024-12-19 changelog lists the same 17. Docs errors: the shipment.delivered page says 'Occurs when a new Inventory Item is delivered', and the overview links a wrong path, /webhooks/sales-order-item/shipped.

claims.claim: WEBHOOK: com.quartzy.order-request.created fires for both Quartzy Shop and non-Quartzy vendor requests.
claims.evidence: 'This event is generated for items requested from both the Quartzy Shop or any non-Quartzy vendor.'

claims.claim: WEBHOOK GAP: There are no order-request approved, cancelled, backordered or updated events. Backordered and cancelled exist only for Quartzy Shop line items.
claims.evidence: The docs sidebar under Order Request lists only Created, Deleted, Ordered and Received. https://docs.quartzy.com/webhooks/order-request/approved, /cancelled and /updated all return HTTP 404. The later changelog entries (2026-06-17, 2026-07-01) add no events. Caveat: the 2024-12-19 entry does not say it is a complete list; completeness rests on the current docs. Also, order-request.deleted covers Admin hard-deletes, not cancellations ('Deleting a request will delete it for everyone in the Lab', 115007069047).

claims.claim: WEBHOOK UNKNOWN: Whether event_types in POST /webhooks takes the full type string or the short UI form (e.g. 'sales-order.placed').
claims.evidence: It is indeed undocumented. The spec defines event_types as an array of strings with no enum. Screenshots in the official PDF show the UI checkboxes labeled with short codes ('sales-order.placed', 'sales-order-item.shipped', 'sales-order-item.delivered', 'sales-order-item.cancelled'). Test both forms.

claims.claim: PAGINATION: List endpoints take one integer `page` ('The page of results to retrieve') plus filters (lab_id; organization_id for /labs and /webhooks; name for /types). Responses are bare arrays with no total, next link or page size. There is no status, date or updated_since filter.
claims.evidence: Every list operation's page parameter has the description 'The page of results to retrieve'. Every 200 response is `type: array`. The strings per_page, limit and updated_since do not appear in the spec. Page size and sort order are undocumented.

claims.claim: RATE LIMITS: None documented, and no 429 response on any endpoint.
claims.evidence: The spec contains no 429 and no rate-limit text. The only error body is the Error schema {message: string}.

claims.claim: ToS §3.2(f) forbids imposing 'an unreasonable or disproportionately large load', and §3.2(i) forbids 'spiders, robots, crawlers, data mining tools'.
claims.evidence: Terms dated 'Last Revision: March 9, 2026'. Both phrases appear verbatim. §3.2(e) also forbids working 'around any technical limitations in the Services' and reverse engineering. There are no separate API terms; the spec's info.termsOfService points to this page.

claims.claim: VERSIONING: There is none. Changes and deprecations are announced only in the changelog (RSS/Atom available).
claims.evidence: Paths have no version prefix and the spec shows no usable version. The changelog offers /changelog/rss.xml and /changelog/atom.xml and has 3 entries (2024-12-19, 2026-06-17, 2026-07-01). The word 'only' is inference: help-center articles also announce changes.

claims.claim: STATUSES: The API enum is CREATED, APPROVED, ORDERED, BACKORDERED, RECEIVED, CANCELLED.
claims.evidence: Both UpdateOrderRequest.status and the response's OrderRequest.status enum are exactly CREATED, CANCELLED, APPROVED, ORDERED, BACKORDERED, RECEIVED. 'PENDING', 'DENIED' and 'REJECTED' appear nowhere in the spec.

claims.claim: STATUSES: UI tabs are 'New', 'Approved' (only with an approval flow: 'New (or Approved if you have an approval flow)'), 'Ordered' and 'Received'; Backordered and Cancelled are under 'Other Statuses'; 'All Requests' shows everything.
claims.evidence: Article 7342760442907 (Mark requests as Ordered): 'select New (or Approved if you have an approval flow) in the status navigation bar'. Articles 115001974747 and 234660707 describe the Other Statuses menu (Backordered, Cancelled) and All Requests. That New maps to CREATED is inference.

claims.claim: STATUSES: The UI's 'Pending' means awaiting approval, and the API probably reports it as CREATED.
claims.evidence: Articles 38547448619547 ('already in New or Pending status') and 37075848397595 (requests 'will remain in a Pending or Approved state') use 'Pending' for requests but never define it. The only defined Pending is the PO status 'PO is awaiting approval'. There is also a 'Pending Cancellation' status for Quartzy Shop orders, which stays in the Ordered tab (360006135354). How either maps to the API is undocumented.

claims.claim: STATUSES: There is no DENIED or REJECTED status; a denial is probably CANCELLED.
claims.evidence: No official text says what happens when an approver denies a request; 4411829390875 does not cover it. The spec has no such values.

claims.claim: STATUSES: Without an approval workflow, a request goes New -> Ordered (article 4411829390875).
claims.evidence: 'a request goes from New to Ordered'. The article also says approver emails 'are sent on an hourly basis at the top of the hour'.

claims.claim: STATUSES: Admins can revert Received -> New; nothing can be reverted from Ordered; reverting does not remove the inventory item (article 115001517327).
claims.evidence: 'Admins can revert the status of requests from Received all the way back to New.' 'Quartzy requests cannot be reverted from the Ordered status.' 'reverting the status does not remove the item from the Inventory.'

claims.claim: STATUSES: Purchase orders have statuses Draft, Pending, Open and Closed, and are not exposed in the API.
claims.evidence: Article 37075848397595 defines Draft ('created, but not yet submitted for approval'), Pending ('PO is awaiting approval'), Open ('PO has been approved') and Closed ('PO has been fully received or cancelled'). The spec has no PO paths or schemas; SalesOrder is a Quartzy Shop order, not a PO. 'PO generation' is an add-on on the pricing page.

claims.claim: DUPLICATES: A 'Duplicate request notification' exists (article 115003458074, created and last updated Nov 2017). It is shown 'when they try to add a request for an item that is already in an active stage'.
claims.evidence: Zendesk metadata: created_at 2017-11-08T19:34:37Z, updated_at 2017-11-08T19:36:42Z. The body contains 'already in an active stage of the ordering process'.

claims.claim: DUPLICATES: It triggers only for a request with the same catalog # in New, Approved, Ordered or Backordered, in the lab where the new request is made. Received and Cancelled do not trigger it. It depends only on status, so an old Ordered request keeps triggering it.
claims.evidence: Quotes: 'a request with the same catalog # is in the New, Approved, Ordered, or Backordered status'; 'in the Lab where it's being requested.'; 'The notification is only based on the status of an existing request'.

claims.claim: DUPLICATES: Matching is on exact catalog # only, with no name, vendor, CAS or fuzzy matching, and inventory is not checked.
claims.evidence: The article mentions only catalog # and the status of existing requests. It never mentions inventory, item names, vendors, CAS numbers or how catalog numbers are normalized (case, spaces, dashes). 'Exact' and the exclusions are inferred from what the article leaves out. Test variants such as '12-345' vs '12345'.

claims.claim: DUPLICATES: It is undocumented whether the warning can be dismissed, whether approvers see it, or what form it takes; the screenshot has no text.
claims.evidence: The body never mentions dismissing, overriding, approvers or a link to the existing request. Its single image has alt text 'duplicate_request.png'.

claims.claim: DUPLICATES: The Add Request lookup groups results into 'Found in Request History', 'Found in Inventory', 'Found in Quartzy Shop' (US only) and 'Available from other vendors'. Users can bypass it with 'Skip Lookup' or 'Use Request Form'. It shows only the current lab's items.
claims.evidence: Article 233421407 (updated 2026-10-13): 'items shown here have been requested/ordered in your lab before'; 'exist in your lab's Inventory module as an inventory item'; '(US labs only)'; 'Skip Lookup', 'Use Request Form'. Nuance: the lookup searches 'all of Quartzy'; only the Request History and Inventory groups are limited to your lab. The article does not mention a duplicate warning.

claims.claim: DUPLICATES: Search needs a full catalog # or item name; partial and mid-word searches don't work (article 115001974747).
claims.evidence: 'Search and filter in Requests' (updated 2026-04-14): 'For best results, search a complete Catalog #, the full Item Name, or include multiple terms.' and 'Partial searches will not work, nor text that appears at the end or in the middle of a word.'
claims.correction: This article covers searching the Requests list, not the Add Request lookup. How the lookup matches is not documented.

claims.claim: DUPLICATES: QBot does not create a second automatic request while one for the same low-stock event is in New or Pending (article 38547448619547).
claims.evidence: 'If an automatically created request is already in New or Pending status, a subsequent request will not be created' and 'All automatically generated requests will be created from QBot.' Also: organizations with required custom request fields 'do not yet have access to automatic requests'.

claims.claim: DUPLICATES: 'The contents of each lab are not shared between labs' (article 216561068).
claims.evidence: 'User Tip: Using Quartzy as a Department' (updated 2024-06-18): 'The contents of each lab are not shared between labs.' and 'a member of one lab won't be able to see the contents of other labs.'

claims.claim: DUPLICATES: Mostly ~2020 Capterra/Software Advice reviews complained that Quartzy didn't warn when someone had already requested the same undelivered item.
claims.evidence: These are not official sources, and my search found no such review text. One Software Advice review credits seeing others' orders with helping avoid duplicates.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION (a): Reading new requests in near real time and flagging duplicates is partially supported (read via webhook; no way to flag inside Quartzy except cancelling; polling needed for approve/cancel).
claims.evidence: The order-request.created payload fields are verified. There is no comment endpoint. UpdateOrderRequest accepts only status (additionalProperties: false). Notes can only be set on POST. Approver emails go out hourly ('on an hourly basis at the top of the hour', 4411829390875). There are no approved or cancelled webhooks. That our alert arrives first is inference.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION (b): Creating order requests from our app is supported via POST /order-requests. Requests are attributed to the token owner (inferred). The Benchling, SciNote and Scispot integrations work the same way.
claims.evidence: POST /order-requests is verified. Attribution to the token owner is unverifiable: there is no requested_by input and the body has additionalProperties: false. Benchling: 'Create new order requests in Quartzy without leaving Benchling' (12513786309403). Scispot: users can create order requests from Scispot (12514492535579).
claims.correction: The SciNote article (23258636712603) describes only 'access your Quartzy inventory directly from SciNote', not creating requests. Also, labs can make Budget required ('Make field required', 115003242028) and organizations can make custom request fields required (4407114944155). POST cannot carry either, and what the API does in that case is undocumented.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION (c1): Updating order-request status via PUT is supported. Whether it respects approval workflows and roles, and whether RECEIVED via the API creates inventory, is undocumented.
claims.evidence: The PUT status enum is verified. Neither the spec nor the docs describe role checks, approval enforcement or inventory side-effects.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION (c2): Adding comments or notes to an existing request is not supported; 'notes' can be set only at creation. Only Notes are exported to Excel (article 115002467013).
claims.evidence: There is no comment endpoint, and PUT accepts only status. Article 115002467013: 'Notes will be exported to Excel, and comments will not.' The unreferenced OrderRequestEvent schema has a `comment` field, so comments may be readable (not writable) through the webhook `events` array (inference).

claims.claim: INTEGRATION (d): Creating inventory in our app when items are received. order-request.received fires; partial receipts stay in ORDERED; 'Do Not Add To Inventory' is an option; the payload has no inventory-item id.
claims.evidence: Article 115005303888: 'the Mark Received button will remain active so you can indicate when the rest of the shipment arrives', and 'Do Not Add To Inventory - The request is received and no update is made to inventory.' The received payload has no inventory id. Article 32846540627995 adds: 'Item instances will be created automatically when receiving a requested item and adding it to the Inventory.' Whether order-request.received fires on a partial receipt is undocumented.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION (e): Reading and updating Quartzy inventory quantities is partially supported: read items, write quantity only, and no create, delete, location, lot or expiration edits.
claims.evidence: The spec's only inventory writes are the two quantity PUTs. The instance guide confirms this.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION (f): Bulk historical export is supported: page through GET /order-requests, or use the UI export with 'Submitted' + 'All Time' (article 234660947).
claims.evidence: 'All requests that have ever been added to the lab will be exported to a CSV file!' and 'export from the All Labs view to export requests from all of your labs in one file.' For the API route, stopping at an empty page and the sort order are undocumented.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION: Detecting approvals, cancellations and backorders in real time is only partial: poll for order requests; Quartzy Shop items do emit backordered and cancelled events.
claims.evidence: No order-request approved, cancelled or backordered events exist; their docs URLs return 404. com.quartzy.sales-order-item.backordered and .cancelled do exist.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION: Webhooks can be registered and managed from code, but the docs disagree on lab_id vs organization_id, so test both.
claims.evidence: The capability itself is confirmed. The disagreement is not real: CreateWebhook is a oneOf of a {lab_id, url} body or an {organization_id, url} body. Limits: PUT only toggles is_enabled, there is no DELETE, and the event_types string format is undocumented.
claims.correction: Both bodies are valid by design. Use lab_id for a lab webhook or organization_id for an organization-wide one.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION: Lab members and roles cannot be listed via the API.
claims.evidence: The only person endpoint is GET /user, which returns the token owner. No member or role fields exist in any schema.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION: There are no endpoints for locations, vendors, budgets, POs, invoices or custom request fields. Budget is visible read-only as spend_tracking_code.name.
claims.evidence: Spec paths cover only healthz, inventory-items, labs, order-requests, types, user and webhooks. SpendTrackingCode is {name}. Article 4411829390875 calls Budgets '(formerly spend tracking codes)'. Inventory custom fields and the inventory Owner are not in the API either.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION: Whether OAuth2 delegated per-user authorization is supported is unknown, because the docs document no flow.
claims.evidence: The official spec declares OAuth2 (authorizationCode; https://auth0.quartzy.com/authorize and https://auth0.quartzy.com/oauth/token; scopes {}) as an alternative to AccessToken on every operation.
claims.correction: OAuth2 is declared, but how to obtain a client is undocumented, so contact Quartzy for a client_id. Until then, per-user personal access tokens are the only documented route.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION: There is no native Zapier app. Zapier to Google Sheets needs Lab Admin and a Zapier Professional, Team or Company plan. Power Automate needs Premium connectors. Teams uses a template. All are outbound only.
claims.evidence: https://zapier.com/apps/quartzy/integrations returns 404. The Zapier article requires 'Quartzy: Lab Admin role' and a 'Professional, Team, or Company' Zapier plan. Power Automate needs 'access to Premium connectors' and Lab Admin. The Teams setup (13921305119643) is a Power Automate package plus a webhook, with Lab Admin. The official PDF says 'These integrations are outbound in nature'.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION: The Slack integration is a Slack Workflow Builder template that consumes Quartzy webhooks.
claims.evidence: Help article 5356346153883 (updated 2026-10-16) now describes a native Quartzy Slack app: 'Select the Add to Slack button', then Allow, then Authorize in the Quartzy app, then 'Add Notification'. It requires Lab Admin, and alerts are turned off under Developers tab > Webhooks. Notification types: item requested, ordered and received (any vendor); shipped, delivered, backordered and canceled (Quartzy Shop only); inventory item created and updated. The older docs.quartzy.com/guides/slack still describes importing .slackworkflow files into Workflow Builder.
claims.correction: The current official route is the native Slack app. It is still outbound only and limited to the existing webhook event set.

claims.claim: INTEGRATION: Native integrations. Benchling is an add-on (syncs inventory to Benchling; creates Quartzy requests from Benchling). SciNote and Scispot are included in Professional, Enterprise and Academic plans. NetSuite and QuickBooks come with Enterprise/Academic or as an add-on.
claims.evidence: Benchling: 'available as an add-on to our subscription plans'; 'Automatically sync new inventory items from Quartzy to Benchling' (one-way). SciNote (23258636712603) and Scispot (12514492535579): 'included in Professional, Enterprise, and Academic subscription plans'. The pricing page lists 'Financial and ERP integrations (QuickBooks, NetSuite)' as an Add-on. The claim that NetSuite and QuickBooks are included in Enterprise/Academic is not verified.

claims.claim: PRICING: Academia is $50/month billed annually with 3 users; Industry is $250/month billed annually with 5 users; Enterprise is custom-priced with unlimited users, PunchOut/ERP and custom SAML/OIDC. Seats can be added, but no per-seat price is shown.
claims.evidence: The pricing page shows '$50 / month', 'Billed annually', '3 users included'; '$250 / month', '5 users included'; and 'Unlimited users' for Enterprise. Its FAQ says 'additional seats can be added at any time'.

claims.claim: PRICING: 'APIs and webhooks to build your own integration' is included (not an add-on). Low-stock alerts, mobile barcode scanning, customizable approval routing, real-time spend reporting, customizable request fields and collaboration tools are also included.
claims.evidence: 'Included with your plan unless marked as an add-on.' Each of these rows is marked Included. The same table marks 'Custom integrations', 'PO generation', 'Automated invoice reconciliation (3-way match)', 'Custom SAML or OIDC' and 'Automated SDS collection' as Add-ons.

claims.claim: PRICING: Add-ons include Benchling, PunchOuts, QuickBooks/NetSuite, SDS Automation and custom analytics.
claims.evidence: All are listed as add-ons. The page also lists 'Procure-to-Pay Automation', 'BioPASS Procurement Services' and 'Custom integrations'. No add-on prices are given ('Add-ons are priced with your plan').

claims.claim: PRICING: Subscription FAQ (article 4405994277147, updated 2026-06-05): Professional, Enterprise or Academic plans; price depends on plan and seats; 14-day trial; with no plan the account goes read-only, but open orders are fulfilled and data can be exported.
claims.evidence: updated_at 2026-06-05T21:12:05Z. Quotes: 'Professional, Enterprise, or Academic'; 'The cost will depend on the plan selected and the number of seats your organization selects.'; 'The Free Trial period is 14 days by default.' API access is not mentioned.

claims.claim: PRICING HISTORY: Quartzy was free for academia until July 1, 2023, then $99/seat/year for existing labs and $149/seat/year for labs joining later.
claims.evidence: Blog post dated Jan 11, 2023 (updated Jan 18): '$99 per user seat per year'; 'Labs that join after will pay $149 per user seat per year'; 'On July 1, 2023 we will implement a yearly subscription fee'. It was written as an upcoming change.

claims.claim: ACCESS: Only US labs can buy from the Quartzy Shop.
claims.evidence: 'items shown here are available to purchase from Quartzy (US labs only)' (233421407).

claims.claim: ACCESS: The mobile app is on iOS in the US and Canada and on Android in the US only.
claims.evidence: Official sources conflict. Articles 8326390071323 and 6180409022747 say 'Apple app store - available in the US and Canada' and that Google Play is 'available in the US only'. The Mobile App FAQs (10728331545499, updated 2025-08-06) say 'Yes! The mobile app has been released to every available country via the Apple iOS and Google Play stores.'

claims.claim: ToS §3.2(a) forbids 'the sharing of login credentials or the sharing of accounts between multiple users', so confirm with Quartzy before routing many people's requests through one token.
claims.evidence: In context, the clause bars attempts to 'circumvent or manipulate the Quartzy fee structure, billing process, or other fees owed to Quartzy' 'through the sharing of login credentials or the sharing of accounts between multiple users'. It targets seat and fee circumvention, which is exactly a one-token-for-30-people setup. §3.2(m) also bars resale and commercial exploitation without written consent.

claims.claim: EXPORT: Requests export (article 234660807) filters by Submitted, Approved, Ordered, Received or Cancelled date, over ranges, in 3 modes. Group Actions has Export CSV (115005489868). The Spend Dashboard exports CSV for Admins and Members (19552088311707). Email reports: monthly spend and weekly reconciliation (234438148).
claims.evidence: Article 234660807 is titled 'Export a spend report' (updated 2026-10-16) and lists the 5 date filters, the ranges and modes (A), (B) and (C). Spend Dashboard: 'Lab Admins and Members both have access to this dashboard', with filters Type, Lab, Month, Requester, Supplier and Budget. The reconciliation report can be Monthly or Weekly and filters by received date.

claims.claim: EXPORT: Inventory exports to Excel per lab only ('There is no option to export the Inventory when viewing All Labs'), either the whole lab or the filtered view, with weekly or monthly emailed backups (article 234448328).
claims.evidence: Quote verbatim. Inventory can be 'automatically emailed to you on a weekly or monthly basis'.

claims.claim: EXPORT: Inventory reports are a CSV Audit Report (Event Time, Event Type, Field Name, Before, After, Event Data), a Detailed Consumption Report and a Summary Consumption Report (article 38529710860571). The audit trail only exists from March 2024.
claims.evidence: Article 38529710860571 lists the Audit columns and gives the Summary columns as 'Beginning Quantity', 'Total Quantity Consumed', 'Total Quantity Restocked (Added)' and 'Ending Quantity'. Reports download as .csv.

claims.claim: IMPORT: Inventory import: Item Name required, Amount in Stock numeric, worksheets are Types with a 31-character name limit, one lab at a time. Freezer boxes: locations must exist first, A1 positions, '>' separators. Order history: Item name, Vendor, Catalog # and Quantity required; MM/DD/YYYY dates; Ordered if not received, New if both dates are blank. Bulk edit is keyed on Serial Number. Bulk delete uses 'Delete? (Y/N)'. Bulk new requests (233421187).
claims.evidence: Quotes: 'There is a 31-character limit for worksheet (Type) names.'; 'There is no option to import when viewing All Labs.'; 'You will not be able to upload your items to freezer boxes unless you create all locations and sublocations in advance.'; 'Quartzy uses the Serial Number to find existing items'. Order history rows go to the Ordered tab when Date Received is blank, and to New when both dates are blank. Bulk requests land in 'New, Ordered, or Received' depending on the date columns.

claims.claim: IMPORT: Excel import is the only bulk way to create inventory in Quartzy; the API cannot create it.
claims.evidence: The spec has no inventory create operation, and no DELETE operation at all.
claims.correction: Help article 5333106670747 says 'Using Quartzy's API, developers can create and update Quartzy requests and inventory items', which overstates what the API does. Trust the spec.

additional_facts: Use the machine-readable spec at https://docs.quartzy.com/redocusaurus/public-api.yaml (the 'Download' link on the API page) as the source of truth. It has 29 schemas and operationIds such as health, inventoryItemList, inventoryItemInstanceUpdate, labList, orderRequestCreate/Update, typeList, me and webhookCreate/Update. The API has no versioning, so generate the client from this file and diff it on a schedule to catch silent changes.

Two authentication methods are allowed on every operation: AccessToken (apiKey in the Access-Token header) or OAuth2 authorization code (https://auth0.quartzy.com/authorize and https://auth0.quartzy.com/oauth/token, scopes {}). The live OIDC discovery document at https://auth0.quartzy.com/.well-known/openid-configuration lists authorization_code, refresh_token and PKCE S256, but that is observed, not documented. Registering a client is undocumented; ask support@quartzy.com.
The API has no DELETE operations at all. PUT /webhooks/{id} accepts only is_enabled (additionalProperties: false), so changing a webhook's URL or event_types needs the UI.

Both CreateOrderRequest and UpdateOrderRequest have additionalProperties: false. Money is {amount: string with format integer, currency: string}, both required, and the unit (dollars vs cents) is undocumented, so test before sending prices. In responses quantity, unit_price and unit_size are nullable strings, while POST quantity is an integer.

Error bodies are {message: string}. No 400 or 403 is documented for the order-request POST or PUT. The 404 descriptions on /labs/{id} and /inventory-items/{id} wrongly say 'No matching Order Request'.

The spec defines an OrderRequestEvent schema that nothing references: {type (required), comment (nullable), created_at, created_by: User}. It is probably the element type of the webhook `events` array (the example shows [null]). If so, status history and comments may be readable from webhook payloads. Test this.

Labs can make Budget required ('Make field required'; 'If required, users cannot add requests without populating the budget field.', 115003242028). Organizations can make custom request fields required ('Users cannot submit a request without completing all required fields.'; formats Text, Single Select, Checkbox, Date; 4407114944155). POST /order-requests can set neither, so whether API-created requests are rejected or bypass these rules is undocumented. Test in a sandbox lab. Organizations with required custom request fields also 'do not yet have access to automatic requests' (QBot, 38547448619547).

Deleting a request is different from cancelling it. Admins can permanently delete requests ('Deleting a request will delete it for everyone in the Lab'; 'Quartzy requests can be cancelled but not deleted', 115007069047). com.quartzy.order-request.deleted covers only deletions; cancellations have no webhook. Quartzy Shop orders also have a UI status 'Pending Cancellation' that stays in the Ordered tab (360006135354) and is not in the API enum.

The UI keeps a per-request status history showing 'the date, the status change, and the name of the person who updated it' (115000746334). The API exposes only the current status and updated_at, so a poller cannot recover intermediate transitions.

Instance rollout: 'Item instances are currently being released to all users that are not using inventory integrations.' (32846540627995, updated 2026-10-08). A lab with an inventory integration may stay un-migrated, so handle uses_instances being true, false or missing. Receiving into inventory creates instances automatically and merges them when location, lot and expiration match.

Inventory items have an Owner in the UI (the permission 'Edit Item owned by them', a bulk-edit column 'Owner', and a lab setting that controls whether Members can edit others' items). The API exposes only added_by and updated_by. Inventory custom fields (234451008) are not in the API either.

There are organization-level roles too: Org Admin vs Org Member (14740305537947). Org Admins manage integrations such as QuickBooks, custom request fields and organization membership. Benchling setup needs a Lab Admin (12312389576731).

New way to create requests: the Quartzy Connect Chrome extension (55420967896475, created 2026-09-04). 'Any Quartzy user can install the extension and create requests with it' from any vendor product page. It auto-fills Item Name, Vendor, Catalog Number, Unit Size and Unit Price, plus Type, Budget and custom fields. Its article mentions no duplicate or inventory check, so the duplicate detector must catch these requests through com.quartzy.order-request.created.

Approvals support price thresholds (e.g. auto-approve under $500, then tiered approvers), Approval Teams and Budget Owners ('Budget owners can be either Admins or Members'). 'Only Lab Admins can add and manage Budgets.' Approver emails go out hourly at the top of the hour (4411829390875, 115003242028).

The Terms of Service (Last Revision March 9, 2026) have no API-specific terms. Besides §3.2(a), (f) and (i), §3.2(e) bans working 'around any technical limitations in the Services' and reverse engineering, and §3.2(m) bars resale or commercial exploitation. Get Quartzy's agreement in writing before the app replaces per-user Quartzy seats.

The official webhook PDF guide's screenshots show short event codes in the UI (sales-order.placed, sales-order-item.shipped, sales-order-item.delivered, sales-order-item.cancelled) and call integrations 'outbound in nature'. It links to an alternate docs host, public-docs.production.qtz.sh.

Help-center HTML pages return 403 to automated fetches, but the Zendesk Help Center API is publicly readable: https://support.quartzy.com/api/v2/help_center/en-us/articles/{id}.json and /api/v2/help_center/articles/search.json?query=... Both return created_at and updated_at, which is handy for tracking doc changes.
The docs offer only curl, NodeJS and Python samples, and they call only GET /user. There is no SDK, no pagination example and no webhook signature-verification example.

Mobile scanning is built around Quartzy-generated barcodes: per the Mobile App FAQs, barcodes 'can only be generated from the Quartzy web application at this time'. Inventory group actions include 'Duplicate an Inventory item' and 'Request items from the Inventory' (29209064536859). Request group actions include Edit, Generate a Requisition Form, Export, Cancel and Delete (115003241928).

research.angle: domain — what a molecular/cell-biology lab must record per material type, the surrounding bench workflows, compliance obligations, and the public databases/APIs that can auto-fill metadata
research.summary: For a 30-person wet lab, "inventory" is really 14 different data models glued to one place-and-amount question. Cell lines need provenance (ATCC/DSMZ/ECACC/JCRB catalog no. + Cellosaurus CVCL accession/RRID), passage and population-doubling history, mycoplasma/STR test dates, bank tier (token/master/working), and LN2 tank→rack→box→position; antibodies need vendor+catalog as the identity key plus RRID (AB_), clone, host, isotype, conjugate and a per-application validated dilution table, with lot as the unit that actually breaks experiments; plasmids need backbone/insert/resistance+concentration/growth strain/growth temperature/copy number plus an attached GenBank or SnapGene file and an Addgene ID; chemicals need CAS, GHS pictograms/H-statements, an SDS link, a storage-compatibility group, and date-opened timers for peroxide formers. Crucially, almost every identity field can be auto-filled from free public APIs: Cellosaurus (`api.cellosaurus.org`, CC BY 4.0, no auth) for cell lines, CLASTR (`/str-search/api/query`) for STR identity scoring, the Antibody Registry API for RRIDs, PubChem PUG-REST/PUG View (≤5 req/s, no auth) for CAS→CID→GHS/LCSS, Addgene's approved-access Developers Portal for plasmids, plus UniProt, NCBI E-utilities and hPSCreg. Quartzy's own REST API (`api.quartzy.com`, `Access-Token` header) exposes inventory items *and* order requests with a 6-value status enum — which is exactly the hook needed to show "someone already ordered this 3 days ago" at request time. The compliance layer (ICLAC misidentified-line register v14 = 608 lines, NIH NOT-OD-15-103 authentication attachment, OSHA BBP/BSL-2 for human cells + IBC registration, MTA onward-transfer limits, campus EHS/fire-code chemical inventory, DEA-registered substance logs) gives the app a second reason to exist beyond cost: it turns reminders and exports that people currently do badly by hand into a by-product of normal inventory use.

fields: source_collection + catalog_no (ATCC CCL-2 / DSMZ ACC-xxx / ECACC 90102526 / JCRB IFO50010 / KCLB / RIKEN RCB)

category (Cellosaurus 14-term enum: Cancer cell line, Conditionally immortalized, Embryonic stem cell, Factor-dependent, Finite cell line, Hybrid cell line, Hybridoma, Induced pluripotent stem cell, Somatic stem cell, Spontaneously immortalized, Stromal, Telomerase immortalized, Transformed, Undefined)
workflows: Receive/import: scan vendor catalog no. -> auto-resolve Cellosaurus accession -> pull category, species, disease, site, problematic flag; quarantine state until mycoplasma-negative
Quarantine release: require negative bacteria/fungi/mycoplasma result before the line can be booked into shared LN2
Tiered banking: token stock (3-5 ampoules) -> Master Cell Bank (10-20) -> Working Cell Bank (20-200); QC 5-10% of each bank; confirm MCB vs WCB identity by STR/DNA profiling
Thaw: creates a culture record with passage = vial passage + 1 (thaw+reseed counts as one passage); passage increments on reseeding, NOT on freezing
Subculture: log split ratio -> auto-compute population doublings (1:2 = 1 PD, 1:4 = 2 PD) and cumulative PDL; warn at per-line passage/PDL ceiling
Periodic authentication: STR profile -> POST to CLASTR -> store Tanabe score vs claimed identity; flag <80% match
Retire/discard with reason; preserve record for publication-time reporting
enrichment_sources: Cellosaurus REST: GET https://api.cellosaurus.org/cell-line/CVCL_0030?fields=ac,id,sy,ca,ox,sx,ag,di,site,str,dr,prob,hi,ch,time&format=json (no auth, CC BY 4.0)
Cellosaurus search: GET https://api.cellosaurus.org/search/cell-line?q=derived-from-site:liver ox:sapiens di:Hepatoblastoma&fields=id,ac
Cellosaurus /release-info to detect new releases and re-sync
CLASTR STR search: GET/POST https://www.cellosaurus.org/str-search/api/query (and /api/batch, POST only)
ICLAC Register of Misidentified Cell Lines v14 (15 Feb 2026, 608 lines) .xlsx import
hPSCreg GET https://hpscreg.eu/api/names and /api/names/{name} for hiPSC/hESC naming
NCBI E-utilities for taxonomy and PubMed references (3 req/s no key, 10 req/s with key)
compliance_notes: NIH NOT-OD-15-103 requires an 'Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources' PDF attachment (applications due on/after 25 Jan 2016) - the app should be able to print the lab's authentication evidence per line
ANSI/ATCC ASN-0002-2022 is the STR standard; 8 core loci + amelogenin; >=80% match = related, <50% = unrelated; Tanabe score == Sorensen-Dice coefficient

ICLAC v14: 560 of 608 lines are misidentified with no known authentic stock; HeLa is the contaminant in 145 entries, T-24 in 21, M14 in 18. Register is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 - do not modify entries, attribute to iclac.org

Human and other primate cell lines: BMBL recommends BSL-2 practices; OSHA's 1994 interpretation puts human cell lines in scope of the Bloodborne Pathogens Standard unless characterized free of HBV/HIV/EBV/HPV etc.; most IBCs require a registered protocol plus annual BBP training records
ATCC: no universal passage cap - establish a per-line window; indicative working ranges from ATCC teaching material are ~20 passages (continuous), 8-12 (primary), up to 30 (stem cells)

item_types.item_type: Primary cells, iPSC and patient-derived lines
fields: consent scope (research use, genetic analysis, redistribution allowed y/n, withdrawal recorded)
tissue of origin, procurement date, procurement site
reprogramming method + vector + integration status (for iPSC)
passage_at_receipt, current_passage, senescence/Hayflick estimate (finite lines ~50-60 PD)
workflows: Register donor + consent before any vial is bankable; block sharing outside the lab if consent or MTA forbids it
Track cumulative PDL rather than passage number for finite lines (passage number ignores seeding density; a 1:4 and a 1:10 split both give 'passage 11')

Re-karyotype / re-authenticate after a set number of passages or after any genome edit - a significant modification (reprogramming, editing, subcloning) creates a NEW line and needs a new bank and new internal ID
enrichment_sources: hPSCreg naming tool + names API; note hPSCreg says some export/API mechanisms are temporarily disabled and access is arranged via their contact form
Cellosaurus (EBiSC-sourced iPSC lines are indexed there)
BioSamples accessions accepted as query keys by hPSCreg's names API
compliance_notes: Donor identifiability and consent terms are the hard constraint - store consent scope as structured flags, not free text, so sharing can be blocked programmatically
Patient-derived material will usually carry an incoming MTA with publication/onward-transfer terms

fields: parent material (cell line / strain / sample FK)
cells_per_vial, viability_at_freeze, cryoprotectant (e.g. 10% DMSO), freezing medium
location path: facility -> tank/freezer_id -> rack -> box/cane -> position (row,col)
storage_phase (LN2 vapour vs liquid), target temperature
qc: post-thaw viability, mycoplasma, sterility, STR confirmation on this bank
withdrawal log: who, when, why, resulting culture record
workflows: Freeze event creates N vials in one transaction and writes N positions into the box map
Checkout/withdraw by scanning the vial: decrements count, creates a culture record, logs who took it (this is the audit trail that makes shared LN2 trustworthy)
Box map UI (grid view) so a person at the tank can find position 'Tank2 / Rack B / Box 4 / C7' in one glance
Low-stock trigger on a bank: 'only 2 WCB vials left -> expand a new WCB from the MCB'
Annual physical inventory reconciliation: expected vs found, with a discrepancy report
Tank LN2 level / temperature alarm log and a freezer-failure recovery checklist
enrichment_sources: None external - this is purely internal location data; derive display codes from the parent material's enriched identity
compliance_notes: ISBER's LN2 guidance: unique ID for every freezer/tank/rack, an explicit numbering convention down to box and position, each sample carrying full location data, and every move written to an audit trail; barcodes or RFID recommended
ASTM E1565 (cryogenic storage practice): unique letter-number code per freezer, per box/cane and per position within a box

Store cryovials in the vapour phase, not submerged (liquid ingress -> vial failure and cross-contamination); use cryo labels rated to -196 C (e.g. thermal-transfer cryo label stock rated -196 to +110 C) because paper labels detach

fields: vendor + catalog_number (the de facto primary key used by the Antibody Registry)
target antigen + UniProt accession + gene symbol
isotype, conjugate/label (conjugated antibodies get a separate registry record and must be a separate inventory item)
validated applications (WB, IF, IHC-P, IHC-F, FC, IP, ChIP, ELISA) with per-application dilution/concentration and diluent
lot_number (per physical tube), lot_received_date, lot_validation_status + evidence link
concentration (mg/mL), volume remaining, format (liquid/lyophilized), storage temp (4 C / -20 C / -80 C)
in-lab validation notes + IWGAV pillar used (genetic KO/KD, orthogonal, independent antibody, tagged protein, IP-MS)
owner, which project/paper used which lot
workflows: Add by typing vendor + catalog no. -> resolve RRID and name via Antibody Registry -> prefill target, clonality, host

New lot arrives -> create a child lot record, mark 'needs re-validation', and alert everyone who used the previous lot (lot-to-lot variability is the single most common silent failure, and the registry explicitly refuses to issue lot-level IDs, so the lab must)
Aliquot-on-receipt workflow: one tube -> N aliquots with a freeze/thaw counter, so the stock tube is thawed once
Per-application dilution table that anyone can read at the bench and append to ('worked at 1:1000 in 5% BSA/TBST on lysate X')
Methods-section export: name, vendor, cat#, lot, host, clonality, clone, RRID, dilution, diluent - exactly what journals and reporting checklists ask for
enrichment_sources: Antibody Registry API (third-party-documented, public, no auth): GET https://www.antibodyregistry.org/api/fts-antibodies?q=<vendor or catalog no> ; GET https://www.antibodyregistry.org/api/antibodies/{AB_2298772|numeric id} ; bare /api/antibodies returns the whole DB - avoid
Full-database CSV download (login required; identifiers are CC0, website code Apache-2.0)
SciCrunch resolver for RRID validation
UniProt REST for the target protein: GET https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/search?query=gene:TP53+AND+reviewed:true&format=json (use /uniprotkb/stream for bulk; search pages at 500)
compliance_notes: RRID issuance is CC0; the registry had ~2.5M curated records as of Sept 2022 and ~303k marked discontinued
The registry will not add lot granularity and tells researchers to report lot numbers in methods - so lot tracking is the lab app's job
NIH NOT-OD-15-103 names antibodies explicitly as a 'key biological resource' requiring an authentication plan

fields: internal plasmid ID (e.g. pLAB-0123) + common name
addgene_id (if applicable) + depositor + depositing article PMID
backbone / parent vector, vector type (bacterial expression, mammalian expression, lentiviral, AAV, retroviral, entry/Gateway, reporter)
insert / gene name + species + insert size + GenBank/RefSeq accession
tags and position (e.g. 'Flag (N terminal on backbone)', HA, His, GFP)
selection: bacterial resistance + working concentration (e.g. Ampicillin 100 ug/mL), mammalian selection marker
growth strain (e.g. Top10; ccdB-containing constructs need a ccdB-resistant strain) and growth temperature (37 C, or 30 C to repress an integrase)
cloning method + cloning sites + sequencing primers
full sequence file attachment (.gb / .dna SnapGene / .fasta) + map image + sequence verification status and date
biosafety: insert hazard class, BSL for viral vectors, IBC protocol no.
physical stock: tube(s), concentration (ng/uL), volume, location; glycerol stock of the harboring strain
workflows: Create from Addgene ID -> prefill backbone, insert, resistance, growth strain/temp, copy number, sequence
Maxi/mini prep event -> new DNA stock record (concentration, A260/280, date, person) linked to the parent plasmid
Sequence-verification gate: cannot be marked 'validated' without an attached alignment/sequencing result
Request-a-plasmid internally: find it, see who has it and where, request an aliquot instead of re-ordering or re-cloning
Outgoing-share workflow that checks the MTA/license flag before generating a shipment
enrichment_sources: Addgene Developers Portal (developers.addgene.org): read-only JSON API, Catalog endpoint currently covers plasmids and viral preps (sequences, expression, vector type, plasmid type, genes, article info); access by approved request with a data access license per scope, ~5 business day review, token valid 1 year and regenerable; bulk JSON datasets refreshed daily, versioned majorVersion.minorVersion, PI/lab-head names excluded; antibodies, pooled libraries, plasmid kits and bacterial strains announced for late 2026
NCBI E-utilities (efetch) for insert reference sequences
UniProt for the encoded protein
compliance_notes: Viral vector plasmids and anything expressing a hazardous insert usually require IBC registration and a specified BSL; keep the IBC protocol number on the record
Addgene requires accepting a data access license per API scope - log the license acceptance and token expiry in the app's admin section

item_types.item_type: Bacterial / yeast strains and glycerol stocks
fields: species + background (e.g. E. coli DH5a, BL21(DE3), S. cerevisiae BY4741)
plasmid(s) harbored (FK to plasmid records) + resistance markers carried
glycerol stock: date frozen, glycerol % final (commonly 15-25%, some SOPs 50% 1:1), number of tubes, backup tube location
growth conditions: medium, temperature, aerobic/anaerobic, selection
verification: colony PCR / sequencing / phenotype check + date
biosafety: risk group, BSL, IBC protocol
workflows: Freeze-down checklist that forces genotype + parental strain + plasmid links before a tube gets a barcode
Always create a duplicate backup tube in a second freezer and record both positions
Streak-out log so a tube's use count is visible (repeated thaw/streak of the same tube is a known failure mode); keep at -80 C, not -20 C (glycerol stocks lose viability above ~-55 C)
Lineage view: 'show everything derived from this parent strain'
Label convention baked into the printer template: strain ID on the lid, plasmid name + resistance on the side
enrichment_sources: Addgene bacterial strains (announced for the Catalog API in late 2026)
CGSC / Addgene / SGD / NBRP strain catalogs for reference genotypes
NCBI Taxonomy via E-utilities
compliance_notes: Risk-group and BSL per organism; IBC registration for recombinant work
Strains carrying regulated inserts or toxin genes must be flagged to the institutional biosafety officer rather than handled by lab policy alone

fields: sequence (5'->3') + length + modifications (5' phosphate, biotin, fluorophore, phosphorothioate)
purpose/assay (cloning, qPCR, sequencing, genotyping, sgRNA cloning)
target gene / amplicon / genome build + coordinates
Tm, GC%, MW, extinction coefficient (all on the vendor spec sheet 'Properties' section)
delivered amount: OD260 units, mass (mg), nmol (as shipped, not as ordered)
resuspension buffer (IDTE pH 7.5/8.0 or nuclease-free water - not DEPC-treated or deionized water, which tend to be acidic and risk depurination), stock concentration (uM), resuspension date
paired primer (forward/reverse pair ID), validated amplicon size, qPCR efficiency
workflows: Resuspension calculator at receipt: uL of buffer for 100 uM = nmol x 10 (e.g. 9 nmol -> 90 uL); write the computed volume and concentration into the record automatically
Primer-pair registry with in-silico and empirical validation status, so nobody re-orders a pair that already works
Search-before-order by sequence (exact and reverse-complement) and by target gene - oligos are the single most duplicated purchase in most labs
Store resuspended stocks at -20 C; prompt to make working dilutions so the 100 uM stock is not repeatedly thawed
enrichment_sources: Vendor spec sheets (IDT/Thermo) for OD260, nmol, Tm, MW, extinction coefficient
NCBI E-utilities / UCSC for target coordinates and in-silico PCR
UniProt/NCBI Gene for gene symbol normalization
compliance_notes: Mostly none, but oligo sequences are also IP/publication artifacts - keep the ELN/notebook link so a primer can be traced to the figure it produced

item_types.item_type: siRNA / shRNA / sgRNA and pooled libraries
fields: nuclease or modality (SpCas9, SaCas9, Cas12a, base editor, prime editor, siRNA, shRNA)
protospacer (20 nt for SpCas9) stored separately from PAM; PAM sequence and orientation (3' NGG for SpCas9; 5' TTTV for Cas12a)
target gene + transcript, genome build (e.g. GRCh38), chromosome, start/end, strand
on-target efficiency score + algorithm and version; off-target score + algorithm and version; number of perfect-match off-targets (Cas-OFFinder etc.)
delivery format (synthetic sgRNA, RNP, lentiviral vector, plasmid) + vector FK
for libraries: library name, pool size, barcode/oligo IDs, coverage per gene, reference screen
validation: editing efficiency (indel %), clone genotype, phenotype
physical stock: concentration, aliquots, location, freeze_thaw_count
workflows: Register a guide once with its design parameters, then link every edited clone/cell line back to it (so an edited line's record always answers 'which guide made this?')
Re-score warning when the genome build or scoring tool changes
Edited-clone lineage: parent line + guide + donor template -> new internal cell line ID with its own bank
enrichment_sources: Addgene (guide-containing plasmids and pooled libraries; libraries coming to the Catalog API late 2026)
NCBI/UCSC for coordinates and build conversion; design tools (CRISPOR, CHOPCHOP, Benchling) for scores
compliance_notes: Gene-editing work and any lentiviral/AAV delivery generally sits under an IBC-registered protocol at a stated BSL; keep the protocol number on both guide and vector records

fields: name (e.g. Q5 High-Fidelity DNA Polymerase), vendor, catalog no., lot
storage temp (-20 C / -80 C / 4 C), do-not-freeze flag
date received, date opened, expiry, stability-after-opening
aliquots + freeze_thaw_count (enzymes degrade with repeated freeze-thaw; aliquot once on receipt)
assay/kit it belongs to, compatible buffer FK
workflows: Aliquot-on-receipt prompt for anything stored at -20/-80
Freeze-thaw counter incremented by checkout scan; warn past a configured count
Consumption-based reorder suggestion using historical usage, not a guessed par level
enrichment_sources: Vendor catalog pages / Quartzy inventory import (vendor, catalog_number, lot_number, expiration_date, price, unit_size all exist as Quartzy fields)
compliance_notes: None beyond general lab records, but expiry + opened-date is where most wasted spend hides

fields: kit name, vendor, catalog no., lot, number of reactions/preps
expiry + date opened; component-level expiry where components differ
kit components with their own storage temps (room temp / 4 C / -20 C) and their own locations
protocol/manual PDF link, internal protocol deviations
workflows: Decrement reactions at use so 'in stock' does not mean 'one prep left in a 250-prep box'
Split-location handling: one kit whose components live in three different places (this is a very common source of 'we had it all along')
Component-level low-stock alert (e.g. the proteinase K ran out but the columns did not)
enrichment_sources: Vendor catalog metadata; Quartzy item import
compliance_notes: Kits containing hazardous components still need the hazard data of those components surfaced (e.g. guanidinium-containing lysis buffers must not be mixed with bleach)

fields: name/formulation + base medium + supplements with final concentrations
vendor, catalog no., lot (critical for serum), bottle/aliquot ID
for FBS: lot number, lot reservation/hold, heat-inactivated y/n, endotoxin/hemoglobin spec, which cell lines are qualified on this lot
date received, date opened, expiry, in-use expiry after opening/after supplementing
sterility check (filtered, filter size, sterility test date), prepared_by, recipe/SOP version
L-glutamine addition date (glutamine in liquid medium drops ~2-3% per month at 2-8 C; or use a stabilized dipeptide)
workflows: In-house solution recipes as versioned templates; 'prepare' creates a batch record with prepared_by, date, recipe version and an expiry computed from the recipe
Serum lot qualification workflow: reserve a lot, test it on the lab's key lines, then record which lines are approved on that lot and how much is reserved
Aliquot-then-freeze for labile supplements (thaw once, aliquot, refreeze) with aliquot tracking
Short-expiry dashboard (next 30 days) so bottles get used rather than discarded
enrichment_sources: Vendor product pages for formulation and shelf life; PubChem for individual buffer components' hazard data
compliance_notes: Serum and animal-origin components may have import/BSE documentation requirements in some institutions; store the certificate with the lot

fields: chemical name + synonyms, CAS registry number, PubChem CID
molecular formula, MW, InChIKey, canonical SMILES
container size and unit, containers on hand, amount remaining per container

location (building/room/cabinet/shelf) + storage group / compatibility class (acids, inorganic bases, flammables, oxidizers incl. peroxides, water-reactives, pyrophorics/air-reactives, highly acutely toxic / reproductive toxins)
GHS: pictograms, signal word, H-statements, P-statements, hazard classes
SDS link + SDS version date + local SOP link
peroxide_former class (A/B/C) + next_test_due + last peroxide test result
regulated flags: DEA-scheduled, EHS-reportable, institutionally restricted (with a pointer to the responsible officer rather than lab-level handling rules)
workflows: Add by CAS or name -> PubChem resolves CID -> auto-fill formula/MW/SMILES/InChIKey and GHS classification + LCSS link; store the SDS URL
Barcode every container individually (not just the chemical) so amount, open date and location are per-container

Peroxide-former timer: Class A test/discard ~3 months after opening, Class B ~6-12 months, unopened 12 months from receipt or the manufacturer expiry, whichever is first - auto-create tasks with the receipt and open dates

Storage-compatibility check on put-away: warn when a container is assigned to a location whose group conflicts (oxidizer into a flammables cabinet, acid next to base, cyanides near acids, water-reactives near a sink)
Annual EHS/fire-code inventory export: quantities per room/control area, grouped by hazard class, in the format the campus EHS system wants

Controlled-substance containers: separate perpetual usage log (receipt -> each use -> disposal), Schedule I-II records kept separate from III-V, biennial physical count, retention per institutional schedule - all generated as a signed report rather than hand-kept paper
enrichment_sources: PubChem PUG-REST (no auth): CAS -> CID via GET /rest/pug/compound/xref/RN/{CAS}/cids/JSON ; name -> CID via /rest/pug/compound/name/{name}/cids/JSON ; properties via /rest/pug/compound/cid/{cid}/property/MolecularFormula,MolecularWeight,IUPACName,CanonicalSMILES,InChIKey/JSON

PubChem PUG View for hazards: GET /rest/pug_view/data/compound/{cid}/JSON?heading=GHS+Classification (also 'Safety and Hazards' with ~11 OSHA-SDS-aligned subheadings); LCSS exists wherever a GHS classification exists, and LCSS data can be bulk-downloaded

PubChem usage policy: no more than 5 requests/second, 30 s time limit per request (secondary sources add 400 requests/min and 300 s running time per minute); violations can get an IP temporarily blocked
CAS Common Chemistry API: key by request form; non-commercial use under CC BY-NC 4.0 with a separate commercial license; search pages at 100 results
Merck/Sigma-Aldrich publish Products, Pricing-and-Availability and Safety-Data-Sheet APIs per third-party API directories - verify terms directly with Merck; do not scrape
compliance_notes: Fire-code Maximum Allowable Quantities are per control area and depend on construction, sprinklers and floor level - a quantity-by-room rollup is what makes this checkable

EPCRA/SARA Title III Tier II reporting thresholds: 10,000 lb for any SDS chemical, or 500 lb / the TPQ (whichever is lower) for an Extremely Hazardous Substance; filed annually, and states can lower thresholds. Labs often have a research exemption but adjacent stockrooms may not
Hazardous Materials Inventory Statement (HMIS) to the fire code official is a separate filing from Tier II

DEA-registered material: continuous receipt-to-disposal records, biennial inventory, Schedule I-II separated, disposal via reverse distributor; see 21 CFR 1301/1304 and the institutional controlled-substance program

CFATS (DHS chemicals of interest) statutory authority lapsed in July 2023 and remains unrestored as of early 2026, so CISA cannot currently require chemical-of-interest reporting; keep a flag field so the lab can re-report quickly if it is reauthorized
Anything in a nationally regulated biological category must be routed to the institutional biosafety officer/responsible official - the app should flag and escalate, not encode the rules

fields: sample ID (pseudonymized) + donor/subject ID + consent ID + ethics protocol
sample type (controlled vocabulary), anatomical source, collection/creation date and time
pre-analytical details modelled on ISBER SPREC (collection type, time to processing, centrifugation, fixation, storage temperature)
processing/derivation chain: parent sample -> aliquots/derivatives (DNA, RNA, FFPE block, slides, plasma)
linked events (sampling, diagnosis, treatment) per MIABIS event model
clinical annotations (minimal, pointer to the clinical DB rather than a copy)
quantity/volume remaining, QC metrics (RIN, DIN, A260/280, viability)
workflows: Accession -> process -> derive, with every derivative inheriting consent and restriction flags from the parent
Volume/aliquot depletion tracking with 'last aliquot' warnings
Request/approval workflow for using a shared specimen, with an audit record of who approved it
Export a de-identified collection summary for collaborators
