tech_components.need: 1) Application stack (one-person maintainability, CRUD/admin speed, auth, ecosystem, longevity)
tech_components.recommended: Django 6.1 now, upgrading to Django 6.2 LTS (April 2027). Server-rendered templates with htmx 2.0.x (homepage ships 2.0.11) and Alpine.js 3.17.x. Django admin as the lab-manager back office. One small ES module for camera scanning. django-ninja for the few JSON endpoints.
tech_components.rationale:
Verified:
- Django 6.0 (Dec 3 2025) added template partials ({% partialdef %}/{% partial %}, 'template#partial' in render/include). These map directly to htmx fragment responses.
- Django 6.0 also added built-in CSP (SECURE_CSP + ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware + nonce context processor) and a Tasks API.
- Django 6.1 (Aug 5 2026) added FETCH_PEERS (cuts N+1 queries to two) and DB-level on_delete.
- Support runway: 6.1 security fixes to Dec 2027; 6.2 LTS to Apr 2030. Under DEP 20, from Jan 2028 there is one release a year, each with 3 years of support.
- InvenTree runs the same backend pattern (Django API-first, Django-Q2 workers, Gunicorn behind Caddy).

Inference: admin + ModelForms gives CRUD for ~20 models in days; there is one language and one deploy artifact, and no Node runtime in production.
alternatives: Django + React SPA (InvenTree's frontend pattern): only if you need a rich offline client, and it doubles the codebase

FastAPI 0.162.0 (Oct 23 2026, still 0.x, Python >=3.10) + React: excellent typed APIs, but no admin/auth/migrations/forms built in (SQLAlchemy + Alembic + auth + admin to assemble) and a second SPA codebase

Next.js 16.4 (Oct 6 2026) / TypeScript: strong app-like UX, but not Python, and needs an ORM, auth and a hand-built admin. Patch burden is heavy: scheduled security releases Jul/Aug/Sep 2026, out-of-band critical upstream fixes on Sep 22 and Oct 14 2026, and critical RSC CVE-2025-66478 in Dec 2025
gotchas: Django 6.1 requires Python 3.12+ and PostgreSQL 15+ (PG14 dropped); 6.1 mainstream support ends Apr 2027
Django 6.1 admin has backwards-incompatible styling changes (fields below labels, 'wide' class removed), which can break admin customizations
htmx 4.0 is released but deliberately not npm 'latest'; pin 2.0.x
Admin is not a bench UI: build 5-6 dedicated mobile views (scan, use, move, receive, request, box map)
Third-party packages lag Django releases; check 6.1 support (pghistory classifiers stop at 6.0, auditlog at 5.2, guardian at 6.0)

tech_components.need: 2) Database and fuzzy product / catalog-number search
tech_components.recommended:
PostgreSQL 18 (18.6; supported until Nov 14 2030):
- pg_trgm, enabled via the TrigramExtension migration: GIN gin_trgm_ops indexes on name/synonyms, and GiST gist_trgm_ops where you need ORDER BY distance LIMIT k.
- Django full-text search: SearchVectorField as a GeneratedField + GinIndex, SearchQuery(search_type='websearch'), Lexeme to escape user input.
- B-tree unique indexes on the normalized catalog keys.
tech_components.rationale:
Verified:
- pg_trgm offers similarity, word_similarity and strict_word_similarity; operators %, <% and <<%; distance operators <->, <<-> and <<<->.
- Default thresholds: similarity 0.3, word_similarity 0.6, strict_word_similarity 0.5.
- GIN and GiST both speed up LIKE/ILIKE/regex; only GiST supports KNN distance ordering.
- Django exposes TrigramSimilarity, TrigramWordSimilarity, TrigramStrictWordSimilarity (+Distance variants) and trigram_similar / trigram_word_similar lookups.

Inference: SQLite (WAL) is fine for a prototype, but it lacks pg_trgm and has weaker write concurrency once a worker and 30 users write at once.
alternatives: SQLite + FTS5 for a throwaway prototype (Django 6.1 needs SQLite >=3.37)
Meilisearch/Typesense as a separate search service if pg_trgm proves insufficient (one more thing to run)
gotchas: Trigrams ignore non-alphanumerics, so short catalog numbers produce few trigrams; always try the exact normalized-key match first and use trigram as a fallback
Tune thresholds on labelled data: export 6-12 months of Quartzy requests and mark true duplicates
PostgreSQL 19 RC1 was announced Oct 15 2026; stay on 18.x until 19 has had a couple of point releases

tech_components.recommended: Product identity = (vendor_family, catalog_base), plus a pack-specific catalog_norm and a many-to-one GTIN table. Matching runs in order: (1) exact GTIN, (2) exact (vendor_family, catalog_norm), (3) same catalog_base with a different pack size, (4) TrigramWordSimilarity on name within the vendor family, (5) confirmed equivalence groups, (6) optional Claude re-rank of the top 20 candidates. It searches on-hand containers, open Quartzy requests and in-app requests.
tech_components.rationale:
Design (inference): normalize as NFKC -> uppercase -> strip spaces and - . / _ -> drop 'CAT#'-style prefixes. Split pack suffixes with per-vendor regex rules (e.g., NEB catalog numbers end in a size letter, as in R0650S; Sigma-style '<base>-<pack>'; legacy hyphenated Gibco numbers).

Verified inputs:
- Quartzy order requests expose vendor_name, catalog_number, item_name, quantity, unit_size, status, requested_by and requested_at.
- MilliporeSigma GS1 labels carry GTIN (01), batch (10) and expiry (17).
alternatives: Fuzzy-only matching without a canonical key (noisy, many false alarms)
LLM-only matching (non-deterministic; use only to re-rank)
gotchas: A GTIN identifies one trade item/pack, not a product family; learn GTIN -> product at first receipt
Distributors (Fisher, VWR) often use their own SKUs for other brands; store manufacturer catalog # and distributor SKU separately (inference)
Make matches warnings with 'order anyway (reason)'; hard blocks push people around the system
Spreadsheet imports mangle catalog numbers (leading zeros, auto-dates); import as text

tech_components.recommended:
- QR and Micro QR: segno 1.6.6 (pure Python, no dependencies, BSD).
- DataMatrix and GS1: zint-bindings (Apache-2.0 bindings to BSD libzint; 50+ symbologies; PNG/SVG/EPS) or treepoem 3.29.0 (BWIPP via Ghostscript, ~100 symbologies, Python 3.10-3.15).
- Code 128: python-barcode 0.16.1 (MIT; SVG with no dependencies, PNG via Pillow).
- Payload: a short internal ID or URL (https://inv.<lab>/i/7F3K9Q) plus the human-readable ID printed next to the code.
tech_components.rationale: Versions and capabilities are verified on PyPI/GitHub. Inference: Micro QR or small DataMatrix fits 1.5-2 mL cryovial labels where a full QR is too big. A URL payload lets any phone camera open the record even without the PWA.
alternatives: pylibdmtx (needs the libdmtx shared library; PyPI 0.1.10, Debian 0.1.11 Apr 2026)
ppf.datamatrix (pure Python, SVG only, no GS1/FNC1 mentioned, 1.0 'in preparation')
gotchas: treepoem needs Ghostscript; versions 9.22+ have a smearing issue only partly fixed in 9.26
segno's last release was Mar 2025 (stable but quiet)
Encode only the immutable ID, never the location or owner

tech_components.need: 3b) Scanning barcodes in a phone browser
tech_components.recommended: barcode-detector (MIT ponyfill/polyfill of the W3C BarcodeDetector API) backed by zxing-wasm (ZXing-C++ -> WASM; reader-only ~1.04 MiB). It uses the native detector where available and falls back to WASM. Self-host the .wasm (prepareZXingModule/locateFile) for CSP and offline use.
tech_components.rationale:
Verified:
- caniuse: BarcodeDetector is supported on Chrome for Android and Samsung Internet, partial on Chrome/Edge desktop, not supported on Firefox, and 'disabled by default' on Safari iOS 17.0-27.2 and macOS Safari. WebKit's flag-only implementation broke after iOS 18.
- html5-qrcode is in 'maintenance mode until further notice' and relies on zxing-js, which is also in maintenance mode ('changes are driven by contributed patches').
- quagga2 reads 1D only.
- zxing-wasm marks GS1 support for DataMatrix, QR, Code 128 and DataBar.
alternatives: USB/Bluetooth 2D imager as a keyboard wedge (see 3c)
Commercial WASM SDKs (Scanbot, Scandit, Dynamsoft) if open-source decoding is too slow on older iPhones
gotchas: getUserMedia needs HTTPS (a secure context), so you need real TLS even on the campus LAN
Keep raw decoded strings including ASCII 29 (GS) separators and hand them to biip; don't strip 'invisible' characters
Small DataMatrix codes on curved vials: use a crop box, torch/zoom constraints and a manual-entry fallback
Test on the lab's real phones in the cold room before committing (performance not verified)

tech_components.recommended: One corded 2D imager at the receiving bench, plus optional Bluetooth 2D scanners for freezer rooms. Read input with an always-focused 'scan' field ended by Enter, plus a global fast-keystroke listener on item pages.
tech_components.rationale: Verified: MilliporeSigma's FAQ says a 2D-capable scanner is needed for its GS1 DataMatrix labels. Inference: keyboard-wedge scanning needs no drivers or camera code, is fastest with gloves on, and covers desktops where BarcodeDetector is missing.
alternatives: Phone camera only (no hardware cost, slower)
gotchas: (Inference; check your scanner manual) GS1 FNC1/GS characters may be dropped in keyboard mode. Enable the AIM symbology-ID prefix (]d2 DataMatrix, ]C1 GS1-128, ]Q3 GS1 QR) and a printable GS substitute, then parse with biip
A keyboard-layout mismatch garbles characters
On iOS a paired Bluetooth HID scanner hides the on-screen keyboard

tech_components.need: 3d) Parsing GS1 and vendor packaging barcodes (AI 01 GTIN, 10 lot, 17 expiry, 21 serial)
tech_components.recommended: biip 5.2.0 (Apache-2.0, Python >=3.11, released Oct 25 2026) as the first parser. Behind it, a registry of vendor-specific parsers (e.g., NEB Code 128), then Claude vision extraction as the last fallback, with human confirmation.
tech_components.rationale:
Verified:
- biip parses GTIN-8/12/13/14, GS1 AI element strings (fixed and variable length with a configurable separator) and GS1 Digital Link URIs (canonical and non-canonical, not compressed).
- It strips symbology identifiers and uses them to pick the parser, outputs HRI, and parses dates with day 00 = end of month and a -49/+50-year window.

Vendor practice:
- MilliporeSigma Smart Label: 2D GS1 DataMatrix with item code, batch, shelf life and GTIN, using AIs 01, 17, 10, 21 and 422, also printed human-readable.
- NEB: Code 128 carrying catalog #, 8-digit lot, YYMM assay date and YYMM expiry (not GS1).
- Not verified (searches found nothing vendor-specific): Thermo Fisher/Invitrogen/Gibco, Bio-Rad, Corning, QIAGEN.
alternatives: Hand-written AI parser (error-prone for variable-length AIs)
Merck Scan Now app/web tool (manual lookup only)
gotchas: MilliporeSigma's rollout timeline dates from 2018 and excluded small labels, so expect partial coverage
Expiry formats vary: YYMMDD with DD=00 (GS1) vs YYMM (NEB)
Run a 'barcode census' of the top ~50 purchased items before designing the receiving screen

tech_components.need: 4) Label printing for tubes, cryovials, boxes and shelves
tech_components.recommended:
Two printers:
- Brother QL-820NWB or QL-1110NWB (direct thermal, Ethernet/Wi-Fi) driven by brother_ql_next 0.12.0 from the worker, for boxes, bottles, racks, shelves and location QR codes.
- A Zebra thermal-transfer desktop printer with 8000T CryoCool labels (-196 °C, Zebra 5095 resin ribbon) for cryovials. Send ZPL over raw TCP 9100 with a fresh socket per job.

No-hardware fallback: PDF sheets for laser cryo labels (LabTAG Cryo-LazrTAG) printed from the browser at 'actual size'. Brady BMP41/M511 with FreezerBondz B-490 / B-461 (-196 °C) if the lab already owns Brady handhelds.
tech_components.rationale:
Verified:
- brother_ql_next supports QL-800/810W/820NWB/1100 (1110NWB claimed), with network, pyusb and linux_kernel backends and black/red on DK-22251.
- Upstream brother_ql is unmaintained (last release 2019).
- CryoCool adhesive is rated to -196 °C. Brady B-490/B-461 are rated for liquid nitrogen. Brother TZe laminated tape claims -80 to 150 °C, which is not LN2.
- LabTAG laser cryo labels are LN2-resistant.
- DYMO 550/5XL accept only RFID-authenticated DYMO rolls.
alternatives: Brother P-touch TZe laminated tape (freezer to -80 °C claim; not LN2)
Vendor browser SDKs or local agents (Zebra Browser Print, DYMO Connect; not verified here)
Labelary API or self-hosted 'labelize' to preview ZPL
gotchas: brother_ql's network backend cannot read printer status (no end-of-roll detection)
brother_ql_next installs as module 'brother_ql' and conflicts with the original; it is GPL-3.0 (fine for internal use)
Direct-thermal paper labels are not for LN2 or solvent exposure; apply labels at room temperature before freezing and test adhesion on your vial brand
Server-side printing needs a network path to the printer. A university VM on the campus LAN can print directly; a cloud host needs a small local print agent (e.g., a Raspberry Pi polling for jobs)
Labelary free tier has unpublished usage limits and PNG size limits

tech_components.recommended:
django-allauth 65.21.0 (Oct 26 2026):
- SAML 2.0 via django-allauth[saml] for the university IdP, configured per IdP with entity_id, metadata_url and attribute_mapping.
- OIDC for Microsoft Entra / Google.
- ACCOUNT_LOGIN_BY_CODE_ENABLED: emailed code, 180 s timeout, 3 attempts.
- Passkeys: MFA_SUPPORTED_TYPES += ['webauthn'], MFA_PASSKEY_LOGIN_ENABLED=True.

Roles: Django Groups (Member, Lab manager, PI, Admin) plus rules 3.5 predicates for object-level checks (owner, manager, restricted item).
tech_components.rationale: Verified: allauth lists SAML 2.0, OIDC, MFA and rate limiting, and supports Django 4.2-6.1 on Python >=3.11. Login-by-code and passkey settings are documented. SAML setup covers ACS, SLS and metadata endpoints, and IdP-initiated SSO is rejected by default. rules keeps permissions in code with no DB tables. django-guardian 3.5.2 (Oct 20 2026) is the alternative when you need per-object grants stored in the DB.
alternatives: django-guardian 3.5.2 for explicit per-item sharing grants
A Shibboleth SP on the reverse proxy plus Django RemoteUserMiddleware
Network-level gate (campus VPN, or a zero-trust proxy; not verified here)
gotchas: allauth 65.14.2+ no longer trusts X-Forwarded-For by default; behind Caddy set ALLAUTH_TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT (or the trusted header)
SAML needs HTTPS and xmlsec system packages, and university IT must register your SP metadata (expect lead time)
rules 3.5's last release was Sep 2024, with classifiers only up to Python 3.12 (small and stable; test on 3.12-3.14)
Passkey signup requires mandatory email verification by code

tech_components.recommended:
- Slack: an internal app with a bot token, posting with chat.postMessage and Block Kit buttons, handled by Bolt for Python in Socket Mode (no public Request URL needed).
- Teams: a Workflows (Power Automate) 'post to channel when a webhook request is received' flow, posting Adaptive Cards.
- Email: django-anymail + Amazon SES ($0.10 per 1,000 emails) or the university SMTP relay, for per-user daily/weekly digests.
tech_components.rationale:
Verified:
- Slack incoming webhooks are bound to one channel, can't delete messages, can't override channel/name/icon, return no message ts, and allow 1 msg/s with short bursts.
- chat.postMessage allows about 1 msg/s per channel plus a workspace limit.
- Socket Mode supports buttons, modals and slash commands with up to 10 WebSocket connections. It suits apps behind firewalls and is not allowed in the public Marketplace (irrelevant for internal use).
- Teams: Office 365 connectors were finally retired with a rollout on May 18-22 2026. Workflows webhooks accept MessageCard since Feb 2026 but without HttpPost buttons, and posts show as the Workflows bot; use Adaptive Cards for interactive elements.
alternatives: Slack incoming webhook for one-way alerts only
A Teams bot (Azure Bot / Graph) for interactive Teams buttons (heavier)
gotchas: Old webhook.office.com / outlook.office.com connector URLs no longer work
Respect 1 msg/s; batch alerts into digests
Socket Mode connections refresh; Bolt reconnects, but run it in the always-on worker container
Don't send SDS or regulated-item details to channels that guests can see (inference)

tech_components.need: 7) Background jobs and scheduling (simplest that works)
tech_components.recommended: Django-Q2 1.11.1 (Aug 26 2026; tested on Django 5.2/6.0/6.1) with the ORM broker, so no Redis. Run 'manage.py qcluster' as one worker container. Define schedules (Quartzy sync every 10 min, nightly expiry/low-stock scan, weekly digests, result pruning) as cron Schedule rows visible in admin.
tech_components.rationale:
Verified:
- Django's built-in Tasks framework (6.0+) ships only ImmediateBackend and DummyBackend ('for development and testing only'), no worker and no scheduling API.
- django-tasks-db 0.13.0 adds a DatabaseBackend + db_worker but is marked Beta, has no scheduling, and its classifiers list Django 5.2/6.0.
- Django-Q2's ORM broker gives guaranteed delivery and an admin-editable queue, and the docs call it 'the most convenient' for medium rates and scheduled tasks.
- InvenTree uses Q2 workers with a DB-stored queue.
- Celery 5.6.3 needs a broker plus beat, which is overkill here. Huey 3.5.3 (Oct 24 2026) needs Redis or SQLite storage. Procrastinate 3.10.0 is Postgres-native and Production/Stable, with periodic tasks.
alternatives: Django Tasks API (@task/.enqueue) + django-tasks-db db_worker + cron/systemd timers running management commands (most future-proof; Beta backend)
Celery 5.6.3 + Redis + beat (only if you outgrow the rest)
gotchas: The ORM broker polls the database; fine for 30 users, not for high volume
Make jobs idempotent (Quartzy sync keyed on order-request id + updated_at)
Put long Claude calls and label printing in jobs, never in the request cycle
Monitor the worker with heartbeats; a dead worker silently stops all alerts

tech_components.recommended: Make stock movements a first-class append-only StockTransaction ledger in the domain model. Add django-simple-history 3.13.0 (Jul 22 2026) for who-changed-what on reference records, with admin history/revert. Use django-pghistory 3.9.2 (Postgres triggers) if you need capture that also covers bulk/queryset writes.
tech_components.rationale:
Verified:
- simple-history added Django 6.0 support in 3.11.0 and 6.1 in 3.12.0; 3.13.0 dropped Django 4.2/5.0/5.1. It stores full snapshots and supports time travel and admin revert.
- pghistory tracks changes with database triggers; its maintainers say this catches writes that skip Django signals. PyPI classifiers list Django 4.2-6.0 as of 3.9.2.
- django-auditlog 3.4.1 (Dec 2025) stores diffs; classifiers only up to Django 5.2.
gotchas: Don't derive quantities from audit tables; the ledger is the source of truth (inference)
Signal-based history misses QuerySet.update/bulk operations (per pghistory's comparison); funnel stock changes through one service function
Check Django 6.1 support before adopting pghistory or auditlog

tech_components.recommended: django-import-export 4.4.1 (May 5 2026) for admin imports with dry-run preview (personal spreadsheets, Quartzy inventory exports) and CSV/XLSX exports. openpyxl/pandas for one-off cleanup scripts.
tech_components.rationale: Verified: 4.4.1 is the latest 4.x; 5.0.0 is listed as unreleased in the changelog.
alternatives: Custom pandas importer run as a management command
gotchas: Pin 4.4.x until 5.0 ships (expect breaking changes)
Read catalog # and CAS columns as text
Run every imported row through the duplicate matcher and show proposed merges before commit

tech_components.recommended: django-ninja 1.7.1 (Sep 19 2026; Django 6.0/6.1 supported): Pydantic schemas and automatic OpenAPI, for scanner, print-agent, Quartzy-webhook and AI endpoints. Most pages stay server-rendered with htmx.
tech_components.rationale: Verified: DRF 3.18.3 (Oct 6 2026; Django 5.2/6.0/6.1; Python >=3.10) is maintained and describes itself as 'feature-complete'. Ninja is lighter and typed. Either works.
alternatives: Django REST framework 3.18.3 (browsable API, larger ecosystem)
gotchas: Use token auth for the print agent and scripts (scoped, revocable); session auth for the browser
Validate Quartzy webhook origin/secret (mechanism not documented on the API page)

tech_components.need: 8d) File storage for SDS PDFs, plasmid maps, CoAs and photos
tech_components.recommended: Django FileField on a local Docker volume (FileSystemStorage), served through permission-checked Django views, with a SHA-256 per file for dedupe and backup via restic. Switch to django-storages + a hosted S3-compatible bucket only if the app runs in the cloud.
tech_components.rationale: Verified: MinIO Community Edition removed its admin console (2025), went source-only with no binaries, stopped Docker images (Oct 2025), entered maintenance mode (Dec 3 2025) and was archived (Feb 2026). Inference: at a 30-person scale (thousands of small PDFs and GenBank files) local disk is simplest and fastest.
alternatives: django-storages + AWS S3 / Backblaze B2 / Cloudflare R2 (not priced here)
Garage or SeaweedFS for self-hosted S3 (not evaluated)
gotchas: Don't build on MinIO CE
Keep original .dna/.gb files; parse metadata server-side (Biopython; inference)
Don't serve media as public static files; check permissions in the view

tech_components.recommended:
An installable PWA:
- Web app manifest plus a small hand-written service worker that caches the app shell, static assets and the scanner WASM; HTML is network-first.
- Camera via getUserMedia over HTTPS.
- An offline 'scan queue' in IndexedDB (client UUIDs), flushed when the app opens or the 'online' event fires.
- Request navigator.storage.persist().
tech_components.rationale:
Verified:
- Background Sync is supported in Chrome/Edge/Samsung Internet but not in Firefox or Safari (macOS/iOS), so do the sync manually.
- WebKit (Safari 17+): per-origin quota up to 60% of disk for browsers (15% for other apps). Default storage is best-effort and can be evicted LRU. persist() is granted heuristically, and home-screen web apps get the same quotas.
alternatives: A native wrapper (Capacitor) later, only if web camera or offline limits bite (not evaluated)
gotchas: Offline writes must be idempotent ledger events, not 'set quantity = X', to avoid lost updates
Do a Wi-Fi survey of freezer rooms first; cache box maps for offline placement
Camera permission behaviour in iOS standalone mode was not verified; test on lab iPhones
Gloves: big tap targets, scan-first flows, no free-text fields in the main loops

tech_components.need: 10) Deployment, ops, backups, monitoring, hosting cost, security basics
tech_components.recommended:
Docker Compose on one VM (2 vCPU / 4 GB):
- Services: caddy (v2.11.7, automatic HTTPS), web (Gunicorn + Django), worker (qcluster + Slack Socket Mode), postgres:18.
- Backups: nightly pg_dump -Fc plus media, then 'restic backup' (0.19.1; zstd compression) to off-site storage with forget --keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 4 --keep-monthly 12, and a monthly scripted restore test.
- Monitoring: heartbeat checks on backup and sync jobs; error tracking with Sentry or GlitchTip.
- Security: unattended OS updates and Renovate/Dependabot for dependencies.
tech_components.rationale:
Hosting options (verified, list prices):
- University VM: usually free; on the same LAN as label printers and the SSO IdP.
- Hetzner Cloud: shared vCPU from €5.99/mo (cost-optimized, currently unavailable) or €6.49/mo (regular), plus €0.50/mo IPv4; US sites in Ashburn and Hillsboro.
- AWS Lightsail: $12/mo (2 GB, 2 vCPU, 60 GB) or $24/mo (4 GB, 80 GB); managed DB from $15/mo; snapshots $0.05/GB-mo.
- Fly.io: shared-cpu-1x 1 GB $6.70/mo, volumes $0.15/GB-mo, Managed Postgres from $38/mo, dedicated IPv4 $2/mo.
- Railway: Hobby $5/mo incl. $5 usage (about $20/vCPU-mo, $10/GB-RAM-mo, $0.15/GB volume, $0.05/GB egress).
- Render: pricing page didn't render; not verified.

Practical totals: $0 (university VM), about €7-15 (Hetzner incl. backup storage), about $24-40 (Lightsail with or without managed DB).
alternatives: Traefik v3 instead of Caddy (more config)
Managed Postgres (Lightsail $15+, Fly $38+) instead of a Postgres container
gotchas: University VMs often have no inbound internet, so Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 fails; use DNS-01 (Caddy DNS plugin) or university-issued certs. Avoid a private CA, since every phone would have to trust it
Phones off campus may need VPN if the VM isn't public
Run 'manage.py check --deploy', set SECURE_CSP, HSTS and secure cookies, require MFA for admins, and keep the Quartzy/Anthropic tokens in env vars
Write a one-page runbook (restore, upgrade, rotate tokens) for a successor; bus factor is 1

tech_components.recommended: A service user's Access-Token in env. A Django-Q2 schedule every 10 min pages through GET /order-requests?lab_id=..&page=.. and upserts by id (watching updated_at/status). Optionally register POST /webhooks later. Write path: POST /order-requests from the app's request form after the duplicate check, and PUT /order-requests/{id} for status. Inventory read via GET /inventory-items for the initial import.
tech_components.rationale: Verified: the endpoints, the required create fields (lab_id, type_id, name, vendor_name, catalog_number, price, quantity) and the status enum come from docs.quartzy.com/api.
alternatives: Manual CSV export/import from Quartzy (no live duplicate check)
gotchas: Webhook event types, rate limits and page size are not documented; poll politely and back off
PUT /inventory-items/{id} is deprecated; use instance-level updates if you push quantities back
Decide who owns the API token (a person leaving would break the sync)

tech_components.need: 11) Optional AI features via the Claude API
tech_components.recommended: Anthropic Python SDK (anthropic 2.3.0). Default model claude-opus-5-5 ($4/$20 per MTok; cache hits $0.20). claude-sonnet-5-5 ($2/$10) and claude-haiku-5-5 ($0.10/$0.50 for prompts up to 100K tokens) are cheaper options to compare on a 50-sample eval; which to use is the lab's call. Use structured outputs (output_config.format / messages.parse) for JSON extraction, the Batch API (-50%) for overnight SDS backlogs, prompt caching for static system prompts and tool definitions, and the Files API for SDS PDFs. Every extraction lands in a review form, never directly in inventory.
tech_components.rationale:
Verified token math:
- Images cost ceil(w/28) x ceil(h/28) tokens. On Claude 4.7+ the high-res tier caps at a 2,576 px long edge and 4,784 tokens (1000x1000 = 1,296 tokens).
- PDFs cost about 1,500-3,000 text tokens per page plus the page-image tokens; max 600 pages and 32 MB per request.
- Batch pricing: Opus 5.5 $2/$10, Sonnet 5.5 $1/$5, Haiku 5.5 $0.05/$0.25.

Per-call estimates (inference from those prices):
- (a) Label/packing-slip photo resized to 1568x1176 (2,352 image tokens + ~700 prompt tokens, ~200-1,000 output tokens incl. thinking): Opus 5.5 about $0.016-0.032, Sonnet 5.5 about $0.008-0.015, Haiku 5.5 about $0.0004-0.001.
- (b) Duplicate/equivalent re-rank of 20 candidates (~2.5K in / 150-500 out): Opus about $0.01-0.02, Sonnet about $0.005-0.008, Haiku about $0.0003.
- (c) NL inventory question with tool use (2-3 turns, ~15K in mostly cached, ~1K out): Opus about $0.04-0.08, Sonnet about $0.02-0.04, Haiku about $0.002.
- (d) 12-page SDS as a PDF (~36-60K in, ~1.5K out): Opus about $0.22-0.25, Sonnet about $0.11, Haiku about $0.006; Batch halves these. A text-only pypdf extract (~15K tokens) costs Opus about $0.09, Sonnet about $0.045, Haiku about $0.002.

Illustrative year (2,000 photos, 300 SDS, 1,500 questions, 5,000 match checks): roughly $250 on Opus 5.5, $110 on Sonnet 5.5, under $15 on Haiku 5.5.
alternatives: Local OCR (Tesseract) + regex for labels (cheaper, much less robust)
Rule-based SDS section parsing with pdfplumber (fragile across vendor layouts)
gotchas: Thinking can't be disabled on Opus 5.5; effort is the only control (default 'medium'), so set effort low for extraction. Thinking tokens bill as output. On Sonnet 5.5 use thinking {type:'between_tools'} to turn it off; Haiku 5.5 allows disabled at effort high or below
Opus 5.5 safety classifiers include 'bio', so questions about pathogens or toxins in inventory may hit stop_reason 'refusal'. Check stop_reason and enable server-side fallbacks
Crop to the label before sending; low-quality, rotated or <200 px images raise hallucination risk (per Anthropic's vision docs)
Citations can't be combined with output_config.format; use one or the other per feature
Never give the model raw SQL; expose read-only, permission-scoped tool functions
Vision docs state uploaded images are not used for training; confirm institutional policy before sending anything sensitive

key_insights: Stopping duplicates is mostly data plumbing. It needs (a) one identity per product (vendor family + normalized catalog # + GTIN) and (b) a live copy of Quartzy order requests. Quartzy's API exposes exactly the fields needed (vendor_name, catalog_number, status incl. APPROVED/ORDERED/BACKORDERED, requested_by, requested_at), so a 10-minute sync job is enough to warn 'Ana already ordered this 2 days ago'.

iOS Safari still ships BarcodeDetector disabled by default (iOS 17.0-27.2). The two most popular JS scanner libraries (html5-qrcode, zxing-js) are in maintenance mode, and quagga2 reads 1D only. A ZXing-C++ WASM polyfill (barcode-detector/zxing-wasm) is the practical cross-platform choice.

Vendor barcodes are inconsistent. MilliporeSigma prints GS1 DataMatrix (AI 01/10/17/21/422). NEB prints a custom Code 128 (catalog #, lot, YYMM assay date, YYMM expiry). Other vendors are unverified. Plan a parser chain (biip -> vendor-specific -> AI photo fallback) and measure real coverage with a barcode census before building the receiving screen.
A GTIN is not a catalog number: it identifies one trade item/pack. Learn GTIN -> product mappings at first receipt and keep distributor SKUs separate from manufacturer catalog numbers.

Django 6.x has absorbed several dependencies (template partials for htmx, CSP, a Tasks API), but still ships no worker or scheduler. Django-Q2 with the ORM broker fills that gap without Redis, which is the same choice InvenTree made.

Cryo labeling needs rated media, not just a printer. Brother QL direct thermal is fine for boxes and racks. Zebra 8000T CryoCool (thermal transfer, resin ribbon) and Brady B-490/B-461 are rated to -196 °C. Brother TZe claims only -80 °C. DYMO 550/5XL lock you to RFID-chipped DYMO rolls.

Hosting is trivially cheap ($0 on a university VM, about €7-40/month elsewhere) compared with one duplicated order. The real cost is maintainer time, so pick long-support components: Django 6.2 LTS to Apr 2030, PostgreSQL 18 to Nov 2030.

Network placement drives architecture. A campus VM can print straight to network label printers and can use Slack Socket Mode with no inbound access. A cloud VPS needs a local print agent and real DNS-01 certificates.

Microsoft Teams Office 365 connectors are gone (final retirement rollout May 18-22, 2026); only Workflows webhooks (with Adaptive Cards) or a full bot remain. Slack's incoming webhooks can't receive button clicks, so interactive 'cancel my duplicate request' nudges need a Slack app.

Next.js published security releases in each of Jul, Aug, Sep and Oct 2026 (two out-of-band critical fixes in Sep/Oct) after a critical RSC CVE in Dec 2025. That patch cadence is a real burden for a single non-JS maintainer.

Claude API per-call costs run from fractions of a cent (Haiku 5.5 label photo about $0.0004) to about $0.25 (Opus 5.5 on a 12-page SDS). Accuracy and human confirmation, not cost, are what limit AI features.
Inventory quantities belong in an append-only ledger, not in audit-history tables. Signal-based history libraries miss bulk updates, and offline replays need idempotent events.
MinIO Community Edition was archived in Feb 2026, and the old Teams/DYMO/HTML5-QR defaults are dead or degraded. A lot of 2023-era 'self-host stack' advice is now stale.
recommendations: Adopt Django 6.1 + PostgreSQL 18 + htmx 2.0.x + Alpine.js, deployed with Docker Compose (Caddy, web, worker, postgres). Upgrade to Django 6.2 LTS in Apr 2027.

Ask university IT for a VM on the campus network (direct printer access, SSO, free hosting). If that's slow, start on Hetzner (€6.49/mo, US-East) or Lightsail ($24/mo) with a Raspberry Pi print agent, and migrate later.

Spend week 1 on spikes: (a) scan the 50 most-ordered items with barcode-detector + biip to measure GS1/vendor-barcode coverage; (b) test camera scanning on the lab's actual iPhones/Androids in the cold room; (c) pull 6-12 months of Quartzy order requests through the API and count past duplicates to set a baseline and tune thresholds.
Build product identity first: a vendor-family alias table, catalog_norm/catalog_base columns with unique indexes, a GTIN map and equivalence groups. Every other feature depends on it.

Ship the MVP in this order: bulk import of personal spreadsheets (with dedupe preview), global search, Quartzy sync, the 'Already have it?' check on request, receive-by-scan with label printing, and the scan-first mobile item page. Defer AI and offline mode to phase 2.

Buy one Brother QL-820NWB (general labels, network) and pilot cryo labels. Use LabTAG laser cryo sheets immediately, and a thermal-transfer Zebra with 8000T CryoCool + 5095 resin ribbon if volume justifies it. Test adhesion at -80 °C and in LN2 on your vial brand. Don't buy DYMO 550/5XL.

Use django-allauth with university SAML/OIDC if IT will register the SP. Otherwise use Google/Microsoft OIDC plus login-by-code and passkeys. Set ALLAUTH_TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT behind Caddy and require MFA for admins.

Use Django-Q2 (ORM broker) for jobs and schedules, an append-only StockTransaction ledger plus django-simple-history for audit, django-ninja for the JSON endpoints, and local-volume file storage backed up with restic.

For notifications, build a Slack app with Bolt Socket Mode (or a Teams Workflows webhook with Adaptive Cards) for duplicate and low-stock nudges, plus a weekly email digest via SES or the university SMTP relay.

Ops from day 1: nightly pg_dump + restic off-site, a monthly restore drill, heartbeat monitoring of backup and sync jobs, error tracking, 'check --deploy', CSP, Renovate/Dependabot, and a one-page runbook for a successor.

For AI (phase 2): start with photo intake and SDS extraction using structured outputs. Default model is claude-opus-5-5 at low effort; compare Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 on a 50-sample eval and let the lab choose on accuracy vs cost. Use the Batch API for SDS backlogs, always require human confirmation, handle 'refusal' stop reasons, and log token usage per feature.
Make duplicate detection a soft gate (warning + reason to proceed) and track '$ avoided' from cancelled requests. That dashboard is what keeps the PI backing the tool.
pitfalls: Relying on the native BarcodeDetector API: it is disabled by default on all iPhones/iPads, so half the lab would be unable to scan.
Building on html5-qrcode or zxing-js (maintenance mode) or quagga2 (1D only, no DataMatrix).
Treating the GTIN as the catalog number, or one vendor spelling as canonical; use vendor families and normalized keys.
Hard-blocking 'duplicate' orders: false positives will push people back to ordering outside the app. Use warnings with reasons.
Data entry that needs typing at the bench; with gloves on, any field beyond scan + tap gets skipped and the data rots.
Direct-thermal paper labels in freezers or LN2, or labels applied to already-frozen vials; use rated media (CryoCool, B-490/B-461, laser cryo sheets) applied at room temperature.
Buying DYMO 550/5XL printers (RFID-locked rolls).
Assuming the server can reach label printers: a cloud host can't open TCP 9100 to a printer on the campus LAN without a local agent.
Posting to Teams with legacy Office 365 connector URLs (retired May 2026) or expecting incoming webhooks to handle button clicks.
Using Django's built-in Tasks framework alone: the bundled backends are development-only, with no worker and no scheduler.
Building file storage on MinIO Community Edition (archived Feb 2026).
Storing quantities as mutable 'current amount' fields edited from several devices: offline replays and concurrent edits cause lost updates. Use ledger events with client UUIDs.
Upgrading allauth behind a proxy without setting ALLAUTH_TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT (X-Forwarded-For is no longer trusted by default), which breaks rate limiting and IP logging.
Letting AI extraction write lot/expiry/hazard data without a human check, or giving an LLM raw SQL access.
Skipping restore tests; an untested backup won't help when the one maintainer is away.
Choosing a stack with a heavy patch cadence (e.g., Next.js security releases monthly plus out-of-band) for a part-time solo maintainer.
Importing spreadsheets without forcing catalog # and CAS columns to text (leading zeros and auto-dates get mangled).
open_questions: Will university IT provide a VM on the same network as the lab's label printers? Which SSO protocol do they support (SAML via InCommon/Shibboleth, or Microsoft Entra OIDC), and how long does SP registration take? Is there inbound access from off campus, or will phones need VPN?
Does the lab use Slack or Microsoft Teams (or only email)?
Which Quartzy plan does the lab have? Does it include API access tokens, who should own the token, and what webhook event types and rate limits apply (neither is documented on the API page)?

Which vendors account for most spend? GS1 barcode practice at Thermo Fisher/Invitrogen/Gibco, Bio-Rad, Corning and QIAGEN couldn't be verified because the shared web-search budget ran out; a barcode census on real packages would settle it.
What label printers and scanners does the lab already own (Brady handhelds, Brother P-touch, Zebra)? Which cryovial brands and storage phases (LN2 liquid vs vapor) need labels?
Is Wi-Fi coverage poor enough in cold rooms or freezer corridors to justify building the offline queue in phase 1?

Are there regulated materials (DEA-controlled substances, select agents/toxins, human-derived cell lines with consent/MTA limits) that need restricted visibility, stricter audit, or exclusion from AI processing?
Is the PI willing to make 'declare personal stock' and 'check before ordering' lab policy? Technology alone won't surface hidden inventories.
Is sending label photos and SDS PDFs to the Anthropic API acceptable under institutional data policy, and who pays for API usage?

Not verified in this session (search budget exhausted): Render pricing, camera-permission persistence in iOS home-screen PWAs, keyboard-wedge GS1/FNC1 behaviour on specific scanner models, Brady SDK support for server-driven printing, and enrichment APIs (Cellosaurus, Antibody Registry, Addgene, PubChem).
